Fields with defaults (`bf`, `temperature`, `k`, `coil_resistance`, `position`, `v_pos`, `v_neg`, `parasitic_caps`) can be omitted from JSON and will take their defaults.

#### JSON Schema

The `schemars` feature (on by default) derives `schemars::JsonSchema` on every type that has serde, so an app that describes its tools to others (an MCP server, a form, an API) can publish the exact shape of a netlist, bench, circuit, config or result instead of writing it by hand. Complex numbers are `[re, im]` pairs, as serde writes them.

```rust,ignore
let schema = schemars::schema_for!(sindr::import::Netlist);
println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&schema)?);
```


# Crate `sindr-devices` README (sindr-devices/README.md)

## sindr-devices

Pure electronics device physics companion models for MNA circuit simulation.

`sindr-devices` is a standalone workspace crate that implements the nonlinear device models used by the `sindr` solver. It has no dependency on the solver — pure physics math, independently testable.

### Devices

| Module | Device | Model |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `battery` | Battery | Open-circuit voltage by state of charge, series resistance, optional RC pair; Li-ion and CR2032 presets |
| `diode` | Silicon diode | Shockley companion with series resistance, temperature IS scaling, SPICE `BV`/`IBV` breakdown and junction charge (`CJO`, `VJ`, `M`, `FC`, `TT`) |
| `bjt` | BJT (NPN/PNP) | Ebers-Moll companion with Early voltage |
| `mosfet` | MOSFET (NMOS/PMOS) | Level-1 companion; body effect when called with a `vbs` (in a sindr circuit the body is tied to the source) |
| `jfet` | JFET (N/P-channel) | Shichman-Hodges |
| `igbt` | IGBT | MOSFET square-law collector current, blocks reverse V_CE |
| `led` | LED | Diode with colour-dependent forward voltage |
| `zener` | Zener diode | Shockley plus reverse-breakdown branch |
| `schottky` | Schottky diode | Shockley with Schottky IS/N (~0.3 V forward) |
| `varactor` | Varactor diode | Voltage-dependent junction capacitance C_j(V) |
| `inductor` | Saturating inductor core | `λ(i) = L_sat·i + (L₀ − L_sat)·I_sat·tanh(i/I_sat)` |
| `thermistor` | NTC thermistor | Beta model R(T) = R₀·exp(β·(1/T − 1/T₀)) |
| `regulator` | Linear voltage regulator | Piecewise linear: dropout, quiescent current, current limit, line and load regulation; LM7805 and AMS1117 presets |
| `photodiode` | Photodiode | Diode + photocurrent offset |
| `photoresistor` | Photoresistor (LDR) | Light-level-dependent resistance |

### Usage

Add to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
sindr-devices = "0.3"
```

Two-terminal companions return `(g_eq, i_eq)`: the linearised conductance (S)
and the Norton current source (A) at the operating point. Multi-terminal
devices return a companion struct.

#### Diode

```rust
use sindr_devices::diode::{diode_companion, temperature_scale_is, DiodeParams};

let params = DiodeParams::silicon(); // IS=1e-14, N=1.0, rs=0.0, 300.15 K
let (g_eq, i_eq) = diode_companion(0.65, &params);
assert!(g_eq > 0.0);

// Temperature-scaled IS (SPICE formula): IS, T, Tnom, Eg, XTI, N
let is_at_125c = temperature_scale_is(1e-14, 398.15, 300.15, 1.11, 3.0, 1.0);
assert!(is_at_125c > 1e-14);
```

`DiodeParams` fields: `is` (A), `n` (ideality), `rs` (series resistance, Ω),
`temperature` (K).

#### BJT

```rust
use sindr_devices::bjt::{bjt_companion, BjtParams};

let params = BjtParams::new(100.0); // BF=100, IS=1e-14, no Early effect
let c = bjt_companion(0.65, -5.0, &params); // Vbe, Vbc
// c.g_be, c.g_bc, c.g_ce (Early output conductance, 0 when vaf = 0), c.ic, c.ib
assert!(c.ic > 0.0);
```

`BjtParams` fields: `is`, `bf`, `nf`, `br`, `nr`, `vaf` / `var` (Early
voltages, V; 0.0 = infinite), `temperature` (K).

#### MOSFET

```rust
use sindr_devices::mosfet::{mosfet_companion, MosfetParams};

let params = MosfetParams::default_nmos(); // or default_pmos()
let c = mosfet_companion(2.0, 3.0, 0.0, &params); // Vgs, Vds, Vbs
// c.id, c.gm, c.gds, c.gmb (body effect), c.vth, c.region
assert!(c.id > 0.0);
```

#### JFET

```rust
use sindr_devices::jfet::{jfet_companion, JfetKind};

let c = jfet_companion(-0.5, 5.0, JfetKind::NChannel, 10e-3, -2.0); // Vgs, Vds, kind, IDSS, Vp
// c.gm, c.gds, c.i_eq
assert!(c.gm > 0.0);
```

#### IGBT

```rust
use sindr_devices::igbt::{igbt_companion, IgbtParams};

let params = IgbtParams::default(); // vth=5.0, k=5.0
let c = igbt_companion(10.0, 5.0, &params); // Vge, Vce
// c.gm = ∂Ids/∂Vge, c.g_ce = ∂Ids/∂Vce, c.ids, c.i_eq
assert!(c.ids > 0.0);
```

#### Varactor

```rust
use sindr_devices::varactor::{junction_capacitance, varactor_companion, VaractorParams};

let params = VaractorParams { cj0: 10e-12, phi: 0.7, m: 0.5 };
let c_j = junction_capacitance(-2.0, &params); // reverse-biased capacitance (F)
assert!(c_j < params.cj0);

// Backward Euler companion from the previous timestep's voltage; dt = 0.0 gives a DC open circuit.
let (g_eq, i_eq) = varactor_companion(-2.0, 1e-6, &params);
```

#### Other diodes and sensors

```rust
use sindr_devices::led::{led_params, LedColor};
use sindr_devices::photodiode::{photodiode_companion, PhotodiodeParams};
use sindr_devices::photoresistor::{ldr_resistance, PhotoresistorParams};
use sindr_devices::schottky::{schottky_companion, SchottkyParams};
use sindr_devices::thermistor::{thermistor_resistance, ThermistorParams};
use sindr_devices::zener::{zener_companion, ZenerParams};

let red = led_params(LedColor::Red); // DiodeParams for use with diode_companion
let (g, i) = schottky_companion(0.3, &SchottkyParams::default()); // IS=1e-8, N=1.0
let (g, i) = zener_companion(-5.5, &ZenerParams::new(5.1)); // Vz = 5.1 V
let (g, i) = photodiode_companion(-1.0, 0.1, &PhotodiodeParams::default()); // 0.1 W irradiance

let r_85c = thermistor_resistance(358.15, &ThermistorParams::ntc_10k()); // ~2.5 kΩ
let r_dim = ldr_resistance(0.5, &PhotoresistorParams::default()); // 0.0 dark – 1.0 bright
assert!(r_85c < 10_000.0 && r_dim > 1_000.0);
```

### Optional features

| Feature | Enables |
|---------|---------|
| `serde` *(default)* | `Serialize`/`Deserialize` on all param structs |

```toml
# Without serde:
sindr-devices = { version = "0.3", default-features = false }
```


# Scope and limitations (LIMITATIONS.md)

## Scope & Limitations

sindr is an **analog circuit simulator**: a SPICE-style MNA solver with semiconductor companion models, written in pure Rust. This document is the honest counterpart to the READMEs — it lists capabilities sindr does **not** have today, so you can decide whether it fits your use case before investing.

Status: `0.3.0`, before 1.0. Anything below may change.

### What sindr is

- DC, nonlinear DC (Newton-Raphson), transient (Gear-2 (default), trapezoidal or backward Euler), AC, noise, transfer function (`.tf`), DC and AC sensitivity (`.sens`), pole-zero (`.pz`), loop gain and stability margins, DC sweep, temperature sweep
- Passives, sources, switches, controlled sources, op-amp / comparator macromodels, transformer, crystal, ferrite bead
- Diode family (Si, LED, Zener, Schottky, photodiode, varactor), BJT (Ebers-Moll), MOSFET (Level-1), IGBT, JFET
- Thermistor, photoresistor, potentiometer, relay, fuse, linear voltage regulator (dropout, quiescent current, current limit, line and load regulation), battery (open-circuit voltage by state of charge, series resistance, optional RC pair)
- Programmatic Rust API + serde JSON for circuits and results

If your problem is "given an analog topology built in Rust, what are the node voltages and branch currents (possibly over time, frequency, or temperature)?", sindr is in scope.

### Out of scope (by design, today)

These are non-goals for the current crate split. They may live in sibling crates later, but they will not appear in `sindr` itself.

| Area | Status |
|------|--------|
| Digital logic simulation (gates, flip-flops, clocked sequential, event-driven kernel) | Out of scope |
| HDL ingestion (Verilog, VHDL, SystemVerilog, Verilog-A, VHDL-AMS, SystemC-AMS) | Out of scope |
| Microcontroller / instruction-set simulation | Out of scope |
| PCB layout, routing, parasitics extraction | Out of scope |
| Schematic capture GUI | Out of scope |
| Electromagnetic / field solvers (FEM, FDTD, method-of-moments) | Out of scope |
| Mechanical / multi-physics co-simulation | Out of scope |

For embedded-system design, the practical implication is that sindr can simulate the **analog portions** of a board (power stages, sensor front-ends, signal conditioning, filters) but not the digital MCU + firmware behaviour. To pair the two, run the firmware in your own emulator and drive the circuit with a `TransientSession`: advance it a tick at a time, set the pins' sources, read the ADC nodes, and stop on a threshold crossing for an interrupt.

### Not yet supported, but in scope

These are gaps a SPICE user would reasonably expect. They are plausible additions; none are committed.

#### Netlist & ecosystem

- **SPICE netlist import: partial.** The `spice` feature (`sindr::spice`, on by default) parses a practical subset of SPICE3f5 decks — R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, M, J, B (behavioural, with the `VALUE` form of E/G and the `POLY` form of E/G/F/H), X, linear E/G/F/H, K (two coupled inductors; no three-winding coupling), plus `.subckt`, `.global`, `.model`, `.tran`, `.dc`, `.ac`, `.tf`, `.sens`, `.noise`, `.pz`, `.meas`, `.op`, `.ic`, `.nodeset`, `.options`, `.param`, `.include`, `.lib` — into a `Circuit`. `.options` reads `RELTOL`, `VNTOL`, `TRTOL` and `ITL1`; any other option is rejected in strict mode and ignored with a warning in lenient mode. V and I lines take `[DC] v`, `AC [mag [phase]]` and a `PULSE`/`SIN`/`PWL` waveform in any order; `ParsedNetlist::ac_config` drives `.ac` from the one V line with an `AC` spec, so a deck with an `AC` spec on an I line or on several sources needs its `AcConfig` set by hand (AC analysis drives a single voltage source). Full SPICE3 coverage and the `TABLE`/`LAPLACE` forms of E/G/F/H are **not** implemented. `.model` cards are read only for what sindr's models have: `IS`, `N`, `RS`, `CJO`, `VJ`, `M`, `FC`, `TT`, `BV`, `IBV`, `KF`, `AF`, `EG`, `XTI` on diodes and `IS`, `BF`, `BR`, `NF`, `NR`, `VAF`, `KF`, `AF`, `EG`, `XTI` on BJTs. `EG` and `XTI` set how `IS` follows temperature, as SPICE's `IS(T)`; `TNOM` is read only at 27 °C, the temperature sindr's values are at. Temperature moves `IS` and the thermal voltage only: `VJ`, `CJO` and `BF` (`XTB`) stay at their 27 °C values. Anything else (BJT junction capacitance, Gummel–Poon high-injection terms) is rejected in strict mode and ignored with a warning in lenient mode. Vendor model libraries that rely on BSIM / Gummel-Poon model cards remain unreachable.
- **SPICE netlist export: partial.** `sindr::spice::to_netlist` writes R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, M, J, B, E, G, F, H and transformers (as L–L–K), plus exact equivalents for switches, fuses, potentiometers, photoresistors, thermistors, LEDs and Schottky diodes. A MOSFET with flicker noise, IGBT, zener, op-amp, comparator, relay, photodiode, varactor and regulator have no export, and neither does a junction away from 27 °C or a BJT with parasitic capacitances. No analysis cards or `AC` specs are written. sindr's parser reads every line it writes back.
- **Hierarchy: definitions with evaluated values only.** `Circuit` has blocks, instances, global nets and part data, and the `spice` parser keeps `.subckt` structure. Blocks hold evaluated values, not parameter expressions, so a subckt whose instances bind different `.param`s becomes one block per distinct body (`name`, `name_2`, …). Reference designators are per block definition, with no per-instance annotation.
- **Model cards: Shockley and Ebers–Moll subsets only.** `Diode` and `Bjt` take a `DiodeModel` / `BjtModel` (which a SPICE `.model` card fills in), but there are no BSIM / Gummel-Poon / VBIC / HICUM models, MOSFET and JFET take level-1 `NMOS`/`PMOS` and `NJF`/`PJF` cards (a JFET's `VTO`, `BETA` and gate capacitances `CGS`, `CGD`, `PB`, `M`, `FC`), and the other devices take only their Rust parameter structs. A manufacturer card matches sindr's behaviour only when it uses no parameters beyond those. A diode's charge sits across its terminals in transient, at the junction voltage the diode current sets across RS; the drop the charging current itself makes across RS is left out, which matters only for large RS. AC is exact (RS in series with the junction). CJO and VJ don't scale with temperature, and the reverse leakage between 0 and breakdown is Shockley's `−IS` rather than ngspice's cubic. The BJT's Early effect (`VAF`) is `ic·(1 + vce/VAF)`, not SPICE's Gummel–Poon base charge, and `VAR` isn't modelled.
- **Behavioural sources are expressions, not a device language.** `CircuitElement::Behavioural` (SPICE's `B`) is one voltage or current set by an expression of node voltages, branch currents and time. There is no Verilog-A, no internal state or charge (`ddt`, `idt`), and no XSPICE code models; a new device with its own state means writing a Rust companion model. Steps and comparisons in an expression have zero slope, so a hard switch can stall Newton where a smooth one (`tanh`) converges. An expression has no device limiting (SPICE's `pnjlim`): an exponential written as a `B` source is reached by halving steps that overflow and then source stepping, so it takes more iterations than the built-in diode, and an expression's value is good to the solver's `reltol` rather than to rounding.

#### Analyses

| Analysis | Supported | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| `.op` (operating point) | ✅ | via `solve_op`: capacitors open, inductors shorted, sources at their t = 0 value |
| `.dc` (DC sweep) | ✅ | one source (`dc_sweep`) or two nested (`dc_sweep_nested`), voltage or current; each point an operating point, as `.op` |
| `.tran` (transient) | ✅ | Gear-2, trapezoidal or backward Euler (`solve_transient`). Steps up to `tstep`, shortened by local truncation error and landing on waveform breakpoints. `tstart` keeps the result from there on |
| `.ac` (small-signal AC) | ✅ | swept frequency response |
| `.tf` (transfer function) | ✅ | DC small-signal gain, input and output resistance (`solve_tf`) |
| `.temp` (temperature sweep) | ✅ | junction-device temp parameter |
| `.noise` (noise analysis) | ✅ | thermal, shot and flicker (`solve_noise`), at 27 °C. Op-amps, regulators, controlled sources and a diode's `RS` are noiseless; no BJT base-resistance noise |
| `.disto` / harmonic distortion | ❌ | |
| `.pz` (pole-zero) | ✅ | poles and zeros of a voltage gain or transimpedance between node pairs (`solve_pz`). A repeated root is only accurate to about √ε; a root more than ~1e13 times the circuit's own frequency scale counts as infinite |
| `.sens` (sensitivity) | ⚠️ | DC (`solve_sensitivity`) and AC (`solve_ac_sensitivity`, `.sens ... ac`), for resistance, source values, all four controlled-source gains, and diode (IS, N, RS), BJT (BF, IS, BR, NF, NR, VAF) and MOSFET (KP, VTO, LAMBDA) model parameters; in AC also C, L, the stimulus's AC magnitude and a diode's CJO and TT. AC holds the bias point fixed, as ngspice does: a parameter's effect through the operating point (and so on every other device's small-signal conductances) is left out, and a source's DC value has no AC entry. No entries for LED, Zener, Schottky, photodiode, JFET or IGBT parameters, a diode's BV/IBV, VJ/M/FC, or a transformer. A self-heated device is held at its balanced junction temperature (the thermal loop's dependence on the parameter is left out) |
| Monte Carlo / worst-case / corner analysis | ✅ | `variation::monte_carlo` and `variation::corners`, over resistance, capacitance, inductance and source values (uniform or Gaussian, independent, seeded). Specs (`check_specs`) and ratings (`ratings_over`) at their worst run. No correlated tolerances, no device-model parameters, no `.mc` / `.step` cards, no derating or SOA yet |
| `.four` (Fourier analysis) | ✅ | `sindr::fourier::Fourier`: harmonics, phases and THD of a transient signal, as ngspice's (last period, linear resample, 200 points by default). The `.four` card isn't parsed yet: call it on the result |
| `.fft` on transient output | ✅ | `sindr::fourier::Fft`: a radix-2 FFT of a linear resample onto a power of two of points, windowed (Hann by default; rectangular, Hamming, Blackman, flat-top), one-sided and scaled to peak amplitude. No zero padding, no averaging of segments (Welch) |
| `.meas` (measurements) | ⚠️ | `sindr::measure`: statistics, `FIND … AT`, `WHEN`, `TRIG`/`TARG`, plus rise/fall, settling and −3 dB in the API. No `FIND … WHEN`, `DERIV` or `PARAM=`; no currents on AC results |
| Periodic steady-state (PSS / shooting / harmonic balance) | ❌ | relevant for switching converters, RF |
| S-parameter / two-port extraction | ❌ | |
| Stability / loop-gain (Middlebrook, Tian) | ✅ | Tian's double injection at a 0 V probe source in series with the loop (`solve_loop_gain`): loop gain, crossovers, phase and gain margins. One break point at a time; no all-loops (`stb`-style) search |

#### Device models

- **Op-amp macromodel: single pole.** `OpAmpModel` gives open-loop gain, a dominant pole from GBW, slew rate, output resistance, input offset and bias current, and a rail clamp. There is no second pole or phase margin, no output current limit, no supply current, no input common-mode range, no noise and no CMRR/PSRR. Vendor op-amp models can't be loaded. Without a `model` the op-amp is a gain-1e5 VCVS with no rail clamp.
- **Batteries are an equivalent circuit, with no chemistry.** `Battery` has an open-circuit voltage curve, a series resistance and one RC pair. Capacity doesn't fall at high current (Peukert) or in the cold, resistance doesn't rise as the cell empties, and there's no aging, self-discharge, charging limit or hysteresis between charge and discharge curves. A battery is noiseless in `.noise`, and SPICE export refuses it.
- **Regulators are linear and piecewise.** `VoltageRegulator` has dropout, quiescent current, a current limit and line and load regulation, positive or negative (a negative `voltage` mirrors the characteristic, for a 79xx), but no foldback, thermal shutdown, PSRR that falls with frequency, or start-up behaviour. It has no control loop either, so its output capacitor's value and ESR don't affect stability (an LDO that oscillates without its output capacitor on a real board is stable here) and don't change the load-step response; capacitors on a regulator show up only as inrush and hold-up. Its temperature doesn't feed back: self-heating reports its junction temperature, but its output doesn't drift with it. No references, adjustable regulators (LM317 with its divider) or DC-DC controllers.
- **MOSFET is Level 1 only.** No BSIM (3 / 4 / 6 / -CMG), no EKV, no PSP. Short-channel effects, velocity saturation, mobility degradation and gate leakage are absent.
- **MOSFETs have three terminals, with the body tied to the source** (as in a discrete part), so the body effect (`gamma`, `phi`) never applies in a circuit. There's no fourth body terminal for IC-style biasing to a rail.
- **BJT is Ebers-Moll with optional Early voltage.** No Gummel-Poon, no VBIC, no HICUM. No high-injection, base-width modulation in saturation, charge-storage beyond the optional Cbe/Cbc parasitic caps.
- **JFET gate capacitances are depletion charge only, at 27 °C.** `parasitic_caps` gives CGS and CGD as SPICE's graded junctions (`PB`, `M`, `FC`), but the gate junction conducts no current, and `PB` and the capacitances don't follow temperature. ngspice's JFET grades at `M = 0.5` whatever the card says, so a deck with another `M` solves differently there.
- **A MOSFET's body diode is DC and junction charge only.** `body_diode` takes a full diode card (IS, N, RS, CJO, TT, BV), solved as a diode `<id>.body`; there's no separate reverse-recovery model beyond TT, and no body diode on IGBTs.
- **No SiC / GaN device models.**
- **Crystals and ferrite beads are linear networks.** A crystal is the Butterworth–Van Dyke model: no overtones, spurious modes, drive-level dependence or aging. A ferrite bead is R + L ∥ R (∥ C) with no DC-bias derating, so its impedance doesn't fall with current as a real bead's does.
- **Magnetics: saturating cores, no more.** `Inductor` can saturate along a smooth single-valued curve (`InductorSaturation`), and so can a `Transformer`'s magnetising branch, which carries the shared core flux behind each winding's leakage. There's no hysteresis, remanence, core loss or temperature dependence, a transformer has two windings, and SPICE export refuses a saturating core.
- **No transmission lines** (lossless or lossy / W-element).
- **No piezo / MEMS / electro-mechanical coupling.**
- **No switched-capacitor primitives** (sample-and-hold, charge-redistribution).

#### Solver & numerics

- **Fixed-order integrators only:** Gear-2 (the default), trapezoidal and backward Euler, chosen with `TransientConfig::with_method`. No variable-order Gear. Gear-2 damps lightly-damped LC tanks slightly over many periods; trapezoidal keeps their amplitude but can ring on time constants much shorter than the step; backward Euler damps strongly.
- **Sparse LU above 100 unknowns** (`faer`), dense below. A 10 000-node resistor ladder solves in about 4 ms and a 100×100 RC mesh in about 15 ms per solve. No KLU-style partial refactorisation.
- **Convergence aids: gmin stepping, then source stepping.** When plain Newton–Raphson fails on a nonlinear DC solve, sindr retries with a gmin-stepping homotopy (`1e-2` S down to the `1e-12` floor), then by ramping every source up from zero, warm-starting between steps. `SimulationResult::convergence_aid` says which one was needed. No pseudo-transient continuation. `ConvergenceFailed` names the node that won't settle, the components on it and the point of the analysis (`SolvePoint`), with the last Newton step (not a KCL residual).
- **`.nodeset`** (`SolverOptions::nodeset`) seeds the DC operating point and the bias point of AC, noise, `.tf`, `.sens` and every sweep, through a `Solver`.
- **A transient starts switched on at t = 0 unless asked otherwise:** `TransientConfig::new` starts from the initial conditions alone (SPICE's `UIC`), where SPICE starts from the DC operating point. `TransientStart::OperatingPoint` does what SPICE does, and a deck's `.tran` maps onto it (`uic` onto the other). The operating point it starts from is solved without self-heating. Initial winding currents on a transformer can't be set, and inductor `IC=` on SPICE element lines isn't parsed. With `tstart`, sindr's first snapshot is at `tstart` itself, where ngspice's is its first step past it.
- **Truncation-error control is per node voltage** (SPICE-style RELTOL 1e-3, VNTOL 1 µV, TRTOL 7 by default; set them in `SolverOptions`), not per charge or flux. The step never exceeds `tstep`, so a coarse `tstep` buys speed only between edges.
- **No checkpointing / restart** of long transient runs.
- **Large transients are slower than ngspice.** On a 1 000-node RC ladder, 200 steps take 151 ms in sindr and about 29 ms in ngspice's solve (5×, `examples/vs_ngspice.rs`). Each step re-assembles and refactors the matrix. sindr wins up to a few hundred nodes, where ngspice's 14 ms start dominates, and on DC operating points at every size measured (a 3 000-diode chain: 27 ms against 82 ms). Long transients of thousands of nodes are ngspice's ground.
- **No multithreading** inside one solve. Separate solves do run in parallel threads.
- **Automatic differentiation for behavioural sources only.** A `Behavioural` source's Jacobian comes from forward-mode automatic differentiation of its expression. Device models are differentiated by hand, and so are the sensitivities: adjoint sensitivity (DC, and AC at a fixed bias) covers the parameters in the table above. There's no differentiation of a whole circuit with respect to arbitrary inputs.
- **No interval / affine arithmetic** for guaranteed bounds.

#### Self-heating & thermal

- **Self-heating is one thermal RC per part.** A part with `Part::thermal` runs at `ambient + P·Rθ` (iterated to a balance in DC, a thermal RC state in transient). There's no thermal coupling between parts (a shared heatsink, neighbours on a board), and no multi-pole Foster/Cauer ladder for the junction-to-case path.
- **Only junction devices and the thermistor feel their temperature:** diodes, LEDs, Zeners, Schottkys, photodiodes, BJTs and thermistors. MOSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs and resistors report a junction temperature (and so get Tj-max checks), but their models have no temperature in them, so heating doesn't move their operating point. Power-MOSFET and IGBT runaway is not predicted.
- **An LED's temperature coefficient is one typical figure:** Vf falls 2 mV/K at its rated 20 mA for every colour, from an effective EG per colour. Real parts range from about −1.5 to −4 mV/K.
- **Self-heating applies to `solve_circuit` and `solve_transient`** (and the same on a `Solver`) (and `temperature_sweep`, which sets the ambient), and to the bias point of AC, `.tf`, `.sens` and `.noise`, which linearise each device at its balanced junction temperature. `dc_sweep` solves each point unheated.
- In a transient the electrical step solves at the temperature from the step before. Thermal time constants are far longer than the electrical steps, so the lag doesn't matter unless the step is coarse compared with Rθ·Cθ.

#### Tooling & UX

- **No CLI**. sindr is a library only.
- **No schematic input**. Circuits are written as Rust `Vec<CircuitElement>` (or JSON via serde).
- **No parsers for editors' own netlist files.** `sindr::import` takes a netlist an editor has already read (components, values, nets), not the editor's file format.
- **No part-number lookup.** `sindr::import` builds a model from what a part's data says (a colour, datasheet figures such as `vf` at `if`, `hfe`, `vce_sat`, `vth`, `rds_on`), not from its part number: a `PMBT3904` with no figures gets the default NPN, with a warning in `ImportedCircuit::warnings`.
- **Datasheet fits are as simple as the models.** A BJT's gain is the same at every collector current (`hfe_ic` doesn't move it), and with no collector resistance in the model a Vce(sat) fit gives a low BR. A MOSFET fit is Level 1 through one threshold and one on-resistance point, so the transfer curve between them is a square law. A zener fit shifts only the breakdown voltage; its 1 Ω dynamic resistance is fixed. An LED given by `vf` at `if` imports as a diode element with the fitted model, not as an LED element.
- **ICs import as black boxes.** A part `sindr::import` has no kind for (a microcontroller, a timer) can come in as a `ComponentKind::BlackBox`, which simulates nothing: its pins draw and drive no current, so a net only it holds up floats. Model the part's behaviour with bench sources and loads, or leave it out of the analysis.
- **Waveform export is CSV only.** Transient, AC and sweep results have `to_csv()`; there's no VCD, Touchstone or Common Simulation Data Format.
- **No built-in plotting**. Examples like `bode_plot.rs` produce data; rendering is on the user.
- **No interactive REPL or notebook integration.**
- **No `no_std` support.** `nalgebra` and `std::collections::HashMap` are pulled in.

### Numerical caveats worth knowing

- Transformer coupling `k = 1.0` is mathematically singular — clamp to `≤ 0.999`.
- Switches are modelled as `0.01 Ω` / `1 GΩ` resistors — they are not ideal, and very high-impedance circuits may need explicit values.
- An op-amp without a `model` is a VCVS with gain `1e5` and no frequency response or rail clamp, so its closed-loop bandwidth isn't realistic. Give the op-amp an `OpAmpModel` for GBW and slew rate. Its stage starts from 0 V at t = 0, like the capacitors, so a transient opens with a short settle unless you seed it.
- A comparator has gain `1e5` and its output clamped to `v_neg`/`v_pos`, but no propagation delay, hysteresis or open-collector output: it switches the instant its inputs cross, and a slow, noisy input can chatter.
- For accurate ringing amplitude in a resonant circuit, use `IntegrationMethod::Trapezoidal` with a step well below the period: Gear-2 and especially backward Euler damp it.
- Photodiode / photoresistor / thermistor "stimulus" parameters (irradiance, light level, temperature) have no waveform: they are constant through a `solve_transient`. A `TransientSession` can change them between steps (`set_param`).

### Useful workarounds

- Need a vendor BJT / MOSFET? A level-1 MOSFET or JFET subcircuit loads as is; otherwise fit Ebers-Moll / Level-1 parameters from the datasheet. Accuracy will be modest.
- Need digital control around an analog plant? Drive it with a `TransientSession` from your own loop: advance a control period, read node voltages, set sources, switches and pots, and use `run_until` to stop where a comparator would trip.
- Need a second pole or phase margin on an op-amp? Build it from VCVS stages and RC networks around an `OpAmp` with an `OpAmpModel`.
- Need a tolerance on a device-model parameter, or correlated parts? Loop in Rust over your own variations of the `Circuit`; sindr is fast enough for thousands of solves on small circuits.

### Reporting gaps

If a missing capability is blocking real work, open an issue describing the **circuit and analysis you want to run**, not just the feature name — concrete use cases drive prioritisation.


# Public API of `sindr`

## `sindr/src/ac_analysis.rs`

AC small-signal analysis module.

Performs frequency-domain analysis by:
1. Finding the DC operating point (capacitors open, inductors shorted)
2. Linearizing all nonlinear elements at that point
3. Building a complex-valued MNA system at each frequency
4. Solving for node voltages as complex phasors

```rust
/// Frequency sweep spacing.
pub enum FrequencySpacing {
    /// Logarithmic spacing: `num_points` in total, evenly spaced in
    /// log10(f) from `f_start` to `f_stop`. Not points per decade.
    Logarithmic,
    /// Linear spacing.
    Linear,
}

/// AC analysis configuration. Build one with [`AcConfig::new`] and its
/// `with_*` setters.
pub struct AcConfig {
    /// Start frequency (Hz).
    pub f_start: f64,
    /// Stop frequency (Hz).
    pub f_stop: f64,
    /// Number of frequency points, including both endpoints. With 1, only
    /// `f_start` is solved.
    pub num_points: usize,
    /// Frequency spacing.
    pub spacing: FrequencySpacing,
    /// ID of the AC source (voltage source with AC stimulus).
    pub source_id: String,
    /// AC amplitude of the source: volts, linear (not dB). Results scale
    /// with it; 1 V makes node voltages read as gain.
    pub ac_magnitude: f64,
    /// AC phase of the source in degrees, as SPICE's `AC mag phase`. Every
    /// node's phase shifts by it; 0 makes [`AcPoint::phase_deg`] read as the
    /// phase relative to the source.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub ac_phase_deg: f64,
}

impl AcConfig {
    /// Sweep `num_points` frequencies from `f_start` to `f_stop` (Hz), both
    /// included, driving the voltage source `source_id`. Spacing defaults
    /// to [`FrequencySpacing::Logarithmic`], the source's AC magnitude to
    /// 1 V and its phase to 0°, so node voltages read as gain relative to
    /// the source.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::ac_analysis::{AcConfig, FrequencySpacing};
    ///
    /// // SPICE `.ac lin 101 1k 2k` on `V1 in 0 AC 2 90`.
    /// let config = AcConfig::new("V1", 1e3, 2e3, 101)
    ///     .with_spacing(FrequencySpacing::Linear)
    ///     .with_magnitude(2.0)
    ///     .with_phase_deg(90.0);
    /// assert_eq!(config.num_points, 101);
    /// ```
    pub fn new(source_id: impl Into<String>, f_start: f64, f_stop: f64, num_points: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// Space the frequencies by `spacing` instead of logarithmically.
    pub fn with_spacing(mut self, spacing: FrequencySpacing) -> Self { … }

    /// Drive the source with an AC amplitude of `magnitude` volts (linear,
    /// not dB) instead of 1 V.
    pub fn with_magnitude(mut self, magnitude: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Give the source an AC phase of `phase_deg` degrees instead of 0°, as
    /// SPICE's `AC mag phase`.
    pub fn with_phase_deg(mut self, phase_deg: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// Result at a single frequency point.
pub struct AcPoint {
    /// Frequency of this point (Hz).
    pub frequency: f64,
    /// Complex node voltages (V) keyed by node name. Includes the ground
    /// node (always 0).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "schemars", schemars(with = "HashMap<String, [f64; 2]>"))]
    pub node_voltages: HashMap<String, Complex64>,
}

impl AcPoint {
    /// The complex voltage at `node` (V), or `None` when there's no such
    /// node. Ground reads 0.
    pub fn voltage(&self, node: &str) -> Option<Complex64> { … }

    /// The magnitude of the voltage at `node`, `|V(node)|` (V).
    pub fn magnitude(&self, node: &str) -> Option<f64> { … }

    /// Gain in dB for a node: `20·log10(|V(node)| / source_magnitude)`, a
    /// voltage ratio. `source_magnitude` is in volts, normally
    /// [`AcConfig::ac_magnitude`]. `None` when the node isn't in the
    /// circuit.
    pub fn gain_db(&self, node: &str, source_magnitude: f64) -> Option<f64> { … }

    /// Phase of a node's voltage in degrees, in (−180°, 180°]: relative to
    /// the source when [`AcConfig::ac_phase_deg`] is 0, absolute otherwise,
    /// as ngspice reports it. `None` when the node isn't in the
    /// circuit.
    pub fn phase_deg(&self, node: &str) -> Option<f64> { … }
}

/// Complete AC analysis result.
pub struct AcResult {
    /// Result points, one per swept frequency.
    pub points: Vec<AcPoint>,
    /// Configuration used to produce this result.
    pub config: AcConfig,
}

impl AcResult {
    /// A node's complex voltage as `(frequency in Hz, V)` pairs, one per
    /// point. Empty when there's no such node.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::{solve_ac, AcConfig, Circuit, CircuitElement};
    /// use sindr::element::{Capacitor, Resistor, VoltageSource};
    ///
    /// // RC low-pass, corner at 1/(2π·1k·1µ) ≈ 159 Hz.
    /// let circuit = Circuit::new("0", vec![
    ///     CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 0.0, waveform: None }),
    ///     CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 }),
    ///     CircuitElement::Capacitor(Capacitor { id: "C1".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], capacitance: 1e-6 }),
    /// ]);
    /// let ac = solve_ac(&circuit, &AcConfig::new("V1", 1.0, 1e5, 51))?;
    ///
    /// let first = &ac.points[0];
    /// assert!((first.magnitude("out").unwrap() - 1.0).abs() < 1e-3);
    /// let (f, v) = *ac.node_voltage_curve("out").last().unwrap();
    /// assert_eq!(f, 1e5);
    /// assert!(v.norm() < 0.01);
    /// assert_eq!(ac.magnitude_curve("out").len(), 51);
    /// assert!(ac.node_voltage_curve("nope").is_empty());
    /// # Ok::<(), sindr::SimError>(())
    /// ```
    ///
    pub fn node_voltage_curve(&self, node: &str) -> Vec<(f64, Complex64)> { … }

    /// A node's voltage magnitude as `(frequency in Hz, |V| in V)` pairs,
    /// one per point; [`AcResult::gain_curve`] has it in dB.
    pub fn magnitude_curve(&self, node: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }

    /// The gain curve for a node as `(frequency in Hz, gain in dB)` pairs,
    /// one per point, using [`AcConfig::ac_magnitude`].
    pub fn gain_curve(&self, node: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }

    /// The phase curve for a node as `(frequency in Hz, phase in degrees)`
    /// pairs, one per point; see [`AcPoint::phase_deg`].
    pub fn phase_curve(&self, node: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }
}

/// Performs AC small-signal frequency-domain analysis.
///
/// Returns the complex node voltages at every frequency in the configured
/// sweep, plus helpers on [`AcResult`] for extracting gain (dB) and phase
/// (degrees) curves — i.e. Bode plot data.
///
/// # Algorithm
///
/// 1. Solve the DC operating point of `circuit`, with capacitors and
///    varactors open and inductors and transformer windings shorted.
/// 2. Linearise every nonlinear element at that operating point: diodes,
///    LEDs, Zener, Schottky and photodiodes, BJTs (full terminal Jacobian,
///    junction temperature included), MOSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs, and varactors
///    (their capacitance at the bias). A relay's contact is open or closed
///    as the bias point leaves it.
/// 3. At each frequency, build a complex-valued MNA system (capacitors and
///    inductors become `jωC` / `jωL` admittances, a transformer the coupled
///    pair `V = jω·[[L1, M], [M, L2]]·I`), solve it, and store the complex
///    node voltage phasors.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if `config` is invalid: zero points,
///   non-finite values, `f_start > f_stop`, `f_start <= 0` with logarithmic
///   spacing, `f_start < 0` with linear spacing, or more than 10⁷ points;
///   or if `source_id` isn't the id of a voltage source in `circuit`
/// - Any [`SimError`] from the DC operating-point solve
/// - [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the linearised AC system is singular
///   at any frequency
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::ac_analysis::{solve_ac, AcConfig};
/// use sindr::element::{Capacitor, Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// // Simple RC low-pass: V1 -> R1 -> n_out -> C1 -> gnd
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n_in".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n_in".into(), "n_out".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Capacitor(Capacitor {
///             id: "C1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n_out".into(), "0".into()],
///             capacitance: 1e-6,
///         }),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// // 11 points from 1 Hz to 100 kHz, log-spaced, 1 V on V1.
/// let config = AcConfig::new("V1", 1.0, 100_000.0, 11);
///
/// let result = solve_ac(&circuit, &config).unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(result.points.len(), 11);
///
/// // Bode plot data for the output node:
/// let gain = result.gain_curve("n_out");
/// let phase = result.phase_curve("n_out");
/// ```
///
pub fn solve_ac(circuit: &Circuit, config: &AcConfig) -> Result<AcResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/circuit.rs`

Circuit input format.

[`Circuit`] is the root struct sindr's analyses take: a list of
[`CircuitElement`]s plus the name of the ground node, and optionally a
design hierarchy (see [`crate::design`]). Components share a node by
referencing the same node-name string; there are no separate "wire" or
"net" objects.

[`CircuitElement`] is the open-ended enum of supported component types
(resistors, sources, semiconductors, magnetics, …). Each variant wraps a
struct from [`crate::element`] carrying its parameters and a fixed-size
`nodes` array; sign conventions are documented per struct.

```rust
/// BJT parasitic capacitances. All values in Farads. Default 0.0 disables each cap.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct BjtParasiticCaps {
    /// Base-Emitter junction capacitance (F). Typical: 5–50 pF.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub cbe: f64,
    /// Base-Collector junction capacitance (F). Typical: 1–10 pF.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub cbc: f64,
}

/// Parameters of a [`CircuitElement::Diode`], as a SPICE `.model D` card
/// gives them: Shockley (IS, N, RS), charge storage (CJO, VJ, M, FC, TT) and
/// reverse breakdown (BV, IBV). Values are at the nominal 27 °C; the
/// element's `temperature` scales `is` from there with `eg` and `xti`, as
/// SPICE's `IS(T)` does, and only `is`.
///
/// The default is sindr's built-in silicon diode. With serde, a missing field
/// takes its default, so `{"rs": 0.5}` is a silicon diode with 0.5 Ω in series.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct DiodeModel {
    /// Saturation current IS (A), positive. Default 1e-14.
    pub is: f64,
    /// Emission coefficient N, positive. Default 1.
    pub n: f64,
    /// Series resistance RS (Ω), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub rs: f64,
    /// Zero-bias depletion capacitance CJO (F), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub cjo: f64,
    /// Junction potential VJ (V), positive. Default 1.
    pub vj: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient M, in `[0, 0.9]`. Default 0.5.
    pub m: f64,
    /// Forward-bias depletion capacitance coefficient FC, in `[0, 0.95]`.
    /// Default 0.5.
    pub fc: f64,
    /// Transit time TT (s), zero or positive: the diffusion charge is
    /// `TT·I_d`, which sets reverse recovery. Default 0.
    pub tt: f64,
    /// Reverse breakdown voltage BV (V), positive. Default `None`: no
    /// breakdown, as in SPICE without `BV`.
    pub bv: Option<f64>,
    /// Current at `−BV`, IBV (A), positive. Default 1 mA.
    pub ibv: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise coefficient KF, zero or positive: noise analysis puts
    /// `KF·|Id|^AF / f` (A²/Hz) across the junction. Default 0.
    pub kf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise exponent AF, positive. Default 1.
    pub af: f64,
    /// Bandgap EG (eV), positive: how fast `is` rises with temperature.
    /// Default 1.11, silicon; a Schottky junction is about 0.69.
    pub eg: f64,
    /// Saturation-current temperature exponent XTI, zero or positive.
    /// Default 3, a pn junction; a Schottky junction is 2.
    pub xti: f64,
}

impl DiodeModel {
    /// Whether the diode stores charge (CJO or TT set), which makes the
    /// circuit reactive.
    pub fn stores_charge(&self) -> bool { … }
}

/// Ebers–Moll parameters of a [`CircuitElement::Bjt`], as a SPICE
/// `.model NPN`/`PNP` card gives them. The forward gain is the element's own
/// `bf`. Values are at the nominal 27 °C; the element's `temperature` scales
/// `is` from there with `eg` and `xti`, as SPICE's `IS(T)` does.
///
/// The default is sindr's built-in transistor. With serde, a missing field
/// takes its default.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct BjtModel {
    /// Transport saturation current IS (A), positive. Default 1e-14.
    pub is: f64,
    /// Reverse current gain BR, positive. Default 1.
    pub br: f64,
    /// Forward emission coefficient NF, positive. Default 1.
    pub nf: f64,
    /// Reverse emission coefficient NR, positive. Default 1.
    pub nr: f64,
    /// Forward Early voltage VAF (V), zero or positive; 0 turns the Early
    /// effect off. Default 0. sindr applies it as `ic·(1 + vce/VAF)`, not
    /// through SPICE's Gummel–Poon base charge, so results differ slightly
    /// from SPICE's when it is set.
    pub vaf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise coefficient KF, zero or positive: noise analysis puts
    /// `KF·|Ib|^AF / f` (A²/Hz) across base–emitter. Default 0.
    pub kf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise exponent AF, positive. Default 1.
    pub af: f64,
    /// Bandgap EG (eV), positive: how fast `is` rises with temperature.
    /// Default 1.11, silicon.
    pub eg: f64,
    /// Saturation-current temperature exponent XTI, zero or positive.
    /// Default 3.
    pub xti: f64,
}

/// MOSFET gate parasitic capacitances. All values in Farads.
/// Op-amp macromodel parameters, for [`CircuitElement::OpAmp`]'s `model`.
///
/// The gain stage is a first-order lag towards `gain · (v₊ − v₋ + offset)`,
/// clamped to the rails, with time constant `gain / (2π · gbw)`: open-loop
/// gain `gain / (1 + s·τ)`, so a non-inverting stage of gain G has its
/// −3 dB point near `gbw / G`. Its rate is limited to `slew_rate`. The
/// output is that stage's voltage behind `r_out`.
///
/// The pole and the slew limit act in transient and AC analyses. At DC the
/// stage sits at its clamped target. The op-amp's state doesn't count as
/// reactive, so [`solve_circuit`]-style automatic routing still picks DC
/// for a circuit whose only dynamics are op-amps; run a transient
/// explicitly to see them. Like capacitors, the stage starts from rest
/// (0 V) at t = 0.
///
/// [`solve_circuit`]: https://docs.rs/sindr/latest/sindr/fn.solve_circuit.html
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct OpAmpModel {
    /// Open-loop DC gain (V/V), positive. Default 1e5 (100 dB).
    pub gain: f64,
    /// Gain-bandwidth product (Hz), positive; `None` for no pole. Default
    /// 1 MHz.
    pub gbw: Option<f64>,
    /// Slew rate (V/s), positive; `None` for no limit. Needs `gbw`.
    /// Default 0.5 V/µs.
    pub slew_rate: Option<f64>,
    /// Output resistance (Ω), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub r_out: f64,
    /// Input offset voltage (V), added to `v₊ − v₋`. Default 0.
    pub offset_voltage: f64,
    /// Input bias current (A) drawn by each input, to ground. Default 0.
    pub bias_current: f64,
}

/// Optional gate capacitances of a MOSFET, for transient and AC.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct MosfetParasiticCaps {
    /// Gate-Source capacitance (F). Typical: 100–500 pF for power MOSFETs.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub cgs: f64,
    /// Gate-Drain capacitance (Miller capacitance) (F). Typical: 10–100 pF.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub cgd: f64,
}

/// Gate capacitances of a [`CircuitElement::Jfet`], for transient and AC, as
/// a SPICE `.model NJF`/`PJF` card's `CGS`, `CGD`, `PB`, `M` and `FC` give
/// them.
///
/// Each gate junction is a depletion capacitance
/// `C = C0 / (1 − v/PB)^M` at junction voltage `v` (`vgs` and `vgd` for an
/// N-channel part, their negatives for a P-channel one), continued linearly
/// above `FC·PB` so it stays finite in forward bias, as SPICE's junction
/// charge. Transient integrates the charge, so it is conserved; AC uses the
/// capacitance at the bias point. Values are at the nominal 27 °C.
///
/// The default is no capacitance with SPICE's `PB = 1`, `M = 0.5` and
/// `FC = 0.5`. With serde, a missing field takes its default.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct JfetParasiticCaps {
    /// Zero-bias gate–source capacitance CGS (F), zero or positive. Default 0.
    pub cgs: f64,
    /// Zero-bias gate–drain capacitance CGD (F), zero or positive; the
    /// Miller capacitance of a common-source stage. Default 0.
    pub cgd: f64,
    /// Gate junction potential PB (V), positive. Default 1.
    pub pb: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient M, in `[0, 0.9]`. Default 0.5 (an abrupt
    /// junction, the only value ngspice's JFET has).
    pub m: f64,
    /// Forward-bias depletion coefficient FC, in `[0, 0.95]`: above `FC·PB`
    /// the capacitance is continued linearly. Default 0.5.
    pub fc: f64,
}

impl JfetParasiticCaps {
    /// Whether either gate junction has a capacitance, which makes the
    /// circuit reactive.
    pub fn stores_charge(&self) -> bool { … }
}

/// What a [`CircuitElement::Behavioural`] source's expression sets.
pub enum BehaviouralOutput {
    /// The voltage across the source, `n+` over `n-` (V): SPICE's `V=`.
    Voltage,
    /// The current through the source from `n+` to `n-` (A): SPICE's `I=`.
    Current,
}

/// Which throw of a [`CircuitElement::SwitchSpdt`] the common terminal
/// connects to.
pub enum SpdtPosition {
    /// Common to `nodes[1]`.
    #[default]
    A,
    /// Common to `nodes[2]`.
    B,
}

/// A quartz crystal's Butterworth–Van Dyke model, for
/// [`CircuitElement::Crystal`]: a motional arm `Rm`–`Lm`–`Cm` in series,
/// in parallel with the shunt capacitance `C0`. The series resonance is
/// `frequency`, so `Lm = 1 / ((2π·frequency)²·Cm)`.
///
/// Datasheets give the frequency, the ESR (`Rm`) and the shunt capacitance;
/// the motional capacitance is often only in an application note. The load
/// capacitance a datasheet names isn't part of the crystal: it's the two
/// capacitors on the board.
pub struct CrystalParams {
    /// Series-resonant frequency (Hz), positive.
    pub frequency: f64,
    /// Equivalent series resistance `Rm` (Ω), positive.
    pub esr: f64,
    /// Shunt capacitance `C0` (F), zero or positive.
    pub c0: f64,
    /// Motional capacitance `Cm` (F), positive.
    pub cm: f64,
}

impl CrystalParams {
    /// From a datasheet's frequency, ESR and shunt capacitance, with a
    /// motional capacitance of `c0 / 250`, typical of AT-cut crystals in
    /// the megahertz range.
    pub fn from_datasheet(frequency: f64, esr: f64, c0: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Motional inductance `Lm` (H), from the frequency and `Cm`.
    pub fn lm(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// A ferrite bead's circuit, for [`CircuitElement::FerriteBead`]: `r_dc`
/// in series with `l ∥ r_ac` (and `c`, when set). Below its peak the bead
/// is inductive, at the peak it's `r_ac`, and above it `c` takes over.
pub struct FerriteBeadParams {
    /// DC resistance (Ω), positive.
    pub r_dc: f64,
    /// Inductance (H), positive.
    pub l: f64,
    /// Parallel loss resistance (Ω), positive: about the impedance at the
    /// peak.
    pub r_ac: f64,
    /// Parallel capacitance (F); `None` for none.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub c: Option<f64>,
}

impl FerriteBeadParams {
    /// From a datasheet's impedance at 100 MHz and DC resistance. Takes the
    /// bead as inductive up to 100 MHz, `l = z_100mhz / (2π·100 MHz)`, with
    /// its loss resistance at the same impedance: a rough fit that matches
    /// at 100 MHz and below. Fit `l`, `r_ac` and `c` to the impedance curve
    /// when the peak matters.
    pub fn from_datasheet(z_100mhz: f64, r_dc: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// A single circuit component.
///
/// Each variant carries an `id` (unique per circuit, used to look up results)
/// and a `nodes` array naming its terminals. Node names are arbitrary
/// strings — components share a node by referencing the same string.
///
/// # Sign conventions
///
/// - **Two-terminal components** (resistor, source, capacitor, …):
///   `nodes[0]` is the positive / first terminal, `nodes[1]` is the
///   negative / second.
/// - **Polarised components** (voltage/current sources, diodes, BJTs, …):
///   exact terminal order is documented per variant.
/// - **Currents** are reported as flowing from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]` for
///   two-terminal components.
///
/// # Serde
///
/// With the default `serde` feature enabled, `CircuitElement` serialises
/// using a `type` discriminator: `{"type": "resistor", "id": "R1", ...}`.
pub enum CircuitElement {
    /// Resistor between two nodes.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "resistor"))]
    Resistor(Resistor),

    /// Independent voltage source.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "voltage_source"))]
    VoltageSource(VoltageSource),

    /// Independent current source.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "current_source"))]
    CurrentSource(CurrentSource),

    /// Switch between two nodes.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "switch"))]
    Switch(Switch),

    /// Capacitor.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "capacitor"))]
    Capacitor(Capacitor),

    /// A battery: open-circuit voltage by state of charge behind a series
    /// resistance and an optional RC pair
    /// ([`BatteryParams`](sindr_devices::battery::BatteryParams)).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "battery"))]
    Battery(Battery),

    /// Inductor.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "inductor"))]
    Inductor(Inductor),

    /// Diode (Shockley model, silicon unless `model` says otherwise).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "diode"))]
    Diode(Diode),

    /// LED.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "led"))]
    Led(Led),

    /// BJT transistor (3 terminals): Ebers–Moll with Early effect, solved in
    /// DC, transient and AC.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "bjt"))]
    Bjt(Bjt),

    /// MOSFET transistor (3 terminals: gate, drain, source; the body is tied to
    /// the source).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "mosfet"))]
    Mosfet(Mosfet),

    /// N-channel or P-channel JFET (Shockley square-law model).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "jfet"))]
    Jfet(Jfet),

    /// Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source: V_out = mu * V_control.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "vcvs"))]
    Vcvs(Vcvs),

    /// Voltage-Controlled Current Source: I_out = gm * V_control.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "vccs"))]
    Vccs(Vccs),

    /// Current-Controlled Voltage Source: V_out = rm * I_control.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "ccvs"))]
    Ccvs(Ccvs),

    /// Current-Controlled Current Source: I_out = alpha * I_control.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "cccs"))]
    Cccs(Cccs),

    /// Pushbutton (momentary switch): identical behaviour to Switch.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pushbutton"))]
    Pushbutton(Pushbutton),

    /// Relay: 4-terminal component with a coil and a contact pair.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "relay"))]
    Relay(Relay),

    /// Photoresistor (LDR): resistance varies logarithmically with light.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "photoresistor"))]
    Photoresistor(Photoresistor),

    /// Potentiometer: 3-terminal voltage divider.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "potentiometer"))]
    Potentiometer(Potentiometer),

    /// Zener diode between two nodes: a silicon diode with SPICE reverse
    /// breakdown, `BV = vz` at `IBV` = 5 mA and 1 Ω of series resistance (the
    /// card `D(IS=1e-14 N=1 RS=1 BV=vz IBV=5m)`), so it holds about `vz` at a
    /// small zener's 5 mA test current and rises 1 V per amp past it.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "zener_diode"))]
    ZenerDiode(ZenerDiode),

    /// Op-amp, output referred to ground.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "op_amp"))]
    OpAmp(OpAmp),

    /// Comparator, output referred to ground: gain 1e5 from `v₊ − v₋` with no
    /// frequency response, its output clamped to `[v_neg, v_pos]`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "comparator"))]
    Comparator(Comparator),

    /// Schottky diode: lower forward voltage (~0.3V) than silicon diode.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "schottky_diode"))]
    SchottkyDiode(SchottkyDiode),

    /// NTC thermistor: resistance varies with temperature (passive, no NR).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "thermistor"))]
    Thermistor(Thermistor),

    /// Photodiode: diode + photocurrent source driven by irradiance.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "photodiode"))]
    Photodiode(Photodiode),

    /// Varactor diode: voltage-dependent junction capacitance.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "varactor"))]
    Varactor(Varactor),

    /// IGBT: MOSFET gate control + BJT output characteristics.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "igbt"))]
    Igbt(Igbt),

    /// Ideal transformer with coupled inductors.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "transformer"))]
    Transformer(Transformer),

    /// Fuse between two nodes.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "fuse"))]
    Fuse(Fuse),

    /// Linear voltage regulator: holds the output at `voltage` above its ground
    /// pin while it has headroom, and draws its output current plus its
    /// quiescent current from the input.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "voltage_regulator"))]
    VoltageRegulator(VoltageRegulator),

    /// Single-pole double-throw switch: `nodes: [common, a, b]`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "switch_spdt"))]
    SwitchSpdt(SwitchSpdt),

    /// Quartz crystal: the Butterworth–Van Dyke model ([`CrystalParams`]).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "crystal"))]
    Crystal(Crystal),

    /// Ferrite bead ([`FerriteBeadParams`]): its DC resistance at DC, lossy and
    /// inductive at high frequency.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "ferrite_bead"))]
    FerriteBead(FerriteBead),

    /// Behavioural source, SPICE's `B n+ n- V={expr}` or `I={expr}`: a voltage
    /// or current set by an [`Expression`] of node voltages, branch currents
    /// and time.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "behavioural"))]
    Behavioural(Behavioural),
}

impl CircuitElement {
    /// Returns a reference to the node array for this component.
    pub fn nodes(&self) -> &[String] { … }

    /// Returns all node names referenced by this component, including control nodes.
    pub fn all_nodes(&self) -> Vec<&String> { … }

    /// Returns the component identifier.
    pub fn id(&self) -> &str { … }

    /// Extra MNA unknowns the element adds after the node voltages: one
    /// branch current for a voltage-type source, two for a transformer
    /// (one per winding), and two for an op-amp with an [`OpAmpModel`] or a
    /// comparator (its output current, then its internal gain-stage voltage).
    pub fn branch_slots(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Mutable [`nodes`](Self::nodes), for renaming nets.
    pub fn nodes_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [String] { … }

    /// Mutable [`id`](Self::id), for renaming.
    pub fn id_mut(&mut self) -> &mut String { … }

    /// The control-net pair of a VCVS or VCCS.
    pub fn control_nodes_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut [String; 2]> { … }

    /// The controlling source id of a CCVS or CCCS.
    pub fn control_source_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut String> { … }
}

/// A circuit: components, nets, and optionally a design hierarchy.
///
/// The top level is a list of [`CircuitElement`]s plus the name of the
/// ground net. Components share a net by referencing the same net-name
/// string. A design can also place [`Block`]s through [`Instance`]s and
/// carry [`Part`] data (reference, symbol, footprint) that the simulator
/// ignores. [`Circuit::flatten`] expands the hierarchy; sindr's analyses
/// do that themselves.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit::new(
///     "0",
///     vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 9.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         }),
///     ],
/// );
/// assert!(circuit.is_flat());
/// ```
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct Circuit {
    /// Top-level components. Order has no semantic meaning.
    pub components: Vec<CircuitElement>,
    /// Name of the reference (0 V) net. Must match the net string used by
    /// at least one component (typically `"0"` or `"gnd"`). It is the same
    /// net inside every block.
    pub ground_node: String,
    /// Top-level block instances.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub instances: Vec<Instance>,
    /// Block definitions, by name.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub blocks: BTreeMap<String, Block>,
    /// Part data for top-level components and instances, keyed by their id.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub parts: BTreeMap<String, Part>,
    /// Nets visible inside every block under the same name (supply rails),
    /// besides ground. Never prefixed when flattening.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub globals: Vec<String>,
}

impl Circuit {
    /// A flat circuit: `components` referencing `ground_node`, no hierarchy.
    pub fn new(ground_node: impl Into<String>, components: Vec<CircuitElement>) -> Self { … }

    /// `true` when there are no instances to expand.
    pub fn is_flat(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Every net named at the top level: component and instance nodes plus
    /// ground, sorted and without repeats. Nets local to block instances
    /// show up only after [`flatten`](Self::flatten).
    pub fn nets(&self) -> Vec<&str> { … }

    /// Count the number of independent voltage sources in the circuit.
    /// Also counts VCVS, CCVS, OpAmp, and Comparator which need branch currents.
    /// Transformer adds 2 branch current unknowns (one per winding).
    pub fn count_voltage_sources(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// Returns true if the circuit contains any nonlinear elements.
    pub fn has_nonlinear_elements(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Returns true if the circuit contains any reactive elements (Capacitor, Inductor, or
    /// Relay with inductance > 0, or Transformer, or BJT/MOSFET/JFET with non-zero parasitic caps,
    /// or a diode whose model stores charge).
    pub fn has_reactive_elements(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Returns true if any source has a time-varying waveform.
    pub fn has_waveform_sources(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Find the branch index for a voltage source by its ID.
    /// Returns None if not found.
    pub fn vsource_branch_index(&self, source_id: &str) -> Option<usize> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/csv.rs`

CSV export of transient, AC and sweep results.

Each result type gets a `to_csv` method that writes one row per point:
the scale (time, frequency, swept value or temperature) first, then a
column per node voltage, `v(<node>)` with nodes in name order, then
for real-valued results a column per component current, `i(<id>)`, in
circuit order. AC writes each node voltage as two columns,
`re(v(<node>))` and `im(v(<node>))`.

Numbers are written so they read back as the same `f64`. A value missing
from a row is an empty field. Names that need it are quoted as RFC 4180
has it. Lines end in `\n`.

```rust
impl TransientData {
    /// The waveforms as CSV: `time` (s), then `v(<node>)` (V) and
    /// `i(<id>)` (A, each component's `current_through`), one row per
    /// timestep. See [CSV export](crate#csv-export) for the layout.
    pub fn to_csv(&self) -> String { … }
}

impl DcSweepResult {
    /// The sweep as CSV: the swept source's value, in a column named after
    /// it, then `v(<node>)` (V) and `i(<id>)` (A), one row per point. See
    /// [CSV export](crate#csv-export) for the layout.
    pub fn to_csv(&self) -> String { … }
}

impl TempSweepResult {
    /// The sweep as CSV: `temperature` (K), then `v(<node>)` (V) and
    /// `i(<id>)` (A), one row per point. See [CSV export](crate#csv-export)
    /// for the layout.
    pub fn to_csv(&self) -> String { … }
}

impl AcResult {
    /// The frequency response as CSV: `frequency` (Hz), then for each node
    /// `re(v(<node>))` and `im(v(<node>))` (V, for the source's
    /// [`ac_magnitude`](crate::ac_analysis::AcConfig::ac_magnitude)), one
    /// row per frequency. Magnitude and phase follow from the two parts.
    /// See [CSV export](crate#csv-export) for the layout.
    pub fn to_csv(&self) -> String { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/datasheet.rs`

Models fitted to datasheet figures.

The figures are [`sindr_devices::datasheet`]'s, re-exported here:
[`DiodeDatasheet`], [`ZenerDatasheet`], [`BjtDatasheet`] and
[`MosfetDatasheet`], each figure a [`DatasheetValue`] with optional
minimum, typical and maximum. The constructors sit on the models they
build:

| Constructor | Fits | Through |
|---|---|---|
| [`DiodeModel::from_datasheet`] | IS (N = 1), or IS and N with a second point | `vf` at `if_` (and `vf2` at `if2`) |
| [`DiodeModel::led_from_datasheet`] | IS (N = 2) or IS and N, and EG for −2 mV/K | `vf` at `if_` (and `vf2` at `if2`) |
| [`DiodeModel::zener_from_datasheet`] | BV of sindr's zener card | `vz` at `iz` |
| [`BjtModel::from_datasheet`] | the element's `bf`, and BR | `hfe`; `vce_sat` at `vce_sat_ic` / `vce_sat_ib` |
| [`MosfetParams::from_datasheet`] | KP and VTO | `vth` at `vth_id`; `rds_on` at `rds_on_vgs` |

Figures are read at 27 °C, the temperature sindr's model values are
given at.

```rust
pub use sindr_devices::datasheet:: { … }

pub use sindr_devices::mosfet::MosfetParams;

impl DiodeModel {
    /// A diode through its datasheet forward voltage: IS so that it
    /// conducts `if_` at `vf`, with N = 1 and no series resistance. With a
    /// second point (`vf2` at `if2`), N is fitted too, so the diode passes
    /// through both. Other parameters are the defaults.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::circuit::DiodeModel;
    /// use sindr::datasheet::DiodeDatasheet;
    ///
    /// // 1N4148: 0.62 V at 1 mA, 0.72 V at 10 mA (typical).
    /// let ds = DiodeDatasheet::new(0.62, 1e-3).with_second_point(0.72, 10e-3);
    /// let m = DiodeModel::from_datasheet(&ds).unwrap();
    /// assert!(m.n > 1.5 && m.n < 2.0);
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DatasheetError`] when `vf` or `if_` is missing or not positive,
    /// when only half of the second point is given, or when `vf2` doesn't
    /// rise with current from `vf`.
    pub fn from_datasheet(ds: &DiodeDatasheet) -> Result<Self, DatasheetError> { … }

    /// An LED through its datasheet forward voltage: as
    /// [`from_datasheet`](Self::from_datasheet), with N = 2 (sindr's LED
    /// presets' emission coefficient) when there is one point, and EG set
    /// so `vf` falls 2 mV/K at `if_`, as sindr's LED colours do. Use it as
    /// a [`CircuitElement::Diode`](crate::CircuitElement::Diode)'s model.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::circuit::DiodeModel;
    /// use sindr::datasheet::DiodeDatasheet;
    ///
    /// // An amber LED: 2.05 V at 20 mA.
    /// let m = DiodeModel::led_from_datasheet(&DiodeDatasheet::new(2.05, 20e-3)).unwrap();
    /// assert_eq!(m.n, 2.0);
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// As [`from_datasheet`](Self::from_datasheet).
    pub fn led_from_datasheet(ds: &DiodeDatasheet) -> Result<Self, DatasheetError> { … }

    /// The zener card sindr stamps a
    /// [`CircuitElement::ZenerDiode`](crate::CircuitElement::ZenerDiode)
    /// as (IBV = 5 mA, RS = 1 Ω), with BV solved so that it carries `iz`
    /// in reverse at `vz`. Its `bv` is the element's `vz`: a datasheet's
    /// Vz at a test current other than 5 mA, or with the 1 Ω drop, shifts
    /// it a little.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::circuit::DiodeModel;
    /// use sindr::datasheet::ZenerDatasheet;
    ///
    /// // 1N4733A: 5.1 V at 49 mA.
    /// let m = DiodeModel::zener_from_datasheet(&ZenerDatasheet::new(5.1, 49e-3)).unwrap();
    /// let vz = m.bv.unwrap();
    /// assert!(vz < 5.1 && vz > 4.9);
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DatasheetError`] when `vz` or `iz` is missing or not positive.
    pub fn zener_from_datasheet(ds: &ZenerDatasheet) -> Result<Self, DatasheetError> { … }
}

impl BjtModel {
    /// A transistor through its datasheet gain and saturation voltage:
    /// the element's `bf` (returned first) is `hfe`, and the model's BR is
    /// solved so that at collector current `vce_sat_ic` and base current
    /// `vce_sat_ib` the collector–emitter voltage is `vce_sat`. Without
    /// Vce(sat), BR stays at 1. Other parameters are the defaults, so the
    /// Early effect stays off and the gain is the same at every current.
    ///
    /// The Ebers–Moll saturation voltage, with NF = NR = 1, is
    /// `VT·ln((1 + (1 + β)/BR) / (1 − β/BF))` with `β = Ic/Ib`, solved here
    /// for BR. sindr's transistor has no collector resistance, so a
    /// datasheet's Vce(sat) (which includes it) gives a low BR.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::circuit::BjtModel;
    /// use sindr::datasheet::{BjtDatasheet, DatasheetValue};
    ///
    /// // 2N3904: hFE 100–300 at 10 mA, Vce(sat) 0.2 V max at 10 mA / 1 mA.
    /// let ds = BjtDatasheet::new(DatasheetValue::range(100.0, 300.0), 10e-3)
    ///     .with_vce_sat(DatasheetValue { max: Some(0.2), ..Default::default() }, 10e-3, 1e-3);
    /// let (bf, model) = BjtModel::from_datasheet(&ds).unwrap();
    /// assert_eq!(bf, 200.0);
    /// assert!(model.br > 0.0);
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DatasheetError`] when `hfe` is missing or not positive, when
    /// Vce(sat) comes without both currents, when `ic / ib` isn't below
    /// `hfe` (the part wouldn't saturate), or when `vce_sat` is too low to
    /// reach at that overdrive.
    pub fn from_datasheet(ds: &BjtDatasheet) -> Result<(f64, Self), DatasheetError> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/dc_sweep.rs`

DC parameter sweep module.

Sweeps a voltage or current source across a range and collects operating
point results at each step ([`dc_sweep`]), or two sources, one inside the
other ([`dc_sweep_nested`]). Used for generating I-V curves, families of
device curves and transfer characteristics.

```rust
/// One operating point of a DC sweep: the sweep value and the full result
/// at that value.
pub struct DcSweepPoint {
    /// The value of the swept source at this point (V, or A for a current
    /// source).
    pub sweep_value: f64,
    /// Full simulation result at this sweep value.
    pub result: SimulationResult,
}

/// Result of a DC sweep — one [`DcSweepPoint`] per swept value.
///
/// Use [`DcSweepResult::node_voltage_curve`] or
/// [`DcSweepResult::component_current_curve`] to extract a plottable curve.
pub struct DcSweepResult {
    /// Component id of the source that was swept.
    pub source_id: String,
    /// Operating points, in sweep order from `start` to `stop`.
    pub points: Vec<DcSweepPoint>,
}

impl DcSweepResult {
    /// `(sweep value in V, node voltage in V)` pairs for a node, one per
    /// point.
    pub fn node_voltage_curve(&self, node: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }

    /// `(sweep value in V, current in A)` pairs for a component, one per
    /// point. The current is its [`ComponentResult::current_through`]: from
    /// `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]` for a two-terminal part (the collector or
    /// drain current for a transistor).
    ///
    /// [`ComponentResult::current_through`]: crate::ComponentResult::current_through
    pub fn component_current_curve(&self, component_id: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }
}

/// One axis of a DC sweep: a source and the values it takes, `num_points`
/// of them evenly spaced from `start` to `stop`, both included.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::dc_sweep::DcSweepAxis;
///
/// // SPICE's `V1 0 1 0.1`: 0, 0.1, …, 1 V, eleven points.
/// let axis = DcSweepAxis::from_step("V1", 0.0, 1.0, 0.1).unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(axis.num_points, 11);
/// assert_eq!(axis.stop, 1.0);
/// ```
pub struct DcSweepAxis {
    /// Id of the [`VoltageSource`](CircuitElement::VoltageSource) or
    /// [`CurrentSource`](CircuitElement::CurrentSource) to sweep.
    pub source_id: String,
    /// First value (V or A).
    pub start: f64,
    /// Last value (V or A).
    pub stop: f64,
    /// Points including both ends. At least 2, or 1 when `start == stop`.
    pub num_points: usize,
}

impl DcSweepAxis {
    /// `num_points` values of `source_id` from `start` to `stop`.
    pub fn new(source_id: impl Into<String>, start: f64, stop: f64, num_points: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// SPICE's `.dc` form: from `start` in steps of `step` for as long as
    /// it doesn't pass `stop`. When `step` doesn't divide the span, the last
    /// value is short of `stop`, as in SPICE. When `start == stop`, or the
    /// first step already passes `stop`, the axis is the one point `start`
    /// (with `stop` set to `start`).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] for a value that isn't finite, a step
    /// that is zero (with `start != stop`) or points away from `stop`, or
    /// more than 10⁷ points.
    pub fn from_step(
        source_id: impl Into<String>,
        start: f64,
        stop: f64,
        step: f64,
    ) -> Result<Self, SimError> { … }
}

/// Sweeps a voltage or current source across a range and solves the
/// operating point at each step.
///
/// Used for generating I-V curves and transfer characteristics. The returned
/// [`DcSweepResult`] has helpers to pull out plottable curves for any node
/// voltage or component current. Each point's Newton–Raphson starts from
/// the previous point's solution, as in SPICE, so a curve follows one
/// branch of a circuit with several operating points.
///
/// # Arguments
///
/// - `circuit` — the base circuit (unchanged; each sweep point gets a
///   modified copy)
/// - `source_id` — id of the [`VoltageSource`](CircuitElement::VoltageSource)
///   or [`CurrentSource`](CircuitElement::CurrentSource) to sweep
/// - `start`, `stop` — sweep endpoints (V or A), inclusive
/// - `num_points` — total points including both endpoints: at least 2, or
///   1 when `start == stop` (one solve at `start`)
///
/// For two sources at once, as SPICE's `.dc V1 … V2 …`, see
/// [`dc_sweep_nested`].
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if `num_points < 2` (1 is allowed when
///   `start == stop`) or above 10⁷, `start` or `stop` is not finite, or
///   `source_id` doesn't match any voltage or current source in the circuit
/// - Any [`SimError`] returned by [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit)
///   at one of the sweep points (propagated immediately)
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, dc_sweep};
/// use sindr::dc_sweep::DcSweepAxis;
/// use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         }),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// // Sweep V1 from 0 V to 10 V in 11 steps.
/// let sweep = dc_sweep(&circuit, &DcSweepAxis::new("V1", 0.0, 10.0, 11)).unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(sweep.points.len(), 11);
///
/// // I = V/R should rise linearly from 0 to 10 mA.
/// let curve = sweep.component_current_curve("R1");
/// assert!((curve.last().unwrap().1 - 0.010).abs() < 1e-9);
/// ```
///
pub fn dc_sweep(circuit: &Circuit, axis: &DcSweepAxis) -> Result<DcSweepResult, SimError> { … }

/// A two-source DC sweep: one [`DcSweepResult`] along the inner source per
/// value of the outer one.
pub struct NestedDcSweepResult {
    /// Component id of the outer (slower) source.
    pub outer_source_id: String,
    /// One curve per outer value, in sweep order.
    pub curves: Vec<NestedDcSweepCurve>,
}

/// One curve of a [`NestedDcSweepResult`]: the inner sweep at one value of
/// the outer source.
pub struct NestedDcSweepCurve {
    /// The outer source's value for this curve (V or A).
    pub outer_value: f64,
    /// The inner sweep at that value.
    pub sweep: DcSweepResult,
}

/// Sweeps two sources, `inner` fastest: for each value of `outer`, a full
/// sweep of `inner`. SPICE's `.dc SRC1 … SRC2 …`, with `SRC1` as `inner`.
/// This is how a family of device curves is drawn: a MOSFET's drain current
/// against V_DS for each V_GS, or a BJT's collector current against V_CE
/// for each base current.
///
/// Each point's Newton–Raphson starts from its neighbour along the inner
/// axis, and each curve's first point from the first point of the curve
/// before.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] for an axis with fewer than 2 points (1 is
/// allowed when its `start` and `stop` are equal), values that aren't
/// finite, a source that isn't a voltage or current source in the circuit,
/// both axes on the same source, or more than 10⁷ points in all; and any
/// error from [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit) at a point.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{dc_sweep_nested, Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::dc_sweep::DcSweepAxis;
/// use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// // Two sources into a 1 kΩ: the current is (V1 + V2) / 1 kΩ.
/// let circuit = Circuit::new(
///     "0",
///     vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["a".into(), "b".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V2".into(),
///             nodes: ["b".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["a".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 1e3,
///         }),
///     ],
/// );
/// let sweep = dc_sweep_nested(
///     &circuit,
///     &DcSweepAxis::new("V1", 0.0, 1.0, 3),
///     &DcSweepAxis::new("V2", 0.0, 2.0, 2),
/// )
/// .unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(sweep.curves.len(), 2);
/// let last = sweep.curves[1].sweep.component_current_curve("R1");
/// assert!((last[2].1 - 3e-3).abs() < 1e-12); // (1 V + 2 V) / 1 kΩ
/// ```
///
pub fn dc_sweep_nested(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    inner: &DcSweepAxis,
    outer: &DcSweepAxis,
) -> Result<NestedDcSweepResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/design.rs`

Design hierarchy and part data: [`Block`], [`Instance`], [`Part`], and
[`Circuit::flatten`].

A [`Block`] is a reusable definition, what `.subckt` is in SPICE. An
[`Instance`] places a block and binds its ports to the caller's nets,
what an `X` line is. Inside a block a net name is a port, ground
([`Circuit::ground_node`]), a global ([`Circuit::globals`]), or local to
each instance.

Flattening names things the way the SPICE parser always has: elements
and local nets get the instance path joined with `.` (`x1.x2.r1`,
`x1.mid`), ports become the caller's net, and ground and globals are
never prefixed.

```
use sindr::{Block, Circuit, CircuitElement, Instance};
use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};

let divider = Block {
    ports: vec!["top".into(), "out".into()],
    components: vec![
        CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["top".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 }),
        CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R2".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], resistance: 1e3 }),
    ],
    ..Block::default()
};
let mut circuit = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 10.0, waveform: None })],
);
circuit.blocks.insert("divider".into(), divider);
