circuit.instances.push(Instance::new("X1", "divider", ["in", "mid"]));

let flat = circuit.flatten().unwrap();
assert!(flat.is_flat());
assert_eq!(flat.components[1].id(), "X1.R1");
assert_eq!(flat.components[2].nodes(), ["mid", "0"]);
```

```rust
/// Separator between instance-path segments in flattened names.
pub const PATH_SEPARATOR: char = '.';

/// A reusable block definition: what `.subckt` is in SPICE.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct Block {
    /// Port nets, in the order [`Instance::nodes`] binds them.
    pub ports: Vec<String>,
    /// Components inside the block, named in the block's own scope.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub components: Vec<CircuitElement>,
    /// Instances of other blocks placed inside this one.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub instances: Vec<Instance>,
    /// Part data for the block's components and instances, keyed by id.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub parts: BTreeMap<String, Part>,
}

/// One placement of a [`Block`]: what an `X` line is in SPICE.
pub struct Instance {
    /// Instance id, unique in its scope (`"X1"`). Prefixes everything inside
    /// it when flattened.
    pub id: String,
    /// Name of the block it places, a key of [`Circuit::blocks`].
    pub block: String,
    /// The caller's nets, bound to [`Block::ports`] by position.
    pub nodes: Vec<String>,
}

impl Instance {
    /// An instance of `block` with `nodes` bound to its ports in order.
    pub fn new<S: Into<String>>(
        id: impl Into<String>,
        block: impl Into<String>,
        nodes: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>,
    ) -> Self { … }
}

/// Part data for a component or instance: what a schematic or BOM needs.
/// The simulator ignores it.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct Part {
    /// Reference designator (`"R1"`). `None` means the element id is the
    /// reference.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub reference: Option<String>,
    /// Display value (`"10k"`, `"BC547"`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub value: Option<String>,
    /// Schematic symbol, in whatever form the design tool uses
    /// (`"Device:R"`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub symbol: Option<String>,
    /// PCB footprint (`"Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric"`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub footprint: Option<String>,
    /// Any other fields: manufacturer, MPN, tolerance, …
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty"))]
    pub fields: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Absolute maximum ratings from the datasheet. `sindr::check_ratings`
    /// compares a simulation against them.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Ratings::is_empty"))]
    pub ratings: Ratings,
    /// How the part sheds heat. When set, the solver heats its junction by
    /// the power it dissipates; see [`Thermal`].
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub thermal: Option<Thermal>,
}

/// A part's thermal path to ambient, for self-heating.
///
/// With it, the part's junction runs at `ambient + P·Rθ` in DC, or follows
/// `Cθ·dT/dt = P − (T − ambient)/Rθ` in a transient, and the solver feeds
/// that temperature back into the device (IS and kT/q for diodes, LEDs and
/// BJTs; the thermistor's resistance). The element's own `temperature`
/// field is then ignored.
///
/// Rθ is [`rth_jc`](Self::rth_jc) + [`rth_ca`](Self::rth_ca) when both are
/// set (a part on a heatsink), otherwise [`rth_ja`](Self::rth_ja).
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct Thermal {
    /// Junction to ambient (K/W), the datasheet's Rθja for the part on its
    /// own.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rth_ja: Option<f64>,
    /// Junction to case (K/W).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rth_jc: Option<f64>,
    /// Case to ambient through what the part is mounted on: interface pad
    /// plus heatsink (K/W).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rth_ca: Option<f64>,
    /// Thermal capacitance (J/K). `None` in a transient means the junction
    /// follows its power with no lag.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub cth: Option<f64>,
    /// Ambient temperature (K). Default 300.15 K (27 °C).
    pub ambient: f64,
}

impl Thermal {
    /// A free-standing part: junction to ambient `rth_ja` (K/W).
    pub fn junction_to_ambient(rth_ja: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A part on a heatsink: junction to case `rth_jc` plus case to ambient
    /// `rth_ca` (K/W).
    pub fn on_heatsink(rth_jc: f64, rth_ca: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The thermal resistance from junction to ambient (K/W) the solver
    /// uses, or `None` when neither path is set.
    pub fn resistance(&self) -> Option<f64> { … }
}

/// Absolute maximum ratings: the datasheet limits a part must never pass.
///
/// Every limit is a magnitude in SI units and `None` when unknown. A rating
/// a part needs but doesn't have is reported as unverified, never as a
/// pass. Which ratings a component needs depends on its kind; see
/// `sindr::ratings`.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct Ratings {
    /// Power dissipation (W).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub power: Option<f64>,
    /// Voltage across the part (V): a capacitor's rated voltage, a
    /// resistor's working voltage.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub voltage: Option<f64>,
    /// Current through the part (A): an inductor's saturation current.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub current: Option<f64>,
    /// Reverse voltage (V): a diode's cathode above its anode, or a
    /// polarised capacitor's `nodes[1]` above its `nodes[0]` (the `+`
    /// terminal). Most electrolytics allow 1 V or less; set it on a
    /// polarised capacitor's part to have reverse bias flagged.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub reverse_voltage: Option<f64>,
    /// Diode forward current, anode to cathode (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub forward_current: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT or IGBT collector–emitter voltage, `|Vce|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vce: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT collector–base voltage, `|Vcb|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vcb: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT emitter–base voltage, `|Veb|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub veb: Option<f64>,
    /// BJT or IGBT collector current, `|Ic|` (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub ic: Option<f64>,
    /// MOSFET or JFET drain–source voltage, `|Vds|` (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vds: Option<f64>,
    /// MOSFET or JFET gate–source voltage, `|Vgs|`; an IGBT's gate–emitter
    /// voltage (V).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vgs: Option<f64>,
    /// MOSFET or JFET drain current, `|Id|` (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub id: Option<f64>,
    /// Maximum junction temperature (K): 423.15 K for a 150 °C part. Checked
    /// against the junction temperature self-heating reports, so it needs
    /// [`Part::thermal`].
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub tj_max: Option<f64>,
}

impl Ratings {
    /// `true` when no limit is set.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { … }
}

/// Why a design can't be flattened.
pub enum DesignError {
    /// An instance names a block that isn't in [`Circuit::blocks`].
    #[error("instance `{instance}` places block `{block}`, which is not defined")]
    UnknownBlock {
        /// Full path of the instance (`x1.x2`).
        instance: String,
        /// The missing block.
        block: String,
    },
    /// An instance binds a different number of nets than the block has ports.
    #[error("instance `{instance}` connects {got} nets, but block `{block}` has {expected} ports")]
    PortCount {
        /// Full path of the instance.
        instance: String,
        /// The block it places.
        block: String,
        /// Ports the block declares.
        expected: usize,
        /// Nets the instance binds.
        got: usize,
    },
    /// A block places itself, directly or through other blocks.
    #[error("instance `{instance}` places block `{block}` inside itself")]
    RecursiveBlock {
        /// Full path of the instance that closes the loop.
        instance: String,
        /// The block that recurses.
        block: String,
    },
    /// Two components or instances in one scope share an id.
    #[error("id `{id}` is used twice in {scope}")]
    DuplicateId {
        /// The repeated id.
        id: String,
        /// `"the top level"` or `"block `name`"`.
        scope: String,
    },
}

impl Circuit {
    /// Expand every instance into a flat circuit with no instances or
    /// blocks. Names follow the module docs; `parts` keys get the same
    /// prefix as their element, and `globals` carry over.
    ///
    /// Top-level components come first, then each instance's expansion in
    /// order, depth-first.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DesignError`] for an unknown block, a port-count mismatch, a
    /// recursive block, or a repeated id in one scope.
    pub fn flatten(&self) -> Result<Circuit, DesignError> { … }

    /// [`flatten`](Self::flatten), borrowing `self` when it is already flat.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// As [`flatten`](Self::flatten).
    pub fn flattened(&self) -> Result<Cow<'_, Circuit>, DesignError> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/ac_stamp.rs`

What an element's small-signal (AC) stamp writes into and reads from.

## `sindr/src/element/battery.rs`

A battery: open-circuit voltage by state of charge behind its internal
resistance and an optional RC pair.

```rust
/// A battery: open-circuit voltage by state of charge behind a series
/// resistance and an optional RC pair ([`BatteryParams`]). At DC it is
/// its open-circuit voltage at `state_of_charge` behind `R0 + R1`. In
/// transient the RC pair charges and the state of charge falls with the
/// charge drawn, reported per step in `state_of_charge`. In AC it is
/// the impedance `R0 + R1‖C1`. `current_through` flows
/// `nodes[0] → nodes[1]` inside the cell, so it is negative while the
/// battery discharges, as for a voltage source.
///
/// [`BatteryParams`]: sindr_devices::battery::BatteryParams
pub struct Battery {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[positive, negative]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// The cell's equivalent circuit.
    pub params: sindr_devices::battery::BatteryParams,
    /// State of charge at the start, 0 (empty) to 1 (full).
    pub state_of_charge: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/behavioural.rs`

A behavioural source: a voltage or current set by an expression.

```rust
/// Behavioural source, SPICE's `B n+ n- V={expr}` or `I={expr}`: a
/// voltage or current set by an [`Expression`] of node voltages,
/// branch currents and time.
///
/// A voltage output holds `V(nodes[0]) − V(nodes[1])` at the
/// expression, and like a [`CircuitElement::VoltageSource`] has a
/// branch current others can read with `i(id)`. A current output
/// drives the expression's value through the source from `nodes[0]` to
/// `nodes[1]`, as a [`CircuitElement::CurrentSource`] does. Newton
/// stamps it with the expression's exact gradient, AC analysis
/// linearises it at the bias point, and `time` reads the transient's
/// time (0 elsewhere).
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{BehaviouralOutput, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::expression::Expression;
/// use sindr::element::Behavioural;
///
/// let multiplier = CircuitElement::Behavioural(Behavioural {
///     id: "b1".into(),
///     nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()],
///     output: BehaviouralOutput::Voltage,
///     expr: Expression::parse("v(a)*v(b)")?,
/// });
/// # Ok::<(), sindr::expression::ExpressionError>(())
/// ```
///
/// [`CircuitElement::VoltageSource`]: crate::CircuitElement::VoltageSource
/// [`CircuitElement::CurrentSource`]: crate::CircuitElement::CurrentSource
pub struct Behavioural {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[n+, n-]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Whether the expression is a voltage or a current.
    pub output: BehaviouralOutput,
    /// The value, in volts or amperes.
    pub expr: Expression,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/bjt.rs`

A bipolar junction transistor: Ebers–Moll with the Early effect.

```rust
/// BJT transistor (3 terminals): Ebers–Moll with Early effect, solved in
/// DC, transient and AC.
pub struct Bjt {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[base, collector, emitter]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3], // [base, collector, emitter]
    /// Polarity (NPN or PNP).
    pub kind: BjtKind,
    /// Forward current gain β (unitless), positive and finite. Default 100.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_bf"))]
    pub bf: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
    /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default = "super::default_junction_temperature")
    )]
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Optional parasitic capacitances (Cbe, Cbc). None = no parasitic caps (default).
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub parasitic_caps: Option<BjtParasiticCaps>,
    /// Ebers–Moll parameters besides `bf` (IS, BR, NF, NR, VAF). `None`
    /// is the built-in transistor, the same as `Some(BjtModel::default())`.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub model: Option<BjtModel>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/capacitor.rs`

/// Capacitor. Open-circuit in DC analysis; charges/discharges in

pub struct Capacitor {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,

    /// Capacitance (F).

## `sindr/src/element/cccs.rs`

A current-controlled current source, SPICE's `F`.

```rust
/// Current-Controlled Current Source: I_out = alpha * I_control.
/// nodes: [out_from, out_to], control_source: id of controlling voltage source
///
/// Like [`CircuitElement::CurrentSource`] and SPICE's `F n+ n-`, a
/// positive `I_out` flows through the source from `nodes[0]` to
/// `nodes[1]`. `I_control` is the controlling source's branch current,
/// positive from its `+` terminal through it to `-`, as in SPICE.
///
/// [`CircuitElement::CurrentSource`]: crate::CircuitElement::CurrentSource
pub struct Cccs {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Output terminals `[out_from, out_to]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Id of the voltage source whose current is sensed.
    pub control_source: String,
    /// Current gain α (A/A): `I_out = alpha * I_control`.
    pub alpha: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/ccvs.rs`

A current-controlled voltage source, SPICE's `H`.

```rust
/// Current-Controlled Voltage Source: V_out = rm * I_control.
/// nodes: [out+, out-], control_source: id of controlling voltage source
pub struct Ccvs {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Output terminals `[out+, out-]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Id of the voltage source whose current is sensed.
    pub control_source: String,
    /// Transresistance rm (Ω): `V_out = rm * I_control`.
    pub rm: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/comparator.rs`

A comparator: the op-amp macromodel with no pole, its output clamped.

```rust
/// Comparator, output referred to ground: gain 1e5 from `v₊ − v₋` with
/// no frequency response, its output clamped to `[v_neg, v_pos]`. It is
/// an op-amp with an [`OpAmpModel`] of that gain and no pole, so it makes
/// the circuit nonlinear (Newton). No hysteresis, no open-collector output.
///
/// [`OpAmpModel`]: crate::circuit::OpAmpModel
pub struct Comparator {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[in_plus, in_minus, out]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3], // [in_plus, in_minus, out]
    /// Output high level (V): the output's upper limit. Default 15.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "super::default_v_pos"))]
    pub v_pos: f64,
    /// Output low level (V): the output's lower limit, below
    /// `v_pos`. Default -15.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "super::default_v_neg"))]
    pub v_neg: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/crystal.rs`

A quartz crystal: the Butterworth–Van Dyke model. The analyses replace

```rust
/// Quartz crystal: the Butterworth–Van Dyke model ([`CrystalParams`]).
/// An open circuit at DC. Its result's `power` is what the motional
/// resistance dissipates: the drive level a datasheet limits.

pub struct Crystal {

    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// The equivalent circuit.
    pub params: CrystalParams,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/current_source.rs`

An independent current source, DC plus an optional waveform.

```rust
/// Independent current source. Current flows through it from `nodes[0]`
/// to `nodes[1]`: drawn out of `nodes[0]` and pushed into `nodes[1]`, as
/// SPICE's `I`.
pub struct CurrentSource {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[from, to]`; current flows from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// DC current (A); also the offset added to any `waveform`.
    pub current: f64,
    /// Optional time-varying waveform added on top of `current`.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub waveform: Option<Waveform>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/fuse.rs`

A fuse: a small resistance, or open once blown.

```rust
/// Fuse between two nodes.
///
/// Intact (blown=false): stamped as 0.001 Ω (1 mΩ) — negligible voltage drop.
/// Blown (blown=true): stamped as 1e9 Ω — effectively open circuit.
///
/// NOTE: Do NOT use 0 Ω — that would cause a singular MNA matrix.
/// `rating` is stored for display only: the fuse never blows by itself;
/// set `blown` to open it. To flag an overcurrent, put
/// [`Ratings::current`](crate::Ratings::current) on its part.
pub struct Fuse {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[a, b]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Current rating (A), for display only: the fuse never blows by itself.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_fuse_rating"))]
    pub rating: f64,
    /// When true, fuse is blown (open circuit). User-settable, like switch.closed.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub blown: bool,
}
```

/// IGBT: MOSFET gate control + BJT output characteristics.

pub struct Igbt {

    /// Terminals `[gate, collector, emitter]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3],

}
```

## `sindr/src/element/inductor.rs`

An inductor, linear or with a saturating core.

```rust
/// Inductor. Stamped as **open-circuit in pure DC analysis** (sindr
/// solves DC as a single algebraic step, not as t→∞ of a transient);
/// integrates `dI/dt` properly during transient. The DC bias point that
/// AC, `.tf` and `.sens` linearise around shorts it instead. `voltage_across` is
/// reported as `nodes[0] − nodes[1]`, `current_through` flows
/// `nodes[0] → nodes[1]`. To get steady-state current, run a
/// transient long enough to settle.
pub struct Inductor {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[a, b]`; `current_through` flows `nodes[0] → nodes[1]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Inductance (H): the small-signal value, at zero current.
    pub inductance: f64,
    /// Core saturation: the inductance falls towards `l_sat` as the
    /// current passes `i_sat`. `None` is a linear inductor.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub saturation: Option<sindr_devices::inductor::InductorSaturation>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/jfet.rs`

A junction FET: the Shockley square law, with optional gate junctions.

```rust
/// N-channel or P-channel JFET (Shockley square-law model).
/// nodes: [gate, drain, source]
pub struct Jfet {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[gate, drain, source]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3], // [gate, drain, source]
    /// Channel type (N-channel or P-channel).
    pub kind: JfetKind,
    /// Drain saturation current at Vgs=0 (A). Typical: 1–20 mA.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_jfet_idss"))]
    pub idss: f64,
    /// Pinch-off voltage (V, negative for N-channel, e.g. -2.0).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_jfet_vp"))]
    pub vp: f64,
    /// Optional gate capacitances (CGS, CGD as SPICE junctions). None =
    /// no capacitance (default).
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub parasitic_caps: Option<JfetParasiticCaps>,
}
```

/// LED. `nodes: [anode, cathode]`. Forward voltage drop depends on
/// `color` (e.g. `"red"` ≈ 1.8 V, `"blue"` ≈ 3.2 V).
pub struct Led {

    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Emission colour, any case: `"red"`, `"orange"`, `"amber"`,
    /// `"yellow"`, `"green"`, `"blue"` or `"white"`

    /// voltage drop. Any other name is red.

## `sindr/src/element/mod.rs`

The circuit elements: one struct per [`CircuitElement`] variant.

[`CircuitElement`] wraps each of them, so a resistor is
`CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { .. })`. The structs carry the
element's fields and serialise as the enum's variant did, inside the
enum's `type`-tagged object.

[`CircuitElement`]: crate::CircuitElement

```rust
pub use battery::Battery;

pub use behavioural::Behavioural;

pub use bjt::Bjt;

pub use capacitor::Capacitor;

pub use cccs::Cccs;

pub use ccvs::Ccvs;

pub use comparator::Comparator;

pub use crystal::Crystal;

pub use current_source::CurrentSource;

pub use diode::Diode;

pub use ferrite_bead::FerriteBead;

pub use fuse::Fuse;

pub use igbt::Igbt;

pub use inductor::Inductor;

pub use jfet::Jfet;

pub use led::Led;

pub use mosfet::Mosfet;

pub use op_amp::OpAmp;

pub use photodiode::Photodiode;

pub use photoresistor::Photoresistor;

pub use potentiometer::Potentiometer;

pub use pushbutton::Pushbutton;

pub use relay::Relay;

pub use resistor::Resistor;

pub use schottky_diode::SchottkyDiode;

pub use switch::Switch;

pub use switch_spdt::SwitchSpdt;

pub use thermistor::Thermistor;

pub use transformer::Transformer;

pub use varactor::Varactor;

pub use vccs::Vccs;

pub use vcvs::Vcvs;

pub use voltage_regulator::VoltageRegulator;

pub use voltage_source::VoltageSource;

pub use zener_diode::ZenerDiode;
```

## `sindr/src/element/mosfet.rs`

A MOSFET, its body tied to its source, with an optional body diode.

```rust
/// MOSFET transistor (3 terminals: gate, drain, source; the body is tied
/// to the source).
pub struct Mosfet {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[gate, drain, source]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3], // [gate, drain, source]
    /// Channel type (NMOS or PMOS).
    pub kind: MosfetKind,
    /// Model parameters (threshold voltage, transconductance, etc.).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub params: MosfetParams,
    /// Optional parasitic capacitances (Cgs, Cgd). None = no parasitic caps (default).
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub parasitic_caps: Option<MosfetParasiticCaps>,
    /// A power MOSFET's body diode, as a SPICE diode card: anode at the
    /// source and cathode at the drain for NMOS, the other way round for
    /// PMOS. It conducts when the drain is pulled past the source, as
    /// in a bridge's freewheeling interval. Every analysis solves it as
    /// a [`CircuitElement::Diode`] with id `<id>.body`, which is where
    /// its current is reported. `None` (default) is no body diode.
    ///
    /// [`CircuitElement::Diode`]: crate::CircuitElement::Diode
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub body_diode: Option<DiodeModel>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/op_amp.rs`

An op-amp: a near-ideal VCVS, or a macromodel with an [`OpAmpModel`].

[`OpAmpModel`]: crate::circuit::OpAmpModel

```rust
/// Op-amp, output referred to ground.
///
/// With `model: None` it is the near-ideal VCVS sindr has always used:
/// gain 1e5, no frequency response, no output resistance, and `v_pos` /
/// `v_neg` not enforced. With an [`OpAmpModel`] it gets a dominant pole
/// from the gain-bandwidth product, slew-rate limiting, output
/// resistance, input offset and bias current, and an output clamped to
/// `v_pos`/`v_neg`.
pub struct OpAmp {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[in_plus, in_minus, out]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3], // [in_plus, in_minus, out]
    /// Positive supply rail (V): the output's upper limit with a
    /// `model`. Default 15.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "super::default_v_pos"))]
    pub v_pos: f64,
    /// Negative supply rail (V): the output's lower limit with a
    /// `model`. Default -15.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "super::default_v_neg"))]
    pub v_neg: f64,
    /// Macromodel parameters; `None` for the near-ideal VCVS.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub model: Option<OpAmpModel>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/photodiode.rs`

A photodiode: a junction diode in parallel with a photocurrent.

```rust
/// Photodiode: diode + photocurrent source driven by irradiance.
/// nodes: [anode, cathode]
pub struct Photodiode {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Incident irradiance in W (optical power, not W/m²).
    /// 0.0 = dark, 0.1 = ~50mA photocurrent with default responsivity.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub irradiance: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
    /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default = "super::default_junction_temperature")
    )]
    pub temperature: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/relay.rs`

A relay: a coil whose voltage opens or closes a contact pair.

```rust
/// Relay: 4-terminal component with a coil and a contact pair.
/// nodes: [coil+, coil-, contact1, contact2]
/// Contact closes when |V_coil| >= pickup_voltage. AC and `.tf` take the
/// contact as open or closed at the DC bias point.
pub struct Relay {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[coil+, coil-, contact1, contact2]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 4],
    /// Coil resistance (Ω). Default 500.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_relay_coil_resistance"))]
    pub coil_resistance: f64,
    /// Coil voltage magnitude at which the contact closes (V).
    pub pickup_voltage: f64,
    /// Coil inductance in Henry, in series with `coil_resistance` in
    /// transient. 0.0 = purely resistive coil.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub inductance: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/schottky_diode.rs`

A Schottky diode: a junction diode with a low forward drop.

```rust
/// Schottky diode: lower forward voltage (~0.3V) than silicon diode.
/// nodes: [anode, cathode]
pub struct SchottkyDiode {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
    /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default = "super::default_junction_temperature")
    )]
    pub temperature: f64,
}
```

/// Single-pole double-throw switch: `nodes: [common, a, b]`. The common
/// terminal connects to `a` or `b` as [`Switch`] does
/// (0.01 Ω), and the other throw is open (1 GΩ). Its result is the path
/// in use: `voltage_across` from common to the selected throw and the

## `sindr/src/element/transformer.rs`

A transformer: two coupled windings, linear or with a saturating core.

```rust
/// Ideal transformer with coupled inductors.
///
/// nodes: [p1, q1, p2, q2] where:
///   - [p1, q1]: primary winding (+ and - terminals)
///   - [p2, q2]: secondary winding (+ and - terminals)
///
/// Coupling: M = k * sqrt(L1 * L2) where k ∈ [0, 1).
/// k=1 is ideal (no leakage), but mathematically singular — use k<=0.999.
///
/// In DC analysis: both windings stamped as short circuits; the bias point
/// for AC, `.tf` and `.sens` shorts each with a 0 V source.
/// In AC: the coupled pair `V = jω·[[L1, M], [M, L2]]·I`.
/// In transient: coupled-inductor companion with 2 branch current unknowns,
/// each winding `V = L·dI/dt` plus the mutual term. The windings start at
/// 0 A; an initial current on a transformer is rejected.
///
/// With `saturation`, the core is modelled as a leakage inductance
/// `(1 − k)·L` on each winding and a magnetising inductance `k·L1` on the
/// primary carrying the shared core flux, driven by the magnetising
/// current `i1 + n·i2` (n = √(L2/L1), the turns ratio). That branch
/// saturates as a saturating [`Inductor`] does, so a
/// winding driven past its volt-second rating, or with a DC bias, draws
/// a magnetising current that climbs once the core saturates. Without
/// it the pair is linear and identical to the coupled inductors above.
///
/// [`Inductor`]: super::Inductor
pub struct Transformer {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[p1, q1, p2, q2]`: primary `[p1, q1]`, secondary `[p2, q2]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 4], // [p1, q1, p2, q2]
    /// Primary winding inductance (H).
    pub l1: f64, // Primary inductance (H)
    /// Secondary winding inductance (H).
    pub l2: f64, // Secondary inductance (H)
    /// Coupling coefficient (unitless) in `[0, 0.999]`. Default 0.999 (near-ideal).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_coupling"))]
    pub k: f64, // Coupling coefficient [0, 0.999]. Default 0.999 (near-ideal).
    /// Core saturation, on the magnetising branch: `i_sat` is the
    /// magnetising current referred to the primary, and `l_sat` at
    /// most the magnetising inductance `k·l1`. `None` is a linear core.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub saturation: Option<sindr_devices::inductor::InductorSaturation>,
}
```

/// Voltage-Controlled Current Source: I_out = gm * V_control.
/// nodes: [out_from, out_to], control_nodes: [ctrl+, ctrl-]
///
/// Like [`CircuitElement::CurrentSource`] and SPICE's `G n+ n-`, a

## `sindr/src/element/voltage_regulator.rs`

A linear voltage regulator with dropout, quiescent current and a
current limit.

```rust
/// Linear voltage regulator: holds the output at `voltage` above its
/// ground pin while it has headroom, and draws its output current plus
/// its quiescent current from the input.
///
/// Piecewise linear (see `sindr_devices::regulator`): out of headroom
/// the output follows the input down by the dropout; past the current
/// limit it holds the current. `model` sets dropout, quiescent current,
/// current limit and line and load regulation;
/// `RegulatorParams::lm7805()` and `::ams1117()` are datasheet presets.
/// Its result is the pass element: `Vin − Vout`, the output current,
/// and the power it dissipates.
///
/// `nodes: [input, output, gnd]`
pub struct VoltageRegulator {
    /// Unique component identifier.
    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[input, output, gnd]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 3], // [input, output, gnd]
    /// Regulated output voltage (V) from the ground pin. E.g. 5.0 for a
    /// 7805, or −5.0 for a 7905, whose input sits below ground and whose
    /// output current flows in at the output pin.
    pub voltage: f64,
    /// Dropout, quiescent current, limit and regulation. `None` is an
    /// ideal regulator that still can't put out more than it gets in.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub model: Option<sindr_devices::regulator::RegulatorParams>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/element/zener_diode.rs`

A zener diode: a silicon diode with reverse breakdown at `vz`.

```rust
/// Zener diode between two nodes: a silicon diode with SPICE reverse
/// breakdown, `BV = vz` at `IBV` = 5 mA and 1 Ω of series resistance
/// (the card `D(IS=1e-14 N=1 RS=1 BV=vz IBV=5m)`), so it holds about
/// `vz` at a small zener's 5 mA test current and rises 1 V per amp past
/// it. For another knee, use a [`CircuitElement::Diode`] with a
/// [`DiodeModel`] setting `bv` and `ibv`.
/// nodes: [anode, cathode]
///
/// [`CircuitElement::Diode`]: crate::CircuitElement::Diode
/// [`DiodeModel`]: crate::circuit::DiodeModel
pub struct ZenerDiode {

    pub id: String,
    /// Terminals `[anode, cathode]`.
    pub nodes: [String; 2],
    /// Reverse breakdown (Zener) voltage (V).
    pub vz: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K), positive and finite. Default 300.15 K.
    /// Sets IS (SPICE temperature scaling) and the thermal voltage kT/q.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default = "super::default_junction_temperature")
    )]
    pub temperature: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/error.rs`

Error type returned by the solver.

```rust
/// Anything that can go wrong while validating or solving a circuit.
///
/// Returned by [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit),
/// [`solve_transient`](crate::solve_transient),
/// [`solve_ac`](crate::ac_analysis::solve_ac), [`solve_tf`](crate::solve_tf),
/// [`solve_sensitivity`](crate::solve_sensitivity),
/// [`dc_sweep`](fn@crate::dc_sweep) and
/// [`temperature_sweep`](crate::temperature_sweep).
///
/// Variants split into four groups:
///
/// - **Design errors** ([`Design`](Self::Design)) — the hierarchy can't be
///   flattened.
/// - **Topology / validation errors** ([`NoGround`](Self::NoGround),
///   [`DisconnectedNodes`](Self::DisconnectedNodes),
///   [`FloatingNode`](Self::FloatingNode)) — caught before solving.
/// - **Numerical errors** ([`SingularMatrix`](Self::SingularMatrix),
///   [`InvalidSolution`](Self::InvalidSolution),
///   [`ConvergenceFailed`](Self::ConvergenceFailed)) — the matrix has no
///   unique solution or Newton–Raphson failed to converge.
/// - **Configuration errors** ([`InvalidComponent`](Self::InvalidComponent),
///   [`InvalidResistance`](Self::InvalidResistance)) — a component value or
///   analysis setting that the solver explicitly rejects.
pub enum SimError {
    /// The design hierarchy can't be flattened: an unknown block, a
    /// port-count mismatch, a recursive block or a repeated id.
    #[error("{0}")]
    Design(#[from] crate::DesignError),

    /// No ground node was defined. Every circuit needs a reference node.
    #[error(
        "No ground node defined in circuit. Every circuit needs a ground (reference) node \
         — try connecting a component terminal to node \"0\"."
    )]
    NoGround,

    /// One or more nodes have no path to the rest of the circuit.
    #[error(
        "These nodes are not connected to the rest of the circuit: {0:?}. \
         Make sure every node has a path to ground through components."
    )]
    DisconnectedNodes(Vec<String>),

    /// A node has fewer than two component terminals attached and so can't
    /// carry current.
    #[error(
        "Node \"{0}\" has fewer than 2 connections and cannot carry current. \
         Connect it to at least 2 components."
    )]
    FloatingNode(String),

    /// The MNA matrix is singular — typically a voltage-source loop or a
    /// subcircuit that's not tied to ground.
    #[error(
        "Circuit matrix is singular — the circuit has no unique solution. \
         Common causes: voltage sources in a loop, or a subcircuit disconnected from ground."
    )]
    SingularMatrix,

    /// The solver produced NaN or infinity, usually due to component values
    /// spanning an extreme dynamic range.
    #[error(
        "Solver produced invalid values (NaN or Infinity). This usually means component \
         values span an extreme range. Try checking for very small or very large values."
    )]
    InvalidSolution,

    /// A component definition or analysis setting is malformed: a device
    /// `temperature` or BJT `bf` that isn't positive and finite, an id that
    /// names no suitable source or component, a non-finite or out-of-range
    /// sweep or transient setting, a transient of more than 10⁷ steps or a
    /// sweep of more than 10⁷ points, a bad initial condition. Carries a
    /// human-readable description naming the offending id or field.
    #[error("Invalid component: {0}")]
    InvalidComponent(String),

    /// A resistor's resistance is zero, negative or not finite.
    #[error(
        "Resistor \"{0}\" has a zero, negative or non-finite resistance, which is not physically meaningful."
    )]
    InvalidResistance(String),

    /// Newton–Raphson exhausted its iteration budget without converging,
    /// in DC after the gmin- and source-stepping fallbacks failed too, or in
    /// transient after halving the step down to its floor.
    ///
    /// Says where the circuit is stuck: the node whose voltage was still
    /// moving most on the last iteration, the components on that node, and
    /// the point of the analysis that failed. The message names them, so a
    /// designer or an agent knows which part to look at.
    ///
    /// A final step near the convergence tolerance suggests slow
    /// convergence: try initial conditions (`.nodeset`) or scaling values. A
    /// large one usually means there's no valid operating point there, such
    /// as a nonlinear element with no DC path to ground.
    #[error(
        "Newton-Raphson failed to converge at {at} after {iterations} iterations{}. \
         The circuit may have no valid operating point there.",
        stuck(.node, .components, .max_step_volts)
    )]
    ConvergenceFailed {
        /// Number of Newton iterations executed before giving up.
        iterations: usize,
        /// Largest per-node Newton step on the final iteration (V): the max
        /// over nodes of `|V_new − V_prev|`. A Newton step, not a KCL
        /// residual.
        max_step_volts: f64,
        /// The node that took that step: where the circuit won't settle.
        /// `None` only when no iteration ran.
        node: Option<String>,
        /// Ids of the components with a terminal on [`node`](Self::ConvergenceFailed::node),
        /// in circuit order, with blocks flattened (`X1.R2`).
        components: Vec<String>,
        /// Where in the analysis it failed.
        at: SolvePoint,
    },

    /// Self-heating has no stable balance: a part's dissipation heats its
    /// junction, which raises its current, faster than its thermal path can
    /// carry the heat away. The real part would be destroyed.
    #[error(
        "thermal runaway in `{part}`: its junction passed {temperature:.0} K with no stable \
         operating point. Lower its dissipation, add emitter degeneration, or give it a \
         lower thermal resistance (heatsink)."
    )]
    ThermalRunaway {
        /// The part that ran away (the hottest one whose temperature feeds
        /// back into its model).
        part: String,
        /// Its junction temperature when the solve gave up (K).
        temperature: f64,
    },

    /// A transient's step stayed far below `tstep` (three decades or more)
    /// for thousands of steps in a row, the solution still changing too
    /// fast to follow. A node driven with no DC path to ground (a current
    /// source into a capacitor or an open end) ramps without limit like
    /// this. SPICE's "timestep too small". A run whose step settles a
    /// little higher stops this way too once it has taken
    /// [`max_transient_steps`](crate::SolverOptions::max_transient_steps)
    /// steps short of `tstop`.
    #[error(
        "time step too small at t = {time:.3e} s: the step stayed near {step:.1e} s and \
         the solution still changes too fast to follow. Check for a node driven with no \
         DC path to ground, such as a current source into a capacitor or an open end."
    )]
    TimestepTooSmall {
        /// Simulated time when the run stopped (s).
        time: f64,
        /// The last step taken (s).
        step: f64,
    },

    /// A progress hook asked the run to stop
    /// ([`solve_transient_with_progress`](crate::solve_transient_with_progress)).
    #[error("cancelled at t = {time:.3e} s")]
    Cancelled {
        /// Simulated time of the last accepted step (s).
        time: f64,
    },

    /// A [`Measurement`](crate::measure::Measurement) couldn't be taken on
    /// a result: an unknown node or component, a window outside the
    /// result, or a level the signal never crosses.
    #[error("measurement `{name}`: {reason}")]
    Measurement {
        /// The measurement's name.
        name: String,
        /// Why it couldn't be taken.
        reason: String,
    },

    /// A [`Fourier`](crate::fourier::Fourier) analysis or
    /// [`Fft`](crate::fourier::Fft) couldn't be taken: no transient, an
    /// unknown signal, a run shorter than one period, or settings it can't
    /// use.
    #[error("spectrum: {reason}")]
    Spectrum {
        /// Why it couldn't be taken.
        reason: String,
    },

    /// A behavioural source's expression isn't finite (it overflowed, or
    /// left its domain) at the voltages and currents it read.
    ///
    /// During a solve this is a failed iterate, not a final answer: Newton
    /// shortens the step, and gmin and source stepping, or a shorter
    /// transient step, are tried before this is returned.
    #[error("`{component}`'s expression `{expression}` isn't finite at {inputs}")]
    NotFinite {
        /// The behavioural source.
        component: String,
        /// Its expression.
        expression: String,
        /// What it read, as `v(a) = 20, time = 0`.
        inputs: String,
    },
}

/// Where in an analysis a solve failed, carried by
/// [`SimError::ConvergenceFailed`].
pub enum SolvePoint {
    /// The DC operating point, including one AC, `.tf`, `.sens` or `.noise`
    /// linearise around and the one a transient starts from.
    OperatingPoint,
    /// A DC sweep point: `source` set to `value` (V or A).
    DcSweep {
        /// The swept source's id.
        source: String,
        /// Its value at the failing point.
        value: f64,
    },
    /// A temperature sweep point (K).
    Temperature {
        /// The device temperature at the failing point (K).
        kelvin: f64,
    },
    /// A transient step to `time` (s), after the step was halved to its
    /// floor.
    Transient {
        /// The time the failing step was solving for (s).
        time: f64,
    },
}
```

## `sindr/src/examples.rs`

Built-in example circuits.

Each circuit is exposed as a named function returning `Circuit` directly,
e.g. `sindr::examples::voltage_divider()`. The dynamic metadata-bearing list
(`get_examples()` returning `Vec<ExampleCircuit>`) is feature-gated behind
`examples` and intended for HTTP/UI consumers that need ids and descriptions.

```rust
/// Two resistors in series across a voltage source. Node `n2` shows the divided voltage.
pub fn voltage_divider() -> Circuit { … }

/// Two resistors in parallel. Current splits inversely proportional to resistance.
pub fn current_divider() -> Circuit { … }

/// Three resistors in series. Voltage drops proportional to resistance.
pub fn series_resistors() -> Circuit { … }

/// A 9 V supply drives a red LED through a 330 Ω current-limiting resistor.
pub fn led_circuit() -> Circuit { … }

/// 5 V source through a 1 A fuse and 100 Ω load. Toggle `blown` for the open-fuse case.
pub fn fuse_protection() -> Circuit { … }

/// Voltage source and current source in the same circuit, demonstrating superposition.
pub fn mixed_sources() -> Circuit { … }

/// Classic measurement bridge with four resistors. Bridge voltage is zero when balanced.
pub fn wheatstone_bridge() -> Circuit { … }

/// 5 V amplitude, 1 kHz sinusoidal source driving a 1 kΩ load.
pub fn sine_wave_source() -> Circuit { … }

/// First-order RC filter with -3 dB cutoff at ~159 Hz (R=1 kΩ, C=1 µF).
pub fn rc_lowpass_filter() -> Circuit { … }

/// 2:1 step-down transformer (L1=1 H, L2=0.25 H, k=0.999). 10 V primary → ~5 V on 100 Ω secondary.
pub fn transformer_stepdown() -> Circuit { … }

/// Classic NPN BJT amplifier. Base resistor sets bias, collector resistor sets gain.
pub fn npn_common_emitter() -> Circuit { … }

/// BJT driven into saturation to switch a load. Low base resistor ensures full turn-on.
pub fn npn_switch() -> Circuit { … }

    /// Returns all built-in example circuits with their display metadata.
    /// Order matches the difficulty grouping in the frontend.
    pub fn get_examples() -> Vec<ExampleCircuit> { … }

pub use meta::{get_examples, ExampleCircuit};
```

## `sindr/src/expression.rs`

Behavioural expressions: the right-hand side of SPICE's `B` sources,
such as `v(a)*v(b)` or `1m*tanh(v(in,ref)/26m)`.

An [`Expression`] is parsed from text once and evaluated at every
Newton iteration, together with its exact gradient by forward-mode
automatic differentiation, so a
[`Behavioural`](crate::CircuitElement::Behavioural) source stamps the true
Jacobian rather than a finite-difference guess.

### Syntax

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `v(n)`, `v(n,m)` | node voltage, or the voltage of `n` over `m` (V) |
| `i(src)` | current through a voltage-defined element (A): an independent or behavioural voltage source, VCVS, CCVS, op-amp output or regulator |
| `time` | simulation time (s); 0 outside a transient |
| `pi` | π |
| `2.5`, `1e-3`, `4.7k`, `10meg`, `26m` | numbers, with SPICE's suffixes (`t g meg k m u n p f mil`) |
| `+ - * / ^` (or `**`) | arithmetic; `^` binds tightest and to the right, so `-2^2` is −4 |
| `== != < <= > >=`, `&& \|\| !` | comparisons and logic, 1 for true and 0 for false |
| `c ? a : b` | `a` where `c` is non-zero, otherwise `b` |

Functions: `abs sqrt exp ln log log10 sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh
cosh tanh` (one argument; `log` is natural, as in ngspice), `atan2 pow
pwr min max` (two), `limit(x, lo, hi)`, and the step-like `u` (1 for
`x > 0`), `uramp` (`max(x, 0)`), `sgn`, `floor`, `ceil`. Function and
variable names ignore case; node and source names are kept as written.

Steps, comparisons and the branches of `?:` have zero derivative, so
Newton sees each smooth piece on its own: keep transitions smooth (with
`tanh`, say) where convergence matters.

```
use sindr::expression::Expression;

let e = Expression::parse("v(a) * v(b) + 2m")?;
assert_eq!(e.to_string(), "v(a)*v(b)+0.002");
assert_eq!(e.evaluate(&[3.0, 4.0]), 12.002);
```

```rust
/// A parsed behavioural expression. See the [module docs](self) for the
/// syntax.
///
/// It prints as canonical text, which parses back to an equal
/// expression; with the `serde` feature it is serialised as that text.
pub struct Expression {
    root: Node,
    variables: Vec<Variable>,
}

/// A quantity an [`Expression`] reads from the circuit.
pub enum Variable {
    /// `v(node)` or `v(node, reference)`: in volts.
    Voltage {
        /// The node.
        node: String,
        /// The node it is measured against; ground when `None`.
        reference: Option<String>,
    },
    /// `i(source)`: the branch current of a voltage-defined element, in
    /// amperes, flowing into its first node.
    Current {
        /// The element's id.
        source: String,
    },
    /// `time`, in seconds.
    Time,
}

/// Why text isn't an [`Expression`].
pub struct ExpressionError {
    /// What is wrong.
    pub message: String,
    /// Byte offset into `text` where it was noticed.
    pub position: usize,
    /// The text that was parsed.
    pub text: String,
}

impl Expression {
    /// Parses `text`. See the [module docs](self) for the syntax.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`ExpressionError`] for text that isn't an expression, an unknown
    /// function or name, or a function given the wrong number of arguments.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Expression, ExpressionError> { … }

    /// The quantities the expression reads, in the order
    /// [`evaluate`](Self::evaluate) takes their values.
    pub fn variables(&self) -> &[Variable] { … }

    /// The expression's value with each of [`variables`](Self::variables)
    /// at the matching entry of `values`. A missing value reads as 0.
    pub fn evaluate(&self, values: &[f64]) -> f64 { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/fourier.rs`

Spectral analysis of transient results: SPICE `.four` harmonics and THD,
and a windowed FFT.

Both read a [`Signal`] (a node voltage, a voltage between two nodes or a
component's current) from a [`SimulationResult`] that holds a transient,
or work on a `(time, value)` trace you already have.

### Fourier analysis (`.four`)

[`Fourier`] follows ngspice's `.four` and `fourier` command, so its
numbers can be checked against ngspice's:

1. Take the last period of the run, `[tstop − 1/f0, tstop]`.
2. Resample it linearly onto [`grid_points`](Fourier::grid_points)
   points (200 by default) at `t_i = tstop − 1/f0 + i/(f0·N)`,
   `i = 0 … N−1`.
3. For harmonic `k`, sum `S = Σ x_i·sin(2πki/N)` and
   `C = Σ x_i·cos(2πki/N)`. The magnitude is `2/N·√(S² + C²)` and the
   phase is `atan2(C, S)` in degrees, measured against a sine that
   starts with the period. The DC term is the mean.
4. THD is `100·√(Σ_{k≥2} mag_k²) / mag_1`, over the harmonics asked for
   (9 above DC by default, ngspice's 10 frequencies).

The run must reach at least one period, and should have settled by its
last period: start-up transients leak into every harmonic. Steps of at
most `1/(f0·N)` keep the linear resample faithful; ngspice's
`.tran tstep` is usually set to that.

### FFT

[`Fft`] resamples a span of the trace onto a uniform grid and takes a
radix-2 FFT, after multiplying by a [`Window`]:

- **Resampling:** [`points`](Fft::points) samples (a power of two; by
  default the smallest power of two at least the number of steps in the
  span) at `t_i = from + i·(to − from)/N`, `i = 0 … N−1`, linearly
  interpolated between steps. The sample at `to` is left out, so a span
  of whole periods repeats seamlessly. The sample rate is
  `N/(to − from)` and the bins are `1/(to − from)` apart.
- **Window:** periodic (DFT-even) forms, `w_i` for `i = 0 … N−1` with
  period `N`; Hann by default. See [`Window`] for each one's
  coefficients and leakage.
- **Scaling:** each bin's [`magnitude`](SpectrumBin::magnitude) is the
  peak amplitude of the sine it stands for: `2·|X_k| / Σw` (`|X_k| / Σw`
  for DC and the Nyquist bin), so a tone centred on a bin reads its own
  amplitude whatever the window. Phases are in degrees against a sine
  that starts at `from`, as `.four`'s are.

A tone centred on bin `k` spreads over bins `k − h … k + h` and leaves
the rest at rounding level, with `h` the window's
[`half_width`](Window::half_width): 0 for rectangular, 1 for Hann and
Hamming, 2 for Blackman, 4 for flat-top. A tone between bins leaks
further, by the window's side lobes.

```
use sindr::fourier::{Fft, Fourier, Window};
use sindr::measure::Signal;
use sindr::{solve_transient, Circuit, CircuitElement, TransientConfig, Waveform};
use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};

// A 1 kHz, 1 V sine across a divider: half of it at `out`.
let circuit = Circuit::new("0", vec![
    CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
        id: "V1".into(),
        nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
        voltage: 0.0,
        waveform: Some(Waveform::Sine { amplitude: 1.0, frequency: 1e3, offset: 0.0, phase: 0.0 }),
    }),
    CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 }),
    CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R2".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], resistance: 1e3 }),
]);
let result = solve_transient(&circuit, &TransientConfig::new(2e-3, 5e-6))?;

let four = Fourier::new(1e3).on(&result, &Signal::v("out"))?;
assert!((four.harmonics[0].magnitude - 0.5).abs() < 1e-3);
assert!(four.thd_percent < 0.1);

let spectrum = Fft::new().window(Window::Hann).on(&result, &Signal::v("out"))?;
let peak = spectrum.peak().unwrap();
assert!((peak.frequency - 1e3).abs() < 1.0);
```

```rust
/// A Fourier analysis at a fundamental frequency: SPICE's `.four`. See the
/// [module docs](self) for the algorithm.
pub struct Fourier {
    /// The fundamental frequency (Hz).
    pub fundamental: f64,
    /// How many harmonics above DC to report, the fundamental included.
    /// 9 by default: ngspice's 10 frequencies, DC counted.
    pub harmonics: usize,
    /// Points the last period is resampled onto. 200 by default, as
    /// ngspice's.
    pub grid_points: usize,
}

impl Fourier {
    /// A Fourier analysis at `fundamental` Hz, with ngspice's defaults: 9
    /// harmonics above DC on a 200-point grid.
    pub fn new(fundamental: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Report `n` harmonics above DC, the fundamental included.
    pub fn harmonics(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// Resample the last period onto `n` points.
    pub fn grid_points(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// The harmonics of `signal` in a transient `result`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::Spectrum`] when the result has no transient, the signal
    /// isn't in it, the run is shorter than one period, or the settings
    /// can't be used (see [`Fourier::of`]).
    pub fn on(
        &self,
        result: &SimulationResult,
        signal: &Signal,
    ) -> Result<FourierResult, SimError> { … }

    /// The harmonics of a `(time in s, value)` trace in ascending time,
    /// such as [`TransientData::node_voltage_curve`](crate::TransientData::node_voltage_curve).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::Spectrum`] when the fundamental isn't a positive finite
    /// frequency, there are no harmonics or fewer grid points than twice
    /// the highest harmonic, the trace is shorter than one period, or it
    /// isn't finite and in ascending time.
    pub fn of(&self, trace: &[(f64, f64)]) -> Result<FourierResult, SimError> { … }
}

/// A Fourier analysis's answer: the DC term, each harmonic and the THD.
pub struct FourierResult {
    /// The fundamental frequency (Hz).
    pub fundamental: f64,
    /// The mean over the last period: harmonic 0 in ngspice's table.
    pub dc: f64,
    /// Harmonics 1 (the fundamental) up, in order.
    pub harmonics: Vec<Harmonic>,
    /// Total harmonic distortion (%): the harmonics above the fundamental,
    /// root-sum-squared, over the fundamental. NaN when the fundamental's
    /// magnitude is zero.
    pub thd_percent: f64,
    /// Points the last period was resampled onto.
    pub grid_points: usize,
}

impl FourierResult {
    /// Harmonic `k` (1 is the fundamental), if it was asked for.
    pub fn harmonic(&self, k: usize) -> Option<&Harmonic> { … }
}

/// One harmonic of a [`FourierResult`].
pub struct Harmonic {
    /// Which harmonic: 1 is the fundamental.
    pub number: usize,
    /// Its frequency (Hz).
    pub frequency: f64,
    /// Its peak amplitude, in the signal's unit.
    pub magnitude: f64,
    /// Its phase (degrees) against a sine starting with the period.
    pub phase: f64,
    /// Its magnitude over the fundamental's.
    pub normalized_magnitude: f64,
    /// Its phase less the fundamental's (degrees).
    pub normalized_phase: f64,
}

/// The window an [`Fft`] multiplies its samples by, in periodic (DFT-even)
/// form: `w_i = Σ_m (−1)^m·a_m·cos(2πmi/N)` for `i = 0 … N−1`.
pub enum Window {
    /// No window (`a = 1`): the narrowest peak and the most leakage, −13 dB
    /// side lobes. Exact for a span of whole periods.
    Rectangular,
    /// Hann (`a = 0.5, 0.5`): side lobes from −31 dB, falling fast. The
    /// default, as ngspice's `fft`.
    #[default]
    Hann,
    /// Hamming (`a = 0.54, 0.46`): a lower first side lobe (−43 dB) that
    /// falls slowly.
    Hamming,
    /// Blackman (`a = 0.42, 0.5, 0.08`): side lobes from −58 dB.
    Blackman,
    /// Flat-top (`a = 0.21557895, 0.41663158, 0.277263158, 0.083578947,
    /// 0.006947368`): reads a tone's amplitude to within 0.01 dB wherever
    /// it falls between bins, at the cost of a wide peak.
    FlatTop,
}

impl Window {
    /// The window's value at sample `i` of `n`.
    pub fn coefficient(self, i: usize, n: usize) -> f64 { … }

    /// How many bins either side of a bin-centred tone it spreads into:
    /// the bins past these hold only rounding.
    pub fn half_width(self) -> usize { … }
}

/// A windowed FFT of a transient trace. See the [module docs](self) for the
/// resampling, window and scaling.
pub struct Fft {
    /// The window; Hann by default.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub window: Window,
    /// Samples, a power of two. `None` (the default) takes the smallest
    /// power of two at least the number of steps in the span.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub points: Option<usize>,
    /// Start of the span (s); the trace's start when `None`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub from: Option<f64>,
    /// End of the span (s); the trace's end when `None`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub to: Option<f64>,
}

impl Fft {
    /// An FFT of the whole trace with a Hann window and as many samples as
    /// it has steps, rounded up to a power of two.
    pub fn new() -> Self { … }

    /// Use `window`.
    pub fn window(mut self, window: Window) -> Self { … }

    /// Resample onto `n` points, a power of two.
    pub fn points(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// Take the span `[from, to)` of the trace only: skip a start-up, or
    /// pick whole periods.
    pub fn span(mut self, from: f64, to: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The spectrum of `signal` in a transient `result`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::Spectrum`] when the result has no transient, the signal
    /// isn't in it, or the settings can't be used (see [`Fft::of`]).
    pub fn on(&self, result: &SimulationResult, signal: &Signal) -> Result<Spectrum, SimError> { … }

    /// The spectrum of a `(time in s, value)` trace in ascending time.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::Spectrum`] when the span is empty or outside the trace,
    /// the point count isn't a power of two of at least 2, or the trace
    /// isn't finite and in ascending time.
    pub fn of(&self, trace: &[(f64, f64)]) -> Result<Spectrum, SimError> { … }
}

/// An [`Fft`]'s answer: one-sided bins from DC to Nyquist.
pub struct Spectrum {
    /// The window used.
    pub window: Window,
    /// Samples the span was resampled onto.
    pub points: usize,
    /// Start of the span (s).
    pub from: f64,
    /// End of the span (s).
    pub to: f64,
    /// Samples per second of the resample (Hz).
    pub sample_rate: f64,
    /// Spacing of the bins (Hz): one over the span.
    pub resolution: f64,
    /// Bins `0 … points/2`, at `k·resolution`.
    pub bins: Vec<SpectrumBin>,
}

impl Spectrum {
    /// The largest bin above DC, or `None` when there's only DC.
    pub fn peak(&self) -> Option<&SpectrumBin> { … }
}

/// One bin of a [`Spectrum`].
pub struct SpectrumBin {
    /// The bin's frequency (Hz).
    pub frequency: f64,
    /// The peak amplitude of a sine centred on this bin, in the signal's
    /// unit (the window's gain divided out).
    pub magnitude: f64,
    /// Phase (degrees) against a sine starting at the span's start.
    pub phase: f64,
}
```

## `sindr/src/import/bench.rs`

The test bench: what a schematic leaves out, and the analysis to run.

```rust
/// Where a bench item connects: a net, or a component's terminal (a
/// connector pin, a test point) standing for the net it is on.
pub enum Attach {
    /// A net, by its id, or by its display name when no net has that id
    /// and only one net has that name.
    Net(String),
    /// A component's terminal.
    Terminal(Pin),
}

/// What a [`BenchSource`] drives.
pub enum SourceKind {
    /// A voltage, `plus` above `minus`.
    Voltage {
        /// DC voltage (V); the offset of any waveform.
        volts: f64,
        /// A time-varying part added on top, for transient.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        waveform: Option<Waveform>,
    },
    /// A current, flowing out of the source into `plus`'s net and back
    /// from `minus`'s: it drives `amps` into `plus`.
    Current {
        /// DC current (A); the offset of any waveform.
        amps: f64,
        /// A time-varying part added on top, for transient.
        #[cfg_attr(
            feature = "serde",
            serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
        )]
        waveform: Option<Waveform>,
    },
}

/// A source the bench adds: a supply on a net, or a signal into an input.
pub struct BenchSource {
    /// Its id, unique among components and bench items. Results are keyed
    /// by it, and an AC or DC sweep names its source by it.
    pub id: String,
    /// Voltage or current, with any waveform.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(flatten))]
    pub kind: SourceKind,
    /// The positive side.
    pub plus: Attach,
    /// The negative side; `None` is the bench's ground.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub minus: Option<Attach>,
    /// A supply [`Bench::with_supplies_from_net_names`] assumed from a net's
    /// name. The circuit leaves it out where the bench's other voltage
    /// sources already fix its net (after ties), and keeps one per group of
    /// tied nets.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")
    )]
    pub assumed: bool,
}

impl BenchSource {
    /// A DC voltage source from `plus` to ground.
    pub fn voltage(id: impl Into<String>, plus: impl Into<Attach>, volts: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A DC current source driving `amps` into `plus`, returning through
    /// ground.
    pub fn current(id: impl Into<String>, plus: impl Into<Attach>, amps: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets the negative side.
    pub fn with_minus(mut self, minus: impl Into<Attach>) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds a waveform on top of the DC value.
    pub fn with_waveform(mut self, waveform: Waveform) -> Self { … }
}

/// What a [`BenchLoad`] is.
pub enum LoadKind {
    /// A resistance (Ω).
    Resistor(f64),
    /// A capacitance (F).
    Capacitor(f64),
    /// An inductance (H).
    Inductor(f64),
    /// A constant current drawn from `a`'s net and returned into `b`'s,
    /// such as an IC's supply current: `amps` flows into the load at `a`
    /// and out of it at `b`. For a current that changes with time, use a
    /// [`SourceKind::Current`] with a waveform, negated: it drives its
    /// current into `plus`, so a sink at `a` is a source on `a` with a
    /// negative value.
    CurrentSink {
        /// The current drawn (A).
        amps: f64,
    },
    /// A switch between `a` and `b` that changes state once, at `at`: an
    /// open-drain output holding a line low and then letting go, or a
    /// short that closes part way through. It is `on_resistance` while
    /// closed and `off_resistance` (the leakage) while open.
    ///
    /// The operating point, a DC sweep and AC take its state at t = 0. A
    /// transient lands a step on `at`; that step still sees the old state,
    /// and the next one the new, as a source's waveform jumps. With `at ≤
    /// 0` it is in its switched state from the start.
    TimedSwitch {
        /// Resistance while closed (Ω).
        on_resistance: f64,
        /// Resistance while open (Ω). In JSON it defaults to 1 GΩ, as a
        /// [`Switch`](CircuitElement::Switch) has.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_off_resistance"))]
        off_resistance: f64,
        /// When it switches (s).
        at: f64,
        /// Closed until `at` and open after it (`true`, the default in
        /// JSON), or open until `at` and closed after it.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_starts_closed"))]
        starts_closed: bool,
    },
}

impl LoadKind {
    /// A [`CurrentSink`](Self::CurrentSink) drawing `amps`.
    pub fn current_sink(amps: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A [`TimedSwitch`](Self::TimedSwitch) closed through `on_resistance`
    /// until `at`, then open (1 GΩ): a line held low and released.
    pub fn released_at(at: f64, on_resistance: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A [`TimedSwitch`](Self::TimedSwitch) open (1 GΩ) until `at`, then
    /// closed through `on_resistance`.
    pub fn closed_at(at: f64, on_resistance: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets a [`TimedSwitch`](Self::TimedSwitch)'s off resistance (Ω);
    /// any other kind is returned unchanged.
    pub fn with_off_resistance(mut self, ohms: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// A load the bench adds: what an output drives, a probe's capacitance.
pub struct BenchLoad {
    /// Its id, unique among components and bench items.
    pub id: String,
    /// What it is.
    pub kind: LoadKind,
    /// One side.
    pub a: Attach,
    /// The other side; `None` is the bench's ground.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub b: Option<Attach>,
}

impl BenchLoad {
    /// A load from `a` to ground.
    pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>, kind: LoadKind, a: impl Into<Attach>) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets the other side.
    pub fn with_b(mut self, b: impl Into<Attach>) -> Self { … }
}

/// The analysis a [`Bench`] runs.
pub enum Analysis {
    /// The DC operating point: capacitors open, inductors shorted,
    /// waveforms at their DC value. Self-heating applies.
    OperatingPoint,
    /// A transient run, as [`solve_transient`].
    Transient(TransientConfig),
    /// A small-signal frequency sweep, as [`solve_ac`]. `source_id` names
    /// a bench source.
    Ac(AcConfig),
    /// A DC sweep of one bench source's value, as [`dc_sweep`].
    DcSweep(DcSweepAxis),
}

/// What a schematic leaves out: the ground net, the sources and loads that
/// drive it, nets to tie together, and the analysis.
pub struct Bench {
    /// The reference (0 V) net.
    pub ground: Attach,
    /// Pairs of nets to join into one node, such as an analog ground and
    /// the ground.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub ties: Vec<[Attach; 2]>,
    /// Sources: supplies, signals.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub sources: Vec<BenchSource>,
    /// Loads.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")
    )]
    pub loads: Vec<BenchLoad>,
    /// The analysis [`simulate`] runs.
    pub analysis: Analysis,
}

impl Bench {
    /// A bench grounding `ground`, with nothing attached, running the
    /// operating point.
    pub fn new(ground: impl Into<Attach>) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds a source.
    pub fn with_source(mut self, source: BenchSource) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds a load.
    pub fn with_load(mut self, load: BenchLoad) -> Self { … }

    /// Joins two nets.
    pub fn with_tie(mut self, a: impl Into<Attach>, b: impl Into<Attach>) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets the analysis.
    pub fn with_analysis(mut self, analysis: Analysis) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds a DC supply to ground on every net of `netlist` whose display
    /// name is a voltage: `3V3`, `+5V`, `5V0`, `12V`, `-12V`, `+3.3V`.
    /// Names that aren't (`VCC`, `VDD`, `GND`) get nothing, and neither do
    /// decorated ones (`3V3_A`, `12V_IN`): those are often rails derived
    /// through a filter or a switch, and a source on them would short it.
    /// Each source's id is `supply:` and the net's id. Never done unless
    /// called: a power port's name is only a hint. [`supply_names`] says
    /// which supplies this assumes and which supply-like names it left for
    /// the caller to set.
    ///
    /// The supplies are [`assumed`](BenchSource::assumed): one the bench
    /// already drives with a voltage source of its own, or ties to ground,
    /// gets none, and nets tied together get one between them, whichever
    /// order the sources and ties are added in. Tied nets whose names
    /// state different voltages are an [`ImportError::ConflictingSupplies`].
    ///
    /// Ground names (`GND`, `AGND`, `GND_ISO`, `0V`) get nothing either, `0V`
    /// included though it states a voltage. A ground net other than the
    /// bench's own stays a separate node: join it with
    /// [`with_tie`](Self::with_tie) when it is the same return, or validation
    /// reports it floating. Joining it here would short an isolated return
    /// without a word.
    pub fn with_supplies_from_net_names(mut self, netlist: &Netlist) -> Self { … }
}

/// What [`Bench::with_supplies_from_net_names`] makes of a netlist's net
/// names, for a UI to show before simulating ("assumed 3.3 V on 3V3; set
/// VCC").
pub struct SupplyNames {
    /// Nets whose name is a voltage, each getting a supply of that voltage,
    /// in netlist order.
    pub assumed: Vec<AssumedSupply>,
    /// Nets whose name looks like a supply but isn't a plain voltage
    /// (`VCC`, `VDD`, `VBAT`, `3V3_A`), in netlist order, by net id: they get
    /// nothing, so the caller sets them or leaves them to the circuit.
    pub unresolved: Vec<String>,
    /// Nets named like a ground (`GND`, `AGND`, `0V`), in netlist order, by
    /// net id. One is the bench's ground; joining the others to it is the
    /// caller's call, with [`Bench::with_tie`].
    pub grounds: Vec<String>,
}

/// A supply assumed from a net's name.
pub struct AssumedSupply {
    /// The net's id.
    pub net: String,
    /// Its display name, which states the voltage.
    pub name: String,
    /// The voltage to ground, in volts.
    pub volts: f64,
}

/// Reads `netlist`'s net display names as power ports: which state a
/// voltage, which look like supplies without one, and which are grounds.
/// Changes nothing; see [`Bench::with_supplies_from_net_names`].
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::import::{supply_names, Net, Netlist};
///
/// let netlist = Netlist {
///     nets: vec![
///         Net::new("n1", [("r1", "1")]).with_name("3V3"),
///         Net::new("n2", [("r1", "2")]).with_name("VCC"),
///         Net::new("n3", [("r2", "1")]).with_name("GND"),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
/// let names = supply_names(&netlist);
/// assert_eq!((names.assumed[0].net.as_str(), names.assumed[0].volts), ("n1", 3.3));
/// assert_eq!(names.unresolved, ["n2"]);
/// assert_eq!(names.grounds, ["n3"]);
/// ```
pub fn supply_names(netlist: &Netlist) -> SupplyNames { … }

/// A netlist built against a bench, and the result of the bench's analysis.
pub struct Imported {
    /// The circuit that ran, and the node of each net.
    pub circuit: ImportedCircuit,
    /// The analysis' result.
    pub result: Simulation,
}

/// The result of a [`Bench`]'s analysis.
pub enum Simulation {
    /// [`Analysis::OperatingPoint`].
    OperatingPoint(SimulationResult),
    /// [`Analysis::Transient`].
    Transient(SimulationResult),
    /// [`Analysis::Ac`].
    Ac(AcResult),
    /// [`Analysis::DcSweep`].
    DcSweep(DcSweepResult),
}

/// Why [`simulate`] failed.
pub enum BenchError {
    /// The netlist and bench don't make a circuit.
    #[error(transparent)]
    Import(#[from] ImportError),
    /// The circuit didn't solve.
    #[error(transparent)]
    Sim(#[from] SimError),
}

/// Builds `netlist` against `bench` ([`Netlist::to_circuit`]) and runs the
/// bench's analysis.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`BenchError::Import`] when the circuit can't be built,
/// [`BenchError::Sim`] when it doesn't solve.
pub fn simulate(netlist: &Netlist, bench: &Bench) -> Result<Imported, BenchError> { … }

/// [`simulate`], reading the netlist as `options` say
/// ([`Netlist::to_circuit_with`]): terminal names from each component's
/// table, unknown kinds refused or kept as black boxes. The black boxes
/// are listed in the result's [`ImportedCircuit::black_boxes`].
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::import::{simulate_with, Bench, BenchSource, Component, ComponentKind,
///                     ImportOptions, Net, Netlist, Simulation};
///
/// // An LED whose nets name its terminals by id.
/// let netlist = Netlist {
///     components: vec![
///         Component::new("r1", ComponentKind::from_name("resistor")).with_value("470"),
///         Component::new("d1", ComponentKind::from_name("led")).with_value("Green"),
///     ],
///     nets: vec![
///         Net::new("vcc", [("r1", "1")]),
///         Net::new("a", [("r1", "2"), ("d1", "1")]),
///         Net::new("gnd", [("d1", "2")]),
///     ],
/// };
/// let options = ImportOptions::new().with_terminal_names("d1", [("1", "Anode"), ("2", "Cathode")]);
/// let bench = Bench::new("gnd").with_source(BenchSource::voltage("vs", "vcc", 5.0));
///
/// let Simulation::OperatingPoint(op) = simulate_with(&netlist, &bench, &options)?.result else {
///     unreachable!()
/// };
/// assert!(op.node_voltages["a"] > 1.5 && op.node_voltages["a"] < 2.2);
/// # Ok::<(), sindr::import::BenchError>(())
/// ```
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`simulate`].
pub fn simulate_with(
    netlist: &Netlist,
    bench: &Bench,
    options: &ImportOptions,
) -> Result<Imported, BenchError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/import/mod.rs`

Import a schematic tool's netlist, plus a test bench, as a [`Circuit`].

A schematic netlist names parts and wires, not physics: there's a
resistor `R3` valued `"4k7"`, and its terminal `1` sits on net `VOUT`.
It has no stimulus either, since a power port names a net (`3V3`)
without driving it. This module takes that shape in, in the caller's
own ids, and gives back a [`Circuit`] sindr can solve:

- A [`Netlist`]: [`Component`]s, each with an id, a [`ComponentKind`], a
  value (a number or text such as `"4k7"`), named parameters and
  optional model and part data; and [`Net`]s, each an id and the
  [`Pin`]s (component and terminal name) on it.
- A [`Bench`]: what the schematic leaves out. The ground net, sources
  and loads attached to nets or terminals, nets tied together, and the
  [`Analysis`] to run.

[`Netlist::to_circuit`] builds the circuit; [`simulate`] builds it and
runs the bench's analysis. Ids carry through: each element's id is the
component's id, and each node's name is a net id (see
[`ImportedCircuit::node`]), so results and errors point back at the
caller's own parts and nets. Every [`ImportError`] names the component,
net or bench item it is about.

Terminals are matched by name, never by pin number, since pin numbers
depend on the package. Names are compared without case, with `-`, `_`
and spaces alike (`Non-inverting`, `non_inverting`); each kind lists
the names it takes in [`ComponentKind::terminals`]. Unpolarised
two-terminal parts also take `1` and `2`. Kind names read the same way,
so a schematic tool's symbol id (`resistor-iec`, `op-amp`, `header-4`)
names its kind.

### Netlists as an editor exports them

An editor's nets often name a terminal by its id (`"1"`) and keep the
terminal's name (`"Base"`) in a table on the component. Pass that table
in [`ImportOptions::with_terminal_names`] and import with
[`Netlist::to_circuit_with`] or [`simulate_with`]: a terminal with a
name is matched by its name, one without by its id. A bare pin number
still never picks a polarised terminal.

A part sindr can't simulate, such as an IC, is a
[`ComponentKind::BlackBox`]: it adds no element, but a bench can still
attach to its terminals. Any other kind sindr doesn't know is refused
by default; [`UnknownKinds::BlackBox`] makes those black boxes too.
Either way each one is listed in [`ImportedCircuit::black_boxes`].
A net a black box leaves floating (a pull-up into an MCU input, a
resistor between two IC pins) is tied to ground through
[`HIGH_IMPEDANCE_OHMS`], the pin's leakage, so the rest of the circuit
solves; each is listed in [`ImportedCircuit::high_impedance`].

An editor's "exclude from simulation" attribute maps onto the same
thing: send that part as a [`ComponentKind::BlackBox`], and its nets
stay for the bench without an element.

### Schematics still being drawn

A required terminal on no net refuses the import with
[`ImportError::Unconnected`]. A schematic being drawn always has loose
ends, so [`UnconnectedTerminals::Skip`] leaves such a component out
instead: it adds no element, its connected nets stay, an
[`ImportWarning`] names it, and it is listed in
[`ImportedCircuit::skipped`]. Open ends (a net only one element
reaches, parts not yet wired to ground) are tied through
[`HIGH_IMPEDANCE_OHMS`], so the finished part of the design still
simulates.

### Models from part data

A part's model comes from its [`Component::model`], its value (an LED's
`"Amber"`), its parameters, or datasheet figures an editor's parts
library holds (`vf` at `if`, `hfe`, `vce_sat`, `vth`, `rds_on`), fitted
by the constructors in [`crate::datasheet`]; [`ComponentKind`] lists
what each kind reads. When none of them says anything, sindr's default
model is used, and never silently: [`ImportedCircuit::models`] records
each component's [`ModelSource`], and [`ImportedCircuit::warnings`]
carries an [`ImportWarning`] for each one that fell back to the default.

### Example

```
use sindr::import::{simulate, Analysis, Bench, BenchSource, Component,
                    ComponentKind, Net, Netlist, Simulation};

let netlist = Netlist {
    components: vec![
