        Component::new("c1", ComponentKind::Resistor).with_value("10k"),
        Component::new("c2", ComponentKind::Resistor).with_value("4k7"),
    ],
    nets: vec![
        Net::new("vin", [("c1", "1")]),
        Net::new("vout", [("c1", "2"), ("c2", "1")]),
        Net::new("gnd", [("c2", "2")]),
    ],
};
let bench = Bench::new("gnd")
    .with_source(BenchSource::voltage("supply", "vin", 5.0))
    .with_analysis(Analysis::OperatingPoint);

let Simulation::OperatingPoint(op) = simulate(&netlist, &bench).unwrap().result else {
    unreachable!()
};
let vout = op.node_voltages["vout"];
assert!((vout - 5.0 * 4.7 / 14.7).abs() < 1e-9);
```

```rust
pub use bench:: { … }

pub use value::parse_value;

/// A schematic's components and the nets joining them.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct Netlist {
    /// The components, in any order.
    pub components: Vec<Component>,
    /// The nets, in any order. A terminal on no net is unconnected.
    pub nets: Vec<Net>,
}

/// One component of a [`Netlist`].
pub struct Component {
    /// The caller's id, unique in the netlist. It becomes the element's id,
    /// so results are keyed by it.
    pub id: String,
    /// What the component is.
    pub kind: ComponentKind,
    /// The main value: resistance (Ω), capacitance (F), inductance (H), a
    /// fuse's rating (A), a zener's or regulator's voltage (V), a
    /// potentiometer's end-to-end resistance (Ω), a crystal's frequency
    /// (Hz). Text such as `"4k7"` goes through [`parse_value`]. Text that
    /// isn't a value (a part number) is ignored where a parameter or model
    /// can stand in, and an error where the kind needs a value.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub value: Option<Value>,
    /// Further parameters by name, such as `bf` for a transistor's gain,
    /// `color` for an LED, or datasheet figures such as `vf` and `if`. Each
    /// kind's are listed on [`ComponentKind`] (figures also take `_min`,
    /// `_typ` and `_max`); any other name is an
    /// [`ImportError::UnknownParameter`].
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")
    )]
    pub params: BTreeMap<String, Value>,
    /// Device model, for the kinds that take one.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub model: Option<Model>,
    /// Part data (ratings, thermal path, reference, MPN …), copied into
    /// [`Circuit::parts`] under the component's id.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub part: Option<Part>,
}

impl Component {
    /// A component with no value, parameters, model or part data.
    pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>, kind: ComponentKind) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`value`](Self::value).
    pub fn with_value(mut self, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds a parameter.
    pub fn with_param(mut self, name: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<Value>) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`model`](Self::model).
    pub fn with_model(mut self, model: Model) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`part`](Self::part).
    pub fn with_part(mut self, part: Part) -> Self { … }
}

/// A value or parameter: a number in SI base units, text, a flag, or a
/// typed quantity.
pub enum Value {
    /// A number in SI base units (Ω, F, H, V, A, Hz, K).
    Number(f64),
    /// A flag, such as a switch's `closed`.
    Bool(bool),
    /// Text: a value as written (`"4k7"`, read by [`parse_value`]) or a
    /// name (an LED's `"red"`).
    Text(String),
    /// A typed quantity, as a parts library stores it: a number in base
    /// units with its unit, and the text it was shown as. In JSON,
    /// `{"value": 300, "unit": "K", "text": "300 K"}`. A quantity whose
    /// unit isn't the one a value or parameter is in is an
    /// [`ImportError::BadValue`]. Boxed, so a `Value` stays as small as
    /// its text.
    Quantity(Box<Quantity>),
}

/// A number in base units with its unit, as a parts library stores a
/// typed spec: `Quantity::new(0.02, Unit::Ampere)` for 20 mA.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// or build it with [`new`](Self::new) and [`with_text`](Self::with_text).
pub struct Quantity {
    /// The number, in the unit's base unit (A, not mA), exact as the
    /// library stores it.
    pub value: f64,
    /// The unit.
    pub unit: Unit,
    /// The quantity as the editor shows it (`"20 mA"`), for messages; the
    /// number is [`value`](Self::value), not this text.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub text: Option<String>,
}

impl Quantity {
    /// `value` in `unit`, with no text.
    pub fn new(value: f64, unit: Unit) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`text`](Self::text).
    pub fn with_text(mut self, text: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }
}

/// The unit of a [`Quantity`]: the base units a parts library stores
/// specs in. Serialised as its symbol: `"Ohm"`, `"F"`, `"H"`, `"V"`,
/// `"A"`, `"W"`, `"Hz"`, `"s"`, `"m"`, `"K"`, and `"1"` for a plain ratio
/// (a gain, a position). [`from_symbol`](Self::from_symbol) also reads
/// `Ω`; any other symbol is [`Other`](Self::Other).
pub enum Unit {
    /// Ohm (Ω).
    Ohm,
    /// Farad.
    Farad,
    /// Henry.
    Henry,
    /// Volt.
    Volt,
    /// Ampere.
    Ampere,
    /// Watt.
    Watt,
    /// Hertz.
    Hertz,
    /// Second.
    Second,
    /// Metre.
    Metre,
    /// Kelvin.
    Kelvin,
    /// A plain ratio, unit `1`: a gain, a coupling, a position.
    #[default]
    Ratio,
    /// A unit sindr doesn't know, by its symbol. Accepted where any unit is.
    Other(String),
}

impl Unit {
    /// The unit with this symbol: `"Ohm"` (or `"Ω"`, `"ohm"`), `"F"`,
    /// `"H"`, `"V"`, `"A"`, `"W"`, `"Hz"`, `"s"`, `"m"`, `"K"`, `"1"`.
    /// Case matters except for `Ohm` and `Hz`, since `m` and `K` aren't
    /// `M` and `k`.
    pub fn from_symbol(symbol: &str) -> Self { … }

    /// The unit's symbol, as [`from_symbol`](Self::from_symbol) reads it.
    pub fn symbol(&self) -> &str { … }
}

/// Where an imported component's model came from. Recorded for every
/// component that becomes an element, in
/// [`ImportedCircuit::models`].
pub enum ModelSource {
    /// [`Component::model`].
    Model,
    /// [`Component::value`]: a resistance, a zener's voltage, an LED's
    /// colour named in the value text.
    Value,
    /// Named parameters that set the model directly: `bf`, `color`,
    /// `idss`.
    Params,
    /// Datasheet figures (`vf` at `if`, `hfe`, `vce_sat`, `vth`,
    /// `rds_on` …), fitted by the `from_datasheet` constructors in
    /// [`crate::datasheet`].
    Datasheet,
    /// Nothing the component gave: sindr's built-in model for the kind.
    /// Each such component has an [`ImportWarning`].
    Default,
}

/// Something about an import worth checking, though it isn't an error:
/// mostly a component that got sindr's default model because nothing in
/// its data said otherwise.
pub struct ImportWarning {
    /// The component's id.
    pub component: String,
    /// What happened, and what sindr used instead.
    pub message: String,
}

/// A device model for a [`Component`] whose kind takes one.
pub enum Model {
    /// For a diode (`.model D`).
    Diode(DiodeModel),
    /// For an NPN or PNP transistor (`.model NPN`/`PNP`), besides `bf`.
    Bjt(BjtModel),
    /// For an NMOS or PMOS transistor.
    Mosfet(MosfetParams),
    /// For an op-amp: its macromodel.
    OpAmp(OpAmpModel),
    /// For a linear regulator: dropout, quiescent current and limits.
    Regulator(RegulatorParams),
    /// For a battery: its equivalent circuit.
    Battery(BatteryParams),
    /// For a varactor.
    Varactor(VaractorParams),
    /// For an IGBT.
    Igbt(IgbtParams),
    /// A SPICE subcircuit, such as a vendor's op-amp or regulator model,
    /// standing in for the whole part. See [`SubcktModel`].
    #[cfg(feature = "spice")]
    Subckt(SubcktModel),
}

/// A part simulated by a SPICE subcircuit instead of a built-in element:
/// the model text a vendor ships, which `.subckt` in it to use, and which
/// of the component's terminals binds to each of its ports.
///
/// A component of any kind with this model is placed as an instance of the
/// subcircuit under the component's id, so its internal nodes are
/// `<id>.<node>` in a result. Only the model's ground and its own
/// `.global` nets join the circuit's: a node named like the circuit's
/// ground net or another model's global stays the model's own, as
/// `<id>.<node>_local`. Its terminals are read like a black box's: any
/// name, through [`ImportOptions::terminal_names`] when given.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::import::{
///     simulate, Bench, BenchSource, Component, ComponentKind, Model, Net, Netlist, Simulation,
///     SubcktModel,
/// };
///
/// // A unity-gain buffer: a vendor-style macromodel with ports in+, in-, out.
/// let text = "
/// .subckt buffer inp inn out
/// Rin inp inn 10meg
/// E1 mid 0 inp inn 1e5
/// Rout mid out 10
/// .ends";
/// let netlist = Netlist {
///     components: vec![
///         Component::new("U1", ComponentKind::BlackBox).with_model(Model::Subckt(
///             SubcktModel::new(text, "buffer", ["IN+", "IN-", "OUT"]),
///         )),
///         Component::new("RL", ComponentKind::Resistor).with_value("10k"),
///     ],
///     nets: vec![
///         Net::new("in", [("U1", "IN+")]),
///         Net::new("out", [("U1", "IN-"), ("U1", "OUT"), ("RL", "1")]),
///         Net::new("gnd", [("RL", "2")]),
///     ],
/// };
/// let bench = Bench::new("gnd").with_source(BenchSource::voltage("v", "in", 2.0));
/// let out = simulate(&netlist, &bench).unwrap();
/// let Simulation::OperatingPoint(r) = &out.result else { unreachable!() };
/// assert!((r.node_voltages["out"] - 2.0).abs() < 1e-3);
/// ```
pub struct SubcktModel {
    /// SPICE text holding the subcircuit: a `.subckt` … `.ends` block, or a
    /// `.lib` excerpt with several and their `.model` cards. Elements
    /// outside any `.subckt` are ignored.
    pub text: String,
    /// The `.subckt` to use, matched without regard to case.
    pub name: String,
    /// The component's terminal for each port, in the subcircuit's port
    /// order: `pins[0]` binds to its first port.
    pub pins: Vec<String>,
}

impl SubcktModel {
    /// Subcircuit `name` from `text`, with `pins` the component's terminal
    /// for each of its ports in order.
    pub fn new<P: Into<String>>(
        text: impl Into<String>,
        name: impl Into<String>,
        pins: impl IntoIterator<Item = P>,
    ) -> Self { … }
}

/// What a [`Component`] is. Serialised as its snake_case name
/// (`"resistor"`, `"npn"`). [`from_name`](Self::from_name) also reads a
/// schematic tool's symbol ids (`"resistor-iec"`, `"op-amp"`); a name
/// sindr doesn't know reads as [`Other`](Self::Other), which
/// [`Netlist::to_circuit`] refuses with the component's id unless
/// [`UnknownKinds::BlackBox`] says to keep it as a black box.
///
/// Parameters each kind takes, besides [`Component::value`] (numbers in SI
/// units, or text for [`parse_value`]):
///
/// | Kind | Value | Parameters | Model |
/// |---|---|---|---|
/// | `resistor` | Ω, required | | |
/// | `capacitor`, `capacitor_polarized` | F, required | | |
/// | `inductor` | H, required | | |
/// | `diode` | | `vf` (V) at `if` (A), and `vf2` at `if2`; `temperature` (K) | `Diode` |
/// | `schottky_diode`, `photodiode` | | `temperature` (K); photodiode `irradiance` (W) | |
/// | `zener_diode` | V (breakdown) or `vz` | `vz` at `iz` (A); `temperature` | |
/// | `led` | colour named in the text (`"Amber"`, `"LED red 3mm"`) | `color` or `colour` (`red`, `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `white`, any case); `vf` (V) at `if` (A), and `vf2` at `if2`; `temperature` | |
/// | `varactor` | | | `Varactor` |
/// | `npn`, `pnp` | | `bf` (or `beta`); `hfe` at `hfe_ic` (A); `vce_sat` (V) at `vce_sat_ic` and `vce_sat_ib` (A); `temperature` | `Bjt` |
/// | `nmos`, `pmos` | | `vth` (V) at `vth_id` (A); `rds_on` (Ω) at `rds_on_vgs` (V), optionally at `rds_on_id` (A) | `Mosfet` |
/// | `njfet`, `pjfet` | | `idss` (A), `vp` (V) | |
/// | `igbt` | | | `Igbt` |
/// | `op_amp`, `comparator` | | `v_pos`, `v_neg` (V; default from bench supplies on its supply pins, else ±15) | op-amp: `OpAmp` |
/// | `dual_op_amp`, `quad_op_amp`, `dual_comparator`, `quad_comparator` | | as `op_amp` and `comparator`, for every unit | op-amps: `OpAmp` |
/// | `potentiometer` | Ω, required | `position` (0 top to 1 bottom, default 0.5) | |
/// | `switch`, `push_button` | | `closed` (default false) | |
/// | `fuse` | A (rating) | `blown` (default false) | |
/// | `relay` | | `pickup_voltage` (V, required), `coil_resistance` (Ω), `inductance` (H) | |
/// | `transformer` | | `l1`, `l2` (H, required), `k` | |
/// | `crystal` | Hz (series resonance) or `frequency` | `frequency`, `esr` (Ω, default 50), `c0` (F, default 5 pF) | |
/// | `ferrite_bead` | Ω (impedance at 100 MHz) or `z_100mhz` | `z_100mhz`, `r_dc` (Ω, default 0.1) | |
/// | `regulator` | V (output) or `voltage` | `voltage` | `Regulator` |
/// | `battery` | V, unless a model | `state_of_charge` (default 1), `r_series` (Ω, default 0.1), `capacity` (Ah, default 1) | `Battery` |
/// | `thermistor` | | `temperature` (K) | |
/// | `photoresistor` | | `light_level` (0 dark to 1 bright) | |
/// | `voltage_source`, `current_source` | V or A, required | | |
/// | `connector`, `test_point`, `net_tie`, `mounting_hole` | | | |
/// | `black_box` | | | |
///
/// # Part data
///
/// `vf`, `vf2`, `vz`, `hfe`, `vce_sat`, `vth` and `rds_on` are datasheet
/// figures: each also takes `_min`, `_typ` and `_max` forms (`hfe_min`,
/// `vce_sat_max`), and a fit uses the typical value, else the middle of
/// minimum and maximum, else whichever is given
/// ([`DatasheetValue::nominal`](crate::datasheet::DatasheetValue::nominal)).
/// The other names are test conditions, read as given. A figure needs its
/// condition (`vf` needs `if`, `vth` needs `vth_id` and `rds_on`), or the
/// import is an [`ImportError::MissingValue`]. What each fit does:
///
/// - **Diode**: [`DiodeModel::from_datasheet`]: IS through `vf` at `if`
///   (N = 1), or IS and N through both points.
/// - **LED** with `vf`: [`DiodeModel::led_from_datasheet`], imported as a
///   [`CircuitElement::Diode`] with that model, since the LED element knows
///   only its colour's preset. Without `vf`, the colour sets the preset; a
///   colour from the `color` parameter wins over one in the value text.
/// - **Zener** with `iz`: [`DiodeModel::zener_from_datasheet`] sets the
///   element's `vz` so that it carries `iz` at the datasheet's Vz.
/// - **NPN, PNP**: `bf` is `hfe` (or `bf`/`beta`, which win); with
///   `vce_sat`, [`BjtModel::from_datasheet`] fits BR through it. `hfe_ic`
///   is kept for the record: the model's gain doesn't change with current.
/// - **NMOS, PMOS**: [`MosfetParams::from_datasheet`] fits KP and VTO.
///
/// [`ImportedCircuit::models`] says, for every component, which of model,
/// value, parameters, datasheet figures or sindr's default the model came
/// from, and [`ImportedCircuit::warnings`] has one warning for every
/// component that got the default (a transistor whose value is only a part
/// number, an LED with no colour). Values and parameters may be typed
/// quantities ([`Value::Quantity`]), whose unit is checked against the
/// parameter's.
///
/// # Other kinds
///
/// The last two rows add no element, and any terminal name is fine. A
/// bench attaches sources and loads to their terminals. The connectors and
/// the like are [passive](Self::is_passive); a black box stands for a part
/// sindr can't simulate (an IC), takes any value, parameters and model and
/// ignores them, and is listed in [`ImportedCircuit::black_boxes`].
///
/// A dual or quad part is one package with two or four units sharing its
/// supply pins. Each unit becomes its own element, `<id>.a`, `<id>.b`
/// and so on, so results are keyed by those; [`Component::part`] stays
/// under the package's id. A unit's terminals are an op-amp's with the
/// unit's letter or number on them: `a_in+`, `in+ a`, `1IN+`, `IN1+`,
/// `INA+`, `-IN B`, `OUT B`, `2OUT`, `Non-inverting A`. The supplies are `v+` and
/// `v-` (or `vcc`, `vee`, `positive supply` …), without a unit. A unit
/// with none of its terminals connected (a spare half) adds no element;
/// one connected in part is an [`ImportError::Unconnected`] as for a
/// single op-amp (or skipped, under [`UnconnectedTerminals::Skip`]).
///
/// Names besides the canonical ones: `resistor_iec`, `resistor_us`, `res`;
/// `cap`, `capacitor_polarised`, `capacitor_electrolytic`, `electrolytic`;
/// `zener`, `schottky`; `opamp`, `operational_amplifier`;
/// `op_amp_dual`, `dual_opamp`, `op_amp_quad`, `quad_opamp`,
/// `comparator_dual`, `comparator_quad`; `pot`,
/// `trimmer`; `pushbutton`, `button`; `switch_spst`, `spst`;
/// `xtal`, `quartz`; `ferrite`, `bead`; `ldo`, `voltage_regulator`;
/// `cell`; `ntc`; `ldr`; `testpoint`; `header`, `header_<n>`,
/// `pin_header`, `terminal_block`, `conn` for a connector; `ic` for a
/// black box.
pub enum ComponentKind {
    Resistor,
    Capacitor,
    CapacitorPolarized,
    Inductor,
    Diode,
    SchottkyDiode,
    ZenerDiode,
    Led,
    Photodiode,
    Varactor,
    Npn,
    Pnp,
    Nmos,
    Pmos,
    Njfet,
    Pjfet,
    Igbt,
    OpAmp,
    Comparator,
    /// Two op-amps in one package, sharing its supply pins.
    DualOpAmp,
    /// Four op-amps in one package, sharing its supply pins.
    QuadOpAmp,
    /// Two comparators in one package, sharing its supply pins.
    DualComparator,
    /// Four comparators in one package, sharing its supply pins.
    QuadComparator,
    Potentiometer,
    Switch,
    PushButton,
    Fuse,
    Relay,
    Transformer,
    Regulator,
    Battery,
    /// A quartz crystal ([`CircuitElement::Crystal`]).
    Crystal,
    /// A ferrite bead ([`CircuitElement::FerriteBead`]).
    FerriteBead,
    /// A part sindr doesn't simulate, kept for its terminals: it adds no
    /// element, and a bench may attach to its terminals.
    BlackBox,
    Thermistor,
    Photoresistor,
    VoltageSource,
    CurrentSource,
    Connector,
    TestPoint,
    NetTie,
    MountingHole,
    /// A kind sindr doesn't simulate, by the caller's name for it.
    Other(String),
}

impl ComponentKind {
    /// The kind with this name, or [`Other`](Self::Other) with the name as
    /// given. Case is ignored and `-`, `_` and spaces are alike, so a
    /// symbol id such as `"Op-Amp"` or `"push button"` reads too; the
    /// aliases on [`ComponentKind`] (`resistor-iec`, `header-4`, `xtal`)
    /// name kinds as well.
    pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Self { … }

    /// The kind's snake_case name; an [`Other`](Self::Other) kind's own.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str { … }

    /// Whether the kind is a connector, test point, net tie or mounting
    /// hole: no element, any terminal name. A [`BlackBox`](Self::BlackBox)
    /// adds no element either, but isn't passive.
    pub fn is_passive(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// The kind's terminals in element order: each a list of the names it
    /// answers to, lowercase, canonical first. A terminal given as
    /// `Non-inverting` or `positive supply` matches `non_inverting` and
    /// `positive_supply`: case is ignored and `-`, `_` and spaces are
    /// alike. Required terminals come first;
    /// [`optional_terminals`](Self::optional_terminals) says how many at
    /// the end may be left off. Empty for passive, black-box and unknown
    /// kinds.
    pub fn terminals(&self) -> &'static [&'static [&'static str]] { … }

    /// How many of [`terminals`](Self::terminals), at the end, may be left
    /// unconnected: a MOSFET's body (tied to its source), an op-amp's two
    /// supply pins (a multi-unit part's too).
    pub fn optional_terminals(&self) -> usize { … }

    /// For a multi-unit part, the kind of each unit and how many there
    /// are: a dual op-amp is two [`OpAmp`](Self::OpAmp)s.
    pub fn units(&self) -> Option<(ComponentKind, usize)> { … }
}

/// A net: the terminals wired together.
pub struct Net {
    /// The caller's id, unique in the netlist. It becomes the node's name.
    pub id: String,
    /// Display name (`"VOUT"`, `"3V3"`). A bench may refer to the net by
    /// it when it is unique.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// The terminals on the net.
    pub pins: Vec<Pin>,
}

impl Net {
    /// A net with no display name.
    pub fn new<C, T>(id: impl Into<String>, pins: impl IntoIterator<Item = (C, T)>) -> Self
    where
        C: Into<String>,
        T: Into<String>,
 { … }

    /// Sets [`name`](Self::name).
    pub fn with_name(mut self, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }
}

/// A component's terminal, by the component's id and the terminal's name.
pub struct Pin {
    /// The component's id.
    pub component: String,
    /// The terminal's name (`"anode"`, `"B"`, `"1"`).
    pub terminal: String,
}

impl Pin {
    /// The terminal `terminal` of component `component`.
    pub fn new(component: impl Into<String>, terminal: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }
}

/// Why a netlist and bench can't become a circuit. Each variant names the
/// caller's component, net or bench item.
pub enum ImportError {
    /// Two components, nets or bench items share an id.
    #[error("id \"{id}\" is used twice")]
    DuplicateId {
        /// The id.
        id: String,
    },
    /// A kind sindr doesn't simulate.
    #[error("component \"{component}\": sindr can't simulate a \"{kind}\"")]
    UnsupportedKind {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// Its kind's name.
        kind: String,
    },
    /// A net names a component that isn't in the netlist.
    #[error("net \"{net}\" names component \"{component}\", which isn't in the netlist")]
    UnknownComponent {
        /// The net's id, or the bench item's.
        net: String,
        /// The missing component's id.
        component: String,
    },
    /// A terminal name the component's kind doesn't have.
    #[error(
        "component \"{component}\" ({kind}) has no terminal \"{terminal}\"; it has {expected}"
    )]
    UnknownTerminal {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// Its kind's name.
        kind: String,
        /// The terminal as given, followed by its name in parentheses when
        /// [`ImportOptions::with_terminal_names`] gave it one.
        terminal: String,
        /// The names it takes.
        expected: String,
    },
    /// A terminal sits on two nets.
    #[error("terminal \"{terminal}\" of component \"{component}\" is on two nets, \"{first}\" and \"{second}\"")]
    TerminalOnTwoNets {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// The terminal.
        terminal: String,
        /// One net's id.
        first: String,
        /// The other's.
        second: String,
    },
    /// A terminal the element needs is on no net.
    #[error("terminal \"{terminal}\" of component \"{component}\" isn't connected")]
    Unconnected {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// The terminal's canonical name.
        terminal: String,
    },
    /// The kind needs a value and the component has none, or one that
    /// isn't a number.
    #[error("component \"{component}\" needs {what}")]
    MissingValue {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// What it needs, with its unit.
        what: String,
    },
    /// A value or parameter that isn't a value of the right type.
    #[error("component \"{component}\": {field} {given:?} isn't {expected}")]
    BadValue {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// `"value"` or the parameter's name.
        field: String,
        /// What was given.
        given: Value,
        /// What it should be.
        expected: String,
    },
    /// A parameter the kind doesn't take.
    #[error("component \"{component}\" ({kind}) takes no parameter \"{parameter}\"")]
    UnknownParameter {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// Its kind's name.
        kind: String,
        /// The parameter's name.
        parameter: String,
    },
    /// A model of the wrong sort for the kind.
    #[error("component \"{component}\" ({kind}) can't take a {model} model")]
    WrongModel {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// Its kind's name.
        kind: String,
        /// The model's sort.
        model: String,
    },
    /// A MOSFET's body is on a different net from its source; sindr's
    /// MOSFET ties the two.
    #[error("component \"{component}\": the body must be on the source's net")]
    BodyNotAtSource {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
    },
    /// The bench names a net that isn't in the netlist, or a display name
    /// several nets share.
    #[error("{item} names net \"{net}\", which {problem}")]
    UnknownNet {
        /// The bench item: `"ground"`, a source's id …
        item: String,
        /// The net as named.
        net: String,
        /// `"isn't in the netlist"` or `"is the name of several nets"`.
        problem: String,
    },
    /// A [`SubcktModel`]'s text doesn't parse, or has no `.subckt` by its
    /// name.
    #[error("component \"{component}\": its subcircuit model {problem}")]
    SubcktModel {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// What's wrong: the parse error, or the missing name.
        problem: String,
    },
    /// A [`SubcktModel`]'s pin map doesn't fit the subcircuit or the
    /// component.
    #[error("component \"{component}\": pin \"{pin}\" of its subcircuit model {problem}")]
    SubcktPin {
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// The pin as given in [`SubcktModel::pins`], or the port count
        /// for a map of the wrong length.
        pin: String,
        /// What's wrong with it.
        problem: String,
    },
    /// The bench attaches to a terminal that's on no net.
    #[error("{item} attaches to terminal \"{terminal}\" of component \"{component}\", which is on no net")]
    AttachedToUnconnected {
        /// The bench item.
        item: String,
        /// The component's id.
        component: String,
        /// The terminal.
        terminal: String,
    },
    /// Two supplies [`Bench::with_supplies_from_net_names`] assumed land on
    /// one node, through the bench's ties, at different voltages.
    #[error(
        "supplies \"{first}\" ({first_volts} V) and \"{second}\" ({second_volts} V) are on one node, \"{node}\""
    )]
    ConflictingSupplies {
        /// The node, by its name in the circuit (a net id).
        node: String,
        /// The first supply's id.
        first: String,
        /// Its voltage.
        first_volts: f64,
        /// The second supply's id.
        second: String,
        /// Its voltage.
        second_volts: f64,
    },
}

/// What to do with a component of a kind sindr doesn't know
/// ([`ComponentKind::Other`]).
pub enum UnknownKinds {
    /// Refuse the import with [`ImportError::UnsupportedKind`], naming the
    /// first such component. The default, and what
    /// [`Netlist::to_circuit`] does.
    #[default]
    Refuse,
    /// Import it as a [`ComponentKind::BlackBox`]: no element, terminals
    /// kept for the bench, listed in [`ImportedCircuit::black_boxes`].
    BlackBox,
}

/// What to do with a component that has a required terminal on no net.
pub enum UnconnectedTerminals {
    /// Refuse the import with [`ImportError::Unconnected`], naming the
    /// first such terminal. The default, and what [`Netlist::to_circuit`]
    /// does.
    #[default]
    Error,
    /// Leave the component out: no element, its connected nets kept, an
    /// [`ImportWarning`] naming it, and listed in
    /// [`ImportedCircuit::skipped`]. Open ends (a net only one element
    /// reaches, or parts not yet wired to ground) are tied through
    /// [`HIGH_IMPEDANCE_OHMS`] and listed in
    /// [`ImportedCircuit::high_impedance`]. For a schematic still being
    /// drawn.
    Skip,
}

/// How [`Netlist::to_circuit_with`] and [`simulate_with`] read a netlist:
/// what to do with unknown kinds and unconnected terminals, and each
/// component's terminal names.
///
/// Built with [`new`](Self::new) and the `with_*` setters. The default
/// reads a netlist as [`Netlist::to_circuit`] does.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::import::{ImportOptions, UnknownKinds};
///
/// let options = ImportOptions::new()
///     .with_unknown_kinds(UnknownKinds::BlackBox)
///     .with_terminal_names("q1", [("1", "Base"), ("2", "Emitter"), ("3", "Collector")]);
/// assert_eq!(options.terminal_names["q1"]["1"], "Base");
/// ```
pub struct ImportOptions {
    /// What to do with a component of a kind sindr doesn't know.
    pub unknown_kinds: UnknownKinds,
    /// What to do with a component that has a required terminal on no net.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(skip_serializing_if = "UnconnectedTerminals::is_error")
    )]
    pub unconnected: UnconnectedTerminals,
    /// Terminal names by component id, then terminal id: the table a
    /// schematic tool keeps on each component (`"1"` is `"Base"`). A pin
    /// whose terminal has a name here is matched by that name, then by its
    /// id; one without is matched by the id alone, so a bare pin number
    /// still can't pick a polarised terminal. On a passive or black-box
    /// part, a bench may attach to a terminal by its name. Names for a
    /// component that isn't in the netlist are unused.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty"))]
    pub terminal_names: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
}

impl ImportOptions {
    /// Options that read a netlist as [`Netlist::to_circuit`] does.
    pub fn new() -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`unknown_kinds`](Self::unknown_kinds).
    pub fn with_unknown_kinds(mut self, unknown_kinds: UnknownKinds) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`unconnected`](Self::unconnected).
    pub fn with_unconnected(mut self, unconnected: UnconnectedTerminals) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds names for `component`'s terminals, as `(terminal id, name)`
    /// pairs. Leave out terminals that have no name.
    pub fn with_terminal_names<T, N>(
        mut self,
        component: impl Into<String>,
        names: impl IntoIterator<Item = (T, N)>,
    ) -> Self
    where
        T: Into<String>,
        N: Into<String>,
 { … }
}

/// A component left out under [`UnconnectedTerminals::Skip`] because a
/// terminal its element needs is on no net.
pub struct SkippedPart {
    /// The component's id, or a dual or quad unit's (`<id>.a`).
    pub component: String,
    /// The required terminals on no net, by canonical name, in terminal
    /// order.
    pub unconnected: Vec<String>,
}

/// A component imported as a black box: a [`ComponentKind::BlackBox`],
/// or an unknown kind under [`UnknownKinds::BlackBox`]. It simulates
/// nothing.
pub struct BlackBoxPart {
    /// The component's id.
    pub component: String,
    /// Its kind's name: `"black_box"`, or the unknown kind as given.
    pub kind: String,
    /// Net id by terminal id, for the terminals that are on a net.
    pub terminals: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

/// The resistance an import ties a floating net to ground through: an IC
/// input's leakage, and SPICE's gmin (10⁻¹² S). A 10 kΩ pull-up into it
/// sits 33 pV below its rail.
pub const HIGH_IMPEDANCE_OHMS: f64 = 1e12;

/// A net whose only connections, besides at most one element terminal,
/// are pins of parts sindr doesn't simulate: an MCU input with a pull-up,
/// an I²C line between two black boxes, a resistor between two IC pins.
/// Electrically those pins are high impedance, so the net is held where its
/// one element puts it; for the solver it would be floating. The import
/// ties it to ground through [`HIGH_IMPEDANCE_OHMS`], as element
/// [`resistor`](Self::resistor), so the rest of the circuit solves.
pub struct HighImpedanceNet {
    /// The node, by its name in the circuit (a net id; see
    /// [`ImportedCircuit::node`]).
    pub node: String,
    /// The id of the tie's resistor in [`ImportedCircuit::circuit`].
    pub resistor: String,
    /// The pins of unsimulated parts on the net, in netlist order. Empty
    /// for an open end under [`UnconnectedTerminals::Skip`]: a net only one
    /// element reaches, or one in a group not yet wired to ground.
    pub pins: Vec<Pin>,
}

/// A [`Circuit`] built from a [`Netlist`], with the map from the caller's
/// net ids to its node names.
pub struct ImportedCircuit {
    /// The circuit. Element ids are component and bench ids; node names
    /// are net ids.
    pub circuit: Circuit,
    /// Node name by net id. Nets the bench ties together share one node,
    /// named after one of them; every other net's node is its own id.
    pub nodes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Every component imported as a black box, in netlist order. None of
    /// them is in [`circuit`](Self::circuit), so a result has nothing for
    /// them; check this list before calling a design done.
    pub black_boxes: Vec<BlackBoxPart>,
    /// Where each component's model came from, by component id, for every
    /// component that became an element (a dual or quad part once, under
    /// its package's id).
    pub models: BTreeMap<String, ModelSource>,
    /// Warnings, in netlist order: one for every component whose model is
    /// [`ModelSource::Default`], and any other part data sindr couldn't use.
    pub warnings: Vec<ImportWarning>,
    /// Nets left floating by parts that simulate nothing, each tied to
    /// ground through [`HIGH_IMPEDANCE_OHMS`] so the rest of the circuit
    /// solves. See [`HighImpedanceNet`].
    pub high_impedance: Vec<HighImpedanceNet>,
    /// Components left out under [`UnconnectedTerminals::Skip`], in
    /// netlist order. Like a black box, none of them is in
    /// [`circuit`](Self::circuit).
    pub skipped: Vec<SkippedPart>,
}

impl ImportedCircuit {
    /// The node name of net `net_id`, for looking up results.
    pub fn node(&self, net_id: &str) -> Option<&str> { … }

    /// Where component `id`'s model came from; `None` for a component
    /// that isn't an element (passive, black box) or isn't in the netlist.
    pub fn model_source(&self, id: &str) -> Option<ModelSource> { … }

    /// The ids of the components that got sindr's default model, in id
    /// order.
    pub fn defaulted(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> { … }
}

impl Netlist {
    /// Builds the circuit: the netlist's components, with `bench`'s ground,
    /// ties, sources and loads. The bench's analysis isn't run; see
    /// [`simulate`]. Unknown kinds are refused; [`to_circuit_with`]
    /// can keep them as black boxes.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// An [`ImportError`] naming the component, net or bench item that
    /// can't be built. Solver checks (a floating node, no path to ground)
    /// come later, from the analysis.
    ///
    /// [`to_circuit_with`]: Self::to_circuit_with
    pub fn to_circuit(&self, bench: &Bench) -> Result<ImportedCircuit, ImportError> { … }

    /// [`to_circuit`](Self::to_circuit), reading the netlist as `options`
    /// say: with each component's terminal names, and unknown kinds
    /// refused or kept as black boxes.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::import::{Bench, BenchSource, Component, ComponentKind, ImportOptions,
    ///                     Net, Netlist, UnknownKinds};
    ///
    /// // A transistor whose nets name terminals by id, and an IC sindr
    /// // doesn't know on the supply.
    /// let netlist = Netlist {
    ///     components: vec![
    ///         Component::new("q1", ComponentKind::from_name("npn")),
    ///         Component::new("r1", ComponentKind::from_name("resistor-iec")).with_value("100k"),
    ///         Component::new("u1", ComponentKind::from_name("mcu-qfn32")).with_value("MCU"),
    ///     ],
    ///     nets: vec![
    ///         Net::new("vcc", [("r1", "1"), ("q1", "3"), ("u1", "8")]),
    ///         Net::new("base", [("r1", "2"), ("q1", "1")]),
    ///         Net::new("gnd", [("q1", "2"), ("u1", "1")]),
    ///     ],
    /// };
    /// let options = ImportOptions::new()
    ///     .with_unknown_kinds(UnknownKinds::BlackBox)
    ///     .with_terminal_names("q1", [("1", "Base"), ("2", "Emitter"), ("3", "Collector")]);
    /// let bench = Bench::new("gnd").with_source(BenchSource::voltage("vs", "vcc", 5.0));
    ///
    /// let imported = netlist.to_circuit_with(&bench, &options).unwrap();
    /// assert_eq!(imported.black_boxes[0].component, "u1");
    /// assert_eq!(imported.black_boxes[0].terminals["8"], "vcc");
    /// assert!(netlist.to_circuit(&bench).is_err());
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// As [`to_circuit`](Self::to_circuit); with
    /// [`UnknownKinds::BlackBox`], never [`ImportError::UnsupportedKind`].
    pub fn to_circuit_with(
        &self,
        bench: &Bench,
        options: &ImportOptions,
    ) -> Result<ImportedCircuit, ImportError> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/import/subckt.rs`

A SPICE subcircuit as a part's model: parse the model text, pick the
`.subckt`, and bind the component's terminals to its ports.

## `sindr/src/import/value.rs`

Component values as a schematic writes them: `10k`, `4.7 µF`, `4k7`, `1M`.

```rust
/// Reads a component value the way a schematic writes it, to a number in
/// SI base units. `None` when the text isn't a value.
///
/// Takes a number with an optional exponent, an optional prefix, and an
/// optional unit: `10k`, `4.7uF`, `4.7 µF`, `100nF`, `2.2mH`, `1e-6`,
/// `5V`, `10 kΩ`. Prefixes are case-sensitive as on a schematic, so `1M`
/// is 1 MΩ, not the 1 mΩ a SPICE deck would read; `meg` is mega too.
/// The prefix (or `R` for 1, or the unit) may stand in for the decimal
/// point, as on a resistor's marking: `4k7` is 4.7 k, `4R7` is 4.7, `2M2`
/// is 2.2 M, `5V1` is 5.1 V.
///
/// A space between the number and its unit doesn't run them together:
/// `"0.01 1"` (a ratio, unit `1`) is 0.01, and `"300 K"` is 300 kelvin.
/// Written with no space, `300K` is 300 k as on a schematic; a bare `m`
/// or `K` after a space is the unit (metre, kelvin), any other text after
/// a space reads as if the space weren't there (`10 k`, `4.7 µF`), and
/// digits after a space make it no value (`1 2` isn't 12). Kelvin
/// and metre also follow a prefix: `300 mK`, `5mm`.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::import::parse_value;
///
/// assert_eq!(parse_value("10k"), Some(10e3));
/// assert_eq!(parse_value("4k7"), Some(4.7e3));
/// assert_eq!(parse_value("1M"), Some(1e6));
/// assert_eq!(parse_value("100 nF"), Some(100e-9));
/// assert_eq!(parse_value("5V1"), Some(5.1));
/// assert_eq!(parse_value("BC547"), None);
/// ```
pub fn parse_value(text: &str) -> Option<f64> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/lib.rs`

A circuit simulator you embed in Rust: build a circuit as a typed value,
solve it natively or in WebAssembly, and get back numbers checked against
ngspice. Pure Rust, no C libraries, no global state. Besides voltages and
currents it answers design questions: whether each part stays inside its
ratings ([`check_ratings`]) and whether a spec passes ([`check_specs`]).
Accuracy against ngspice is tabled in the
[repository](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/docs/ACCURACY.md).

`sindr` solves a [`Circuit`] — a list of components and a ground node —
and returns voltages, currents, and power for every component. The solver
picks the right path automatically:

- **Linear DC** — direct solve of the MNA system.
- **Nonlinear DC** — Newton–Raphson when diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs, etc. are present.
- **Transient** — Gear-2 (or trapezoidal or backward-Euler) timestepping
  when capacitors, inductors, or time-varying sources are present.
- **AC small-signal** — sinusoidal-steady-state via [`ac_analysis::solve_ac`].
- **Noise** — thermal, shot and flicker noise at an output (SPICE's
  `.noise`) via [`solve_noise`].
- **Transfer function** — DC small-signal gain, input and output
  resistance (SPICE's `.tf`) via [`solve_tf`].
- **Sensitivity** — derivative of a DC output with respect to each
  component and device-model parameter (SPICE's `.sens`) via
  [`solve_sensitivity`], and of a small-signal output at each frequency
  (`.sens ... ac`) via [`solve_ac_sensitivity`].
- **DC sweep** — operating point at each value of a swept voltage or current source,
  via [`fn@dc_sweep`].
- **Temperature sweep** — operating-point sweep over junction temperature
  via [`temperature_sweep`].

Device physics (diode, BJT, MOSFET, IGBT, JFET, varactor companion models)
live in the companion crate
[`sindr-devices`](https://crates.io/crates/sindr-devices), re-exported
whole as [`devices`], so `sindr::devices::mosfet::MosfetParams` and
`sindr::devices::inductor::InductorSaturation` need no second
dependency. The few enums you'll typically need ([`BjtKind`],
[`MosfetKind`], [`JfetKind`], etc.) are also at the root.

### Quick start

How much current does a red LED draw from 5 V through 220 Ω?

```
use sindr::{solve_circuit, Circuit, CircuitElement};
use sindr::element::{Led, Resistor, VoltageSource};

let circuit = Circuit::new("gnd", vec![
    CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["vcc".into(), "gnd".into()], voltage: 5.0, waveform: None }),
    CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["vcc".into(), "a".into()], resistance: 220.0 }),
    CircuitElement::Led(Led { id: "D1".into(), nodes: ["a".into(), "gnd".into()], color: "red".into(), temperature: 300.15 }),
]);
let result = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;
let led = result.component("D1").expect("D1 is in the circuit");
println!("{:.1} mA, {:.1} mW", led.current_through * 1e3, led.power * 1e3);

// About 1.8 V across the LED leaves about 3.2 V across R1.
assert!((led.current_through - 3.2 / 220.0).abs() < 1.5e-3);
```

### Data model and hierarchy

[`Circuit`] and everything in it lives in [`circuit`], [`design`] and
[`waveform`]. Besides its flat `components`, a
circuit can place [`Block`]s through [`Instance`]s, name `globals`, and
carry [`Part`] data (reference, symbol, footprint) the solver ignores.
Every analysis flattens the hierarchy first ([`Circuit::flatten`]: `X1.R1`,
`X1.mid`) and reports results under the flattened names. A broken
hierarchy is [`SimError::Design`].

### Capabilities

#### Analyses

| Analysis | Entry point | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Operating point (linear or nonlinear DC) | [`solve_op`], [`solve_circuit`] | Newton–Raphson for nonlinear devices. [`solve_op`] is SPICE's `.op` (C open, L shorted, sources at t = 0); [`solve_circuit`] runs a transient when the circuit has C, L or waveforms |
| Transient | [`solve_transient`] | Gear-2 (default), trapezoidal or backward Euler ([`IntegrationMethod`]), steps up to the [`TransientConfig`]'s `tstep`, shortened by truncation-error control and landing on waveform breakpoints. [`solve_circuit`] also takes this path when the circuit has C, L or waveform sources, choosing 5 τ and τ/50 itself |
| AC small-signal | [`ac_analysis::solve_ac`] | Needs an [`ac_analysis::AcConfig`]. [`solve_circuit`] **never** runs AC |
| Transfer function (`.tf`) | [`solve_tf`] | DC small-signal gain, input and output resistance at the operating point. Input: a voltage or current source; output: a node voltage or a voltage source's current ([`TfOutput`]) |
| DC sensitivity (`.sens`) | [`solve_sensitivity`] | Adjoint method: d(output)/d(parameter) for resistances, source values, VCVS, VCCS, CCVS and CCCS gains, and diode (IS, N, RS), BJT (BF, IS, BR, NF, NR, VAF) and MOSFET (KP, VTO, LAMBDA) model parameters |
| AC sensitivity (`.sens ... ac`) | [`solve_ac_sensitivity`] | One adjoint solve per frequency: d(output phasor)/d(parameter) for R, C, L, the four controlled-source gains, the stimulus's AC magnitude and the device-model parameters (diode CJO and TT too), with the bias point held fixed, as in ngspice |
| Noise (`.noise`) | [`solve_noise`] | Thermal, shot and flicker noise at an output voltage, referred to an input source, with a per-source breakdown and band totals |
| DC sweep | [`fn@dc_sweep`], [`dc_sweep_nested`] | One voltage or current source, or two nested (`.dc V1 … V2 …`); each point an operating point as [`solve_op`] solves it |
| Temperature sweep | [`temperature_sweep`] | Re-solves the operating point at each junction temperature |
| Solver options (`.options`, `.nodeset`) | [`Solver`], [`SolverOptions`] | Tolerances, iteration budget, gmin and source stepping, and a nodeset seeding Newton for every analysis's bias point. The free functions use the defaults |
| Self-heating | [`solve_circuit`], [`solve_transient`] | A part with [`Thermal`] data heats by its dissipation; DC iterates to a balance, transient carries a thermal RC. The small-signal analyses linearise at the heated bias point. Results in `junction_temperatures`; no balance is [`SimError::ThermalRunaway`] |
| Monte Carlo and corners | [`variation::monte_carlo`], [`variation::corners`] | Any analysis repeated with parts drawn within their tolerances (uniform or Gaussian, seeded) or at every low/high corner; each [`measure::Measurement`] per run, with mean, standard deviation, min, max and yield; specs and ratings at their worst run, with the condition behind it ([`variation::ratings_over`]) |
| Ratings check | [`check_ratings`] | Each part against its absolute maximum [`Ratings`], at the operating point or every transient step. Missing ratings report unverified |
| Measurements and specs (`.meas`) | [`check_specs`] | [`Measurement`]s (value at x, min/max/avg/RMS, crossings, delay, rise/fall, settling, −3 dB) on any result; [`Spec`] limits give pass/fail and margin |
| Fourier (`.four`) and FFT | [`Fourier`], [`Fft`] | Harmonics and THD of a transient signal at a fundamental, as ngspice's `.four` (last period, 200-point linear resample); a windowed (Hann, Hamming, Blackman, flat-top or none) radix-2 FFT of a uniform resample, scaled to peak amplitude |
| Initial conditions (`.ic`, `UIC`) | [`TransientConfig::with_initial_voltages`], [`TransientConfig::with_initial_current`], [`TransientConfig::with_start`] | The state a transient starts from: switched on at t = 0 (default) or the DC operating point ([`TransientStart`]) |

Not available: distortion, pole-zero,
periodic steady state, S-parameters, variable-order integration.

#### Device models

| Device | Model |
|---|---|
| Diode, LED, Schottky, photodiode | Shockley; IS and V_T = kT/q follow each device's `temperature` (SPICE IS(T), XTI = 3) |
| Zener | A SPICE diode with breakdown `BV = vz` at 5 mA and RS = 1 Ω |
| BJT (NPN/PNP) | Ebers–Moll with Early voltage; not Gummel–Poon |
| MOSFET (NMOS/PMOS) | SPICE Level 1 (Shichman–Hodges), body tied to source, SPICE-signed VTO (negative for an enhancement PMOS); no BSIM |
| JFET (N/P) | Shichman–Hodges square law; optional CGS/CGD as SPICE gate junctions (transient charge, AC at the bias point) |
| IGBT | MOSFET-like gate control, square-law collector current |
| Varactor | Voltage-dependent junction capacitance (transient; AC at the bias point) |
| Op-amp | VCVS of gain 1e5, or with an [`OpAmpModel`]: single-pole GBW, slew rate, rail clamp, output resistance, offset, bias current |
| Comparator | Gain 1e5, output clamped to its rails; no GBW, slew rate or hysteresis |
| Transformer | Coupled inductors; optional saturating core |
| Battery | Open-circuit voltage by state of charge behind R0 and an optional R1‖C1; state of charge falls with charge drawn ([`battery::BatteryParams`]; Li-ion and CR2032 presets) |
| Voltage regulator | Piecewise linear: dropout, quiescent current, current limit, line and load regulation ([`RegulatorParams`]; LM7805 and AMS1117 presets) |
| Crystal | Butterworth–Van Dyke: `Rm`–`Lm`–`Cm` beside `C0` ([`CrystalParams`]) |
| Ferrite bead | `R_dc` into `L ∥ R_ac` (∥ `C`) ([`FerriteBeadParams`]) |

Parameters are Rust structs, not SPICE `.model` cards.

#### Convergence aids

Junction voltage limiting and Newton damping on every nonlinear solve,
with junctions starting at their critical voltage, as in SPICE. Newton
converges only once node voltages and every diode, LED and BJT junction
voltage have settled. When plain Newton–Raphson fails, the DC solve retries with gmin stepping
(1e-2 S down to 1e-12 S), then with source stepping (every source ramped
up from zero); [`SimulationResult::convergence_aid`] says which one was
needed. A transient step whose Newton solve fails is retried at half the
step.

#### Netlist import for editors

[`import`] takes a schematic tool's netlist in the caller's own ids:
components with a kind, a value (`"4k7"`, `"100nF"`) and named
terminals, and nets of `(component, terminal)` pins. A [`import::Bench`]
adds what a schematic leaves out (ground, supplies, signal sources,
loads, the analysis), and [`import::simulate`] runs it. Results are
keyed by the caller's component and net ids, and every
[`import::ImportError`] names the part, net or bench item at fault.
Symbol ids (`resistor-iec`, `op-amp`) name kinds, a component's
terminal-name table comes in through [`import::ImportOptions`], and
parts sindr can't simulate import as listed black boxes.

#### SPICE input (feature `spice`)

[`spice`] reads a SPICE3 subset into a [`Circuit`]: R, L, C, V, I, D, Q,
M, J, B (behavioural, also E/G `VALUE=` and E/G/F/H `POLY`), linear E/G/F/H,
K (two coupled `L` lines) and X elements, with `[DC] v`,
`AC mag [phase]` and a waveform on V and I lines in any order;
`.subckt`, `.global`, `.model`, `.param`, `.include`, `.lib`,
`.ic`, `.nodeset`, `.options` and `.meas`; and the analysis cards `.op`, `.dc`,
`.ac`, `.tf`, `.sens`, `.noise` and `.tran`. `.model` cards fill in what
sindr's diode and BJT models have (diodes: `IS`, `N`, `RS`, `CJO`, `VJ`,
`M`, `FC`, `TT`, `BV`, `IBV`, `KF`, `AF`; BJTs: `IS`, `BF`, `BR`, `NF`,
`NR`, `VAF`, `KF`, `AF`; level-1 MOSFETs: `KP`, `VTO`, `LAMBDA`, `GAMMA`,
`PHI`, `LD`, `CGSO`, `CGDO`, `CGBO` and the drain–bulk junction; JFETs:
`VTO`, `BETA`, `CGS`, `CGD`, `PB`, `M`, `FC`), inside a `.subckt` or at the top level. Not read:
the `TABLE`/`LAPLACE` forms of E/G/F/H, and
couplings of more than two inductors.
[`spice::to_netlist`] writes a [`Circuit`] back out as a deck, controlled
and behavioural sources and `.subckt`s included.

#### Behavioural sources

[`CircuitElement::Behavioural`] is a voltage or current set by an
[`expression::Expression`] of node voltages, branch currents and time,
such as `v(a)*v(b)` or `1m*tanh(v(in)/26m)`. Newton stamps its exact
gradient (forward-mode automatic differentiation), AC linearises it at
the bias point, and transient reads `time`.

The full list of what sindr doesn't do is in
[LIMITATIONS.md](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/LIMITATIONS.md).

### Conventions

- **Ground node** must exist on at least one component. Its voltage is
  defined as 0 V — every other voltage is reported relative to it.
- **Node names** are arbitrary strings (`"0"`, `"gnd"`, `"vcc"`, …).
  Components share a node simply by referencing the same string.
- **SI units** throughout: V, A, Ω, F, H, s, K.
- **Sign conventions** are documented per [`CircuitElement`] variant.

### Cargo features

All on by default:

- `serde` — `Serialize`/`Deserialize` impls on the public types.
- `schemars` — `JsonSchema` on every serde type, for apps that publish
  the shape of a netlist, config or result to other tools.
- `spice` — the SPICE3 netlist parser and writer in [`spice`] (see
  below).
- `examples` — exposes [`get_examples`]: the built-in named circuits
  (voltage divider, BJT amp, RC transient, etc.) with ids and
  descriptions. The circuits themselves are always in [`examples`].
- `parallel` — [`variation`] spreads its runs over one thread per core,
  and runs them one after another where there are no threads (wasm).

`internals` is off by default and outside semver: it exposes the MNA
matrix for sindr's own benchmarks.

```toml
[dependencies]
sindr = "0.3"

# Only what you pick, here just serde:
sindr = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["serde"] }
```

### Transient results

A circuit with capacitors, inductors or waveform sources takes the
transient path, and [`SimulationResult::transient`] holds the time series.
[`solve_circuit`] picks the duration (5 τ) and step (τ/50) from the
circuit's time constants; to choose them, as SPICE's `.tran` does, call
[`solve_transient`] with a [`TransientConfig`].

```
use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, solve_circuit};
use sindr::element::{Capacitor, Resistor, VoltageSource};

// 5 V step into R = 1 kΩ, C = 1 µF: τ = 1 ms.
let circuit = Circuit {
    ground_node: "0".into(),
    components: vec![
        CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
            id: "V1".into(),
            nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
            voltage: 5.0,
            waveform: None,
        }),
        CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
            id: "R1".into(),
            nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()],
            resistance: 1_000.0,
        }),
        CircuitElement::Capacitor(Capacitor {
            id: "C1".into(),
            nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()],
            capacitance: 1e-6,
        }),
    ],
    ..Default::default()
};

let result = solve_circuit(&circuit).unwrap();
let tran = result.transient.expect("reactive circuit takes the transient path");

// The capacitor charges from 0 V towards 5 V.
let first = &tran.timesteps[0];
let last = tran.timesteps.last().unwrap();
assert!(first.voltage("out").unwrap() < 1.0);
assert!((last.voltage("out").unwrap() - 5.0).abs() < 0.1);
```

### CSV export

[`TransientData::to_csv`], [`AcResult::to_csv`],
[`DcSweepResult::to_csv`] and [`TempSweepResult::to_csv`] write one row
per point: the scale (time, frequency, swept value or temperature)
first, then a column per node voltage, `v(<node>)` with nodes in name
order, then for real-valued results a column per component current,
`i(<id>)`, in circuit order. AC writes each node voltage as two columns,
`re(v(<node>))` and `im(v(<node>))`.

Numbers are written so they read back as the same `f64`. A value missing
from a row is an empty field. Names that need it are quoted as RFC 4180
has it. Lines end in `\n`.

### SPICE netlist input

Parsing SPICE3 `.cir` decks into a [`Circuit`] is the `spice` feature,
on by default:

```toml
[dependencies]
sindr = "0.3"
```

(`no_run`: it reads `amp.cir`, which doesn't exist where doctests run.)

```no_run
let netlist = sindr::spice::parse_file("amp.cir")?;
let result = sindr::solve_circuit(&netlist.circuit)?;
```

See the [`spice`] module for a runnable example, the supported subset and
strictness options.

## `sindr/src/loop_gain.rs`

Loop gain and stability margins at a break point, by Tian's method.

The loop is broken by a probe: an independent voltage source (normally
0 V) in series with the loop, its `nodes[1]` on the side that drives
the loop (an amplifier output, say) and its `nodes[0]` on the side that
is driven (the feedback network). Nothing else is cut, so the loading
of both sides stays as it is.

At each frequency two small-signal solves inject a test signal at the
probe: a unit voltage in series (the probe's own value), then a unit
current into `nodes[0]` with the probe a short. With `v` the voltage at
`nodes[0]` in the first and `i` the probe's current (from `nodes[0]`
through it to `nodes[1]`) in the second, the loop gain is

```text
  T = (i − v) / (v + 1 − i)
```

This is Middlebrook's double-injection result,
`T = (Tv·Ti − 1) / (Tv + Ti + 2)` with `Tv` and `Ti` the voltage and
current loop gains measured at the same point, in the single-probe form
Tian, Kolen et al. gave. It is exact for loops that carry signal both
ways through the break point (finite source and load impedances,
bidirectional feedback), where a voltage or current injection alone is
only an approximation.

`T` is the return ratio: positive at low frequency for negative feedback,
and the closed-loop response goes as `1/(1 + T)`.

```rust
/// Loop-gain analysis configuration. Build one with [`LoopGainConfig::new`].
pub struct LoopGainConfig {
    /// Id of the probe: an independent voltage source in series with the
    /// loop, `nodes[1]` on the driving side and `nodes[0]` on the driven
    /// side. Its DC value biases the circuit as usual; 0 V leaves it out.
    pub probe: String,
    /// Start frequency (Hz).
    pub f_start: f64,
    /// Stop frequency (Hz).
    pub f_stop: f64,
    /// Number of frequency points, both ends included.
    pub num_points: usize,
    /// Frequency spacing. Default logarithmic.
    pub spacing: FrequencySpacing,
}

impl LoopGainConfig {
    /// The loop gain at the probe `probe`, at `num_points` frequencies from
    /// `f_start` to `f_stop` (Hz), log-spaced.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::loop_gain::LoopGainConfig;
    ///
    /// let config = LoopGainConfig::new("Vprobe", 1.0, 100e6, 801);
    /// assert_eq!(config.probe, "Vprobe");
    /// ```
    pub fn new(probe: impl Into<String>, f_start: f64, f_stop: f64, num_points: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets the frequency spacing.
    pub fn with_spacing(mut self, spacing: FrequencySpacing) -> Self { … }
}

/// The loop gain at one frequency.
pub struct LoopGainPoint {
    /// Frequency (Hz).
    pub frequency: f64,
    /// The loop gain `T(j·2πf)`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "schemars", schemars(with = "[f64; 2]"))]
    pub gain: Complex64,
    /// Phase of `T` (degrees), unwrapped along the sweep from the first
    /// point's value in (−180°, 180°].
    pub phase_deg: f64,
}

impl LoopGainPoint {
    /// `|T|` in dB.
    pub fn gain_db(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// Result of a loop-gain analysis.
pub struct LoopGainResult {
    /// The loop gain at every frequency of the sweep.
    pub points: Vec<LoopGainPoint>,
    /// Frequencies (Hz) where `|T|` crosses 1 (0 dB), lowest first.
    pub gain_crossovers: Vec<f64>,
    /// Frequencies (Hz) where the unwrapped phase of `T` crosses −180°
    /// (or −540°, …), lowest first.
    pub phase_crossovers: Vec<f64>,
    /// Phase margin (degrees): `180° + ∠T` at the gain crossover, the
    /// smallest over all of them. `None` when `|T|` never crosses 1 in the
    /// sweep.
    pub phase_margin_deg: Option<f64>,
    /// Gain margin (dB): `−20·log₁₀|T|` at the phase crossover, the
    /// smallest over all of them. `None` when the phase never reaches
    /// −180° in the sweep.
    pub gain_margin_db: Option<f64>,
    /// Configuration used to produce this result.
    pub config: LoopGainConfig,
}

/// Runs a loop-gain analysis at a probe, with phase and gain margins.
///
/// # Algorithm
///
/// 1. Solve the DC operating point and linearise every nonlinear element
///    at it, as [`solve_ac`](crate::ac_analysis::solve_ac) does.
/// 2. At each frequency, inject a unit voltage at the probe and then a
///    unit current beside it, and combine the two responses into the loop
///    gain `T` by Tian's formula (see the [module documentation](self)).
/// 3. Find where `|T|` crosses 1 and where its unwrapped phase crosses
///    −180° between sweep points, refine each crossing by bisection on `T`
///    itself (so a margin is exact, not interpolated), and read the
///    margins there.
///
/// The phase is unwrapped along the sweep, so the sweep must be dense
/// enough that the phase moves less than 180° between points.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if the sweep is invalid (as for
///   [`AcConfig`]), or the probe is not an independent voltage source with
///   neither terminal on ground. Checked before the DC solve
/// - Any [`SimError`] from the DC operating-point solve
/// - [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the linearised system is singular at
///   some frequency
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, OpAmpModel};
/// use sindr::loop_gain::{solve_loop_gain, LoopGainConfig};
/// use sindr::element::{OpAmp, Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// // A follower on a single-pole op-amp (100 dB, 1 MHz GBW), broken at
/// // its output: T = A(s), phase margin just over 90°.
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::OpAmp(OpAmp {
///             id: "U1".into(),
///             nodes: ["0".into(), "fb".into(), "out".into()],
///             v_pos: 15.0,
///             v_neg: -15.0,
///             model: Some(OpAmpModel::default()),
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "Vprobe".into(),
///             nodes: ["fb".into(), "out".into()],
///             voltage: 0.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "RL".into(),
///             nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 10e3,
///         }),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// let lg = solve_loop_gain(&circuit, &LoopGainConfig::new("Vprobe", 1.0, 100e6, 81))?;
/// let pm = lg.phase_margin_deg.unwrap();
/// assert!((pm - 90.0).abs() < 1e-3);
/// assert!((lg.gain_crossovers[0] - 1e6).abs() < 1.0);
/// assert!(lg.gain_margin_db.is_none());
/// # Ok::<(), sindr::SimError>(())
/// ```
///
pub fn solve_loop_gain(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    config: &LoopGainConfig,
) -> Result<LoopGainResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/measure.rs`

Measurements and specs: a verdict on a result, and the reason when it
fails.

A [`Measurement`] turns a result into one number: the value at a time or
frequency, a min, max, average or RMS, a crossing time, a delay, a rise
or fall time, a settling time or a −3 dB point. A [`Spec`] adds limits to
a measurement, and [`check_specs`] reports, for each spec, the measured
value, its limits, pass or fail and the margin left. The ratings checks
([`check_ratings`](crate::check_ratings)) can ride along in the same
[`SpecReport`].

Measurements work on anything [`Measurable`]:

| Result | x axis |
|---|---|
| [`SimulationResult`] with a transient | time (s) |
| [`SimulationResult`] without one (DC operating point) | a single point at x = 0 |
| [`AcResult`] | frequency (Hz) |
| [`DcSweepResult`] | the swept source's value (V or A) |
| [`TempSweepResult`] | temperature (K) |

A [`Signal`] is a node voltage (`v(out)`), a voltage between two nodes
(`v(a, b)`) or a component's current (`i(R1)`, its
[`ComponentResult::current_through`](crate::ComponentResult::current_through)
direction). Its [`View`] picks the real value (the magnitude on an AC
result), dB (`20·log10|x|`) or phase in degrees (AC only, unwrapped
along the sweep).

SPICE `.meas` cards are parsed onto measurements by the `spice` feature
(`ParsedNetlist::measurements`).

```
use sindr::measure::{check_specs, Measure, Measurement, Signal, Spec, Stat};
use sindr::{solve_transient, Circuit, CircuitElement, TransientConfig};
use sindr::element::{Capacitor, Resistor, VoltageSource};

// RC low-pass, τ = 1 ms, charging towards 5 V.
let circuit = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![
        CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource { id: "V1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()], voltage: 5.0, waveform: None }),
        CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor { id: "R1".into(), nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()], resistance: 1e3 }),
        CircuitElement::Capacitor(Capacitor { id: "C1".into(), nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()], capacitance: 1e-6 }),
    ],
);
let result = solve_transient(&circuit, &TransientConfig::new(10e-3, 10e-6))?;

let specs = [
    Spec::new(Measurement::new("vout_final", Measure::stat(Signal::v("out"), Stat::Final)))
        .between(4.9, 5.1),
    // 10–90 % rise of an RC is 2.2·τ.
    Spec::new(Measurement::new("rise", Measure::rise_time(Signal::v("out")))).at_most(2.5e-3),
];
let report = check_specs(&result, &specs);
assert!(report.passed(), "{report:?}");
let rise = report.checks[1].value.unwrap();
assert!((rise - 2.197e-3).abs() < 0.05e-3);
```

```rust
/// What a signal reads: a voltage or a current.
pub enum Quantity {
    /// Voltage at `node` (V), against `reference` or ground.
    Voltage {
        /// Node name.
        node: String,
        /// Reference node; `None` is ground.
        reference: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Current through a component (A), in the direction of its
    /// [`ComponentResult::current_through`](crate::ComponentResult::current_through).
    /// Falls back to [`SimulationResult::branch_currents`] for an element
    /// without a component result. Not available on AC results.
    Current {
        /// Component id, flattened (`X1.R3`).
        component: String,
    },
}

/// How a signal's value is read.
pub enum View {
    /// The value itself; the magnitude on an AC result.
    #[default]
    Value,
    /// `20·log10|x|`, in dB. On AC this is absolute (SPICE's `vdb`), not
    /// relative to the source amplitude.
    Db,
    /// Phase in degrees, AC only, unwrapped along the sweep so a phase that
    /// keeps falling past −180° reads −190°, not +170°.
    Phase,
}

/// A signal to measure: a [`Quantity`] read through a [`View`].
pub struct Signal {
    /// Voltage or current.
    pub quantity: Quantity,
    /// Value, dB or phase.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub view: View,
}

impl Signal {
    /// Voltage at `node` against ground: `v(node)`.
    pub fn v(node: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// Voltage between two nodes, `node − reference`: `v(node, reference)`.
    pub fn v_diff(node: impl Into<String>, reference: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// Current through a component: `i(component)`.
    pub fn i(component: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// The same signal in dB.
    pub fn db(mut self) -> Self { … }

    /// The same signal's phase, in degrees (AC only).
    pub fn phase(mut self) -> Self { … }
}

/// A result a [`Measurement`] can be taken on: one of the results in the
/// [module docs](self). Sealed: it can't be implemented outside sindr.
pub trait Measurable: sealed::Sealed {
    /// The signal's samples as `(x, y)` pairs, in ascending x.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The reason it can't be read: an unknown node, a phase on a
    /// transient.
    fn trace(&self, signal: &Signal) -> Result<Vec<(f64, f64)>, String>;
}

/// A statistic over a signal, within the measurement's window.
pub enum Stat {
    /// Smallest sample.
    Min,
    /// Largest sample.
    Max,
    /// Mean over x, by trapezoids, so uneven time steps don't skew it.
    Avg,
    /// Root mean square over x, by trapezoids of y².
    Rms,
    /// Largest minus smallest sample.
    PeakToPeak,
    /// Integral over x, by trapezoids (V·s for a voltage on a transient).
    Integral,
    /// The last sample: the end of a transient, the only point of a DC
    /// operating point.
    Final,
}

/// Which way a signal crosses a level.
pub enum Edge {
    /// Going up through the level.
    Rise,
    /// Going down through the level.
    Fall,
    /// Either way.
    Cross,
}

/// Which crossing counts.
pub enum Occurrence {
    /// The nth one, from 1, in ascending x.
    Nth(usize),
    /// The last one.
    Last,
}

/// A signal crossing a level: SPICE's `WHEN v(out)=2.5 RISE=2`.
pub struct Crossing {
    /// The signal.
    pub signal: Signal,
    /// The level it crosses, in the signal's unit.
    pub level: f64,
    /// Rising, falling or either.
    pub edge: Edge,
    /// Which crossing.
    pub occurrence: Occurrence,
}

impl Crossing {
    /// The first crossing of `level`, either way.
    pub fn new(signal: Signal, level: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Only rising crossings count.
    pub fn rising(mut self) -> Self { … }

    /// Only falling crossings count.
    pub fn falling(mut self) -> Self { … }

    /// The nth crossing, from 1.
    pub fn nth(mut self, n: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// The last crossing.
    pub fn last(mut self) -> Self { … }
}

/// What a [`Measurement`] measures. Each variant carries its own signal.
pub enum Measure {
    /// The signal's value at `at`, interpolated linearly: SPICE's
    /// `FIND v(out) AT=1m`.
    Find {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// Where, on the result's x axis.
        at: f64,
    },
    /// A statistic over the window: SPICE's `AVG`, `RMS`, `MIN`, `MAX`,
    /// `PP` and `INTEG`.
    Stat {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// Which statistic.
        stat: Stat,
    },
    /// The x at which a crossing happens: SPICE's `WHEN`.
    When(Crossing),
    /// `x(targ) − x(trig)`: SPICE's `TRIG … TARG …`, a propagation delay.
    Delay {
        /// Where the interval starts.
        trig: Crossing,
        /// Where it ends.
        targ: Crossing,
    },
    /// Rise or fall time between two fractions of the signal's swing over
    /// the window (0.1 and 0.9 for the usual 10–90 %). For a rise, from the
    /// last time it rose through `low` before it first rose through `high`;
    /// a fall the other way round.
    Transition {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// [`Edge::Rise`] or [`Edge::Fall`].
        edge: Edge,
        /// Lower fraction of the swing, 0 to 1.
        low: f64,
        /// Upper fraction of the swing, 0 to 1.
        high: f64,
    },
    /// How long, from the start of the window, until the signal stays
    /// within `band` of its final value (or of `target`) to the end.
    Settling {
        /// The signal.
        signal: Signal,
        /// Allowed error either side, in the signal's unit.
        band: f64,
        /// The value it settles to; `None` takes the last sample.
        target: Option<f64>,
    },
    /// The first x after the peak where the signal, in dB, has fallen
    /// `drop_db` below that peak: the −3 dB point of a low-pass or the
    /// upper one of a band-pass, with `drop_db` 3.
    Bandwidth {
        /// The signal; read in dB whatever its view.
        signal: Signal,
        /// How far below the peak, in dB.
        drop_db: f64,
    },
}

impl Measure {
    /// A statistic of a signal.
    pub fn stat(signal: Signal, stat: Stat) -> Self { … }

    /// The signal's value at `at`.
    pub fn find(signal: Signal, at: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// 10–90 % rise time.
    pub fn rise_time(signal: Signal) -> Self { … }

    /// 90–10 % fall time.
    pub fn fall_time(signal: Signal) -> Self { … }

    /// Settling time to within `band` of the final value.
    pub fn settling(signal: Signal, band: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The −3 dB point.
    pub fn bandwidth(signal: Signal) -> Self { … }
}

/// A named measurement, optionally limited to a window of x.
pub struct Measurement {
    /// Name, reported back with the value.
    pub name: String,
    /// What is measured.
    pub measure: Measure,
    /// Start of the window on the x axis; `None` is the start of the result.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub from: Option<f64>,
    /// End of the window; `None` is the end of the result.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub to: Option<f64>,
}

impl Measurement {
    /// A measurement over the whole result.
    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, measure: Measure) -> Self { … }

    /// Limit it to `from ≤ x ≤ to`.
    pub fn window(mut self, from: f64, to: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Take the measurement on a result.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`SimError::Measurement`] when it can't be taken: an unknown node or
    /// component, a window outside the result, a level never crossed.
    pub fn on(&self, result: &impl Measurable) -> Result<f64, SimError> { … }
}

/// A measurement with limits: `V(vout)` 4.9–5.1 V, ripple under 50 mV.
pub struct Spec {
    /// What is measured; its name names the spec.
    pub measurement: Measurement,
    /// Lowest value that passes, inclusive. `None` for no lower limit.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub min: Option<f64>,
    /// Highest value that passes, inclusive. `None` for no upper limit.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub max: Option<f64>,
}

impl Spec {
    /// A spec with no limits yet. With none it passes whenever the
    /// measurement can be taken, which records a value in the report.
    pub fn new(measurement: Measurement) -> Self { … }

    /// Pass when `min ≤ value ≤ max`.
    pub fn between(mut self, min: f64, max: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Pass when `value ≥ min`.
    pub fn at_least(mut self, min: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Pass when `value ≤ max`.
    pub fn at_most(mut self, max: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Measure on a result and judge it.
    pub fn check(&self, result: &impl Measurable) -> SpecCheck { … }
}

/// How a spec did.
pub enum SpecStatus {
    /// Within its limits.
    Pass,
    /// Outside them.
    Fail,
    /// The measurement couldn't be taken; [`SpecCheck::reason`] says why.
    /// Never counted as a pass.
    Unmeasured,
}

/// One spec checked against one result.
pub struct SpecCheck {
    /// The measurement's name.
    pub name: String,
    /// The measured value, in the signal's unit; `None` when unmeasured.
    pub value: Option<f64>,
    /// Lower limit.
    pub min: Option<f64>,
    /// Upper limit.
    pub max: Option<f64>,
    /// Distance to the nearer limit, in the signal's unit: positive inside
    /// the limits, negative outside. `None` with no limits or no value.
    pub margin: Option<f64>,
    /// Pass, fail or unmeasured.
    pub status: SpecStatus,
    /// Why the measurement couldn't be taken.
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

/// Every spec's verdict, with the ratings checks alongside when attached.
pub struct SpecReport {
    /// One entry per spec, in the order given.
    pub checks: Vec<SpecCheck>,
    /// The ratings checks, when attached with [`with_ratings`](Self::with_ratings).
    pub ratings: Option<RatingsReport>,
}

impl SpecReport {
    /// Attach a ratings report, so [`passed`](Self::passed) also needs every
    /// part within its ratings.
    pub fn with_ratings(mut self, ratings: RatingsReport) -> Self { … }

    /// Join another report, such as the specs checked on a second analysis.
    /// Its ratings checks are appended to this one's.
    pub fn merge(mut self, other: SpecReport) -> Self { … }

    /// `true` only when every spec passed and, with ratings attached, every
    /// part is within them ([`RatingsReport::is_safe`]).
    pub fn passed(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// Specs outside their limits.
    pub fn failed(&self) -> Vec<&SpecCheck> { … }

    /// Specs whose measurement couldn't be taken.
    pub fn unmeasured(&self) -> Vec<&SpecCheck> { … }

    /// The check for one spec, by name.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&SpecCheck> { … }
}

/// Check every spec against a result.
///
/// A measurement that can't be taken is [`SpecStatus::Unmeasured`] with the
/// reason, not an error, so one bad spec doesn't hide the others' verdicts.
pub fn check_specs(result: &impl Measurable, specs: &[Spec]) -> SpecReport { … }
```

## `sindr/src/noise.rs`

Noise analysis, SPICE's `.noise`: thermal, shot and flicker noise at an
output voltage, and referred back to an input source.

Every noise source is a current between two nodes with a power spectral
density (A²/Hz), set by the DC operating point:

| Component | Source | Between | PSD |
|---|---|---|---|
| resistor, potentiometer (each half), thermistor, photoresistor | thermal | its terminals | `4kT/R` |
| diode, LED, Schottky, Zener, photodiode | shot | anode–cathode | `2q·\|I\|` |
| diode with a `model` | flicker | anode–cathode | `KF·\|I\|^AF / f` |
| BJT | shot | collector–emitter, base–emitter | `2q·\|Ic\|`, `2q·\|Ib\|` |
| BJT with a `model` | flicker | base–emitter | `KF·\|Ib\|^AF / f` |
| MOSFET | channel thermal | drain–source | `(8/3)·kT·gm` |
| MOSFET | flicker | drain–source | `KF·\|Id\|^AF / f` |
| JFET | channel thermal | drain–source | `(8/3)·kT·gm` |

`T` is 300.15 K (27 °C), as in SPICE, except that a thermistor's thermal
noise uses its own temperature. Sources, controlled sources, op-amps,
regulators, switches, fuses, IGBTs and a diode's series resistance are
noiseless.

At each frequency one adjoint solve, `Aᵀ·y = e_out`, gives the transfer
from a unit current at every node to the output. Each source then adds
`|y_p − y_q|²·PSD` to the output's PSD. One forward solve from the input
source gives the gain that refers the output noise back to the input.
Integrated noise assumes each PSD follows a power law between points, as
ngspice does.

```rust
/// Noise analysis configuration: SPICE's
/// `.noise V(output[,reference]) input_source {dec|lin} points f_start f_stop`.
/// Build one with [`NoiseConfig::new`] and its `with_*` setters.
pub struct NoiseConfig {
    /// The output node.
    pub output: String,
    /// The node the output is measured against; ground when `None`.
    pub reference: Option<String>,
    /// The independent voltage or current source noise is referred back to.
    pub input_source: String,
    /// Start frequency (Hz), above 0: flicker noise is infinite at DC.
    pub f_start: f64,
    /// Stop frequency (Hz).
    pub f_stop: f64,
    /// Number of frequency points, both ends included.
    pub num_points: usize,
    /// Frequency spacing; logarithmic is `num_points` in total.
    pub spacing: FrequencySpacing,
}

impl NoiseConfig {
    /// Noise at node `output` against ground, referred back to the
    /// independent source `input_source`, at `num_points` frequencies from
    /// `f_start` to `f_stop` (Hz), both included. Spacing defaults to
    /// [`FrequencySpacing::Logarithmic`].
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::ac_analysis::FrequencySpacing;
    /// use sindr::NoiseConfig;
    ///
    /// // SPICE `.noise v(out,ref) V1 lin 100 1k 100k`.
    /// let config = NoiseConfig::new("out", "V1", 1e3, 1e5, 100)
    ///     .with_reference("ref")
    ///     .with_spacing(FrequencySpacing::Linear);
    /// assert_eq!(config.reference.as_deref(), Some("ref"));
    /// ```
    pub fn new(
        output: impl Into<String>,
        input_source: impl Into<String>,
        f_start: f64,
        f_stop: f64,
        num_points: usize,
    ) -> Self { … }

    /// Measure the output against node `reference` instead of ground.
    pub fn with_reference(mut self, reference: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// Space the frequencies by `spacing` instead of logarithmically.
    pub fn with_spacing(mut self, spacing: FrequencySpacing) -> Self { … }
}

/// The physical mechanism behind a noise source.
pub enum NoiseKind {
    /// Johnson–Nyquist noise of a resistance, or a FET channel's.
    Thermal,
    /// Shot noise of a current crossing a junction.
    Shot,
    /// Flicker (1/f) noise.
    Flicker,
}

/// One noise source in the circuit.
pub struct NoiseSource {
    /// Component id (flattened).
    pub component: String,
    /// Which mechanism.
    pub kind: NoiseKind,
    /// Which current it sits on, for parts with more than one: `"ic"`,
    /// `"ib"`, `"top"`/`"bottom"` for a potentiometer; empty otherwise.
    pub branch: String,
}

/// Noise at one frequency.
pub struct NoisePoint {
    /// Frequency (Hz).
