    /// assert!((last - 10e-3).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn transient_config(&self) -> Option<crate::TransientConfig> { … }

    /// The [`TfConfig`](crate::TfConfig) for a `.tf` request, to pass to
    /// [`solve_tf`](crate::solve_tf); `None` for any other analysis.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* divider\nV1 in 0 1\nR1 in out 1k\nR2 out 0 3k\n.tf v(out) v1\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.analyses[0].tf_config().unwrap();
    /// let tf = sindr::solve_tf(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    /// assert!((tf.gain - 0.75).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// assert!((tf.output_resistance - 750.0).abs() < 1e-9);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn tf_config(&self) -> Option<crate::TfConfig> { … }

    /// The [`AcConfig`](crate::ac_analysis::AcConfig) for an `.ac` request,
    /// driving `source_id` at 1 V and 0°; `None` for any other analysis.
    /// [`ParsedNetlist::ac_config`](crate::spice::ParsedNetlist::ac_config)
    /// takes the source and its stimulus from the deck's `AC` spec instead.
    ///
    /// The frequencies are ngspice's. A `lin` sweep is `points` from
    /// `fstart` to `fstop`. A `dec` sweep over a decade or more is
    /// ⌊points·decades⌋ equal log steps from `fstart` to `fstop`, so
    /// `.ac dec 10 1 50` is 17 points. Any other `dec` or `oct` sweep steps
    /// from `fstart` by 10^(1/points) or 2^(1/points) and stops at the last
    /// point not past `fstop` (within ngspice's 0.1 % tolerance), so the
    /// config's `f_stop` can fall short of the card's: `.ac oct 3 1 10`
    /// ends at 8 Hz.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* rc\nV1 in 0 0\nR1 in out 1k\nC1 out 0 1u\n.ac dec 10 1 100k\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.analyses[0].ac_config("v1").unwrap();
    /// assert_eq!(config.num_points, 51);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn ac_config(&self, source_id: &str) -> Option<crate::ac_analysis::AcConfig> { … }

    /// The [`NoiseConfig`](crate::NoiseConfig) for a `.noise` request, to
    /// pass to [`solve_noise`](crate::solve_noise); `None` for any other
    /// analysis.
    ///
    /// The frequencies are ngspice's: a `lin` sweep is `points` from
    /// `fstart` to `fstop`; a `dec` or `oct` sweep steps from `fstart` by
    /// 10^(1/points) or 2^(1/points) and stops at the last point not past
    /// `fstop` (within ngspice's 0.1 % tolerance). The config's `f_stop` is
    /// that last point, so `.noise ... dec 10 1 50` ends at 10^1.6 ≈ 39.8 Hz.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* rc\nV1 in 0 0\nR1 in out 1k\nC1 out 0 1u\n.noise v(out) v1 dec 10 1 100k\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.analyses[0].noise_config().unwrap();
    /// assert_eq!(config.num_points, 51);
    /// let noise = sindr::solve_noise(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    /// // 1 kΩ's thermal noise, √(4kTR), well below the pole.
    /// assert!((noise.points[0].output_density() - 4.0713e-9).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn noise_config(&self) -> Option<crate::NoiseConfig> { … }

    /// The [`PzConfig`](crate::PzConfig) for a `.pz` request, to pass to
    /// [`solve_pz`](crate::solve_pz); `None` for any other analysis.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* rc\nV1 in 0 0\nR1 in out 1k\nC1 out 0 1u\n.pz in 0 out 0 vol pz\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.analyses[0].pz_config().unwrap();
    /// let pz = sindr::solve_pz(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    /// // One pole at −1/RC.
    /// assert!((pz.poles[0].re + 1_000.0).abs() < 1e-9);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn pz_config(&self) -> Option<crate::PzConfig> { … }

    /// The [`SensConfig`](crate::SensConfig) for a `.sens` request, to pass
    /// to [`solve_sensitivity`](crate::solve_sensitivity); `None` for any
    /// other analysis.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* divider\nV1 in 0 4\nR1 in out 1k\nR2 out 0 3k\n.sens v(out)\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.analyses[0].sens_config().unwrap();
    /// let sens = sindr::solve_sensitivity(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    /// assert!((sens.get("v1").unwrap().sensitivity - 0.75).abs() < 1e-12);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn sens_config(&self) -> Option<crate::SensConfig> { … }

    /// The [`AcSensConfig`](crate::AcSensConfig) for a `.sens ... ac`
    /// request, with the AC stimulus on `source_id` at 1 V and 0°, to pass to
    /// [`solve_ac_sensitivity`](crate::solve_ac_sensitivity); `None` for any
    /// other analysis. The frequencies are those of the same `.ac` card
    /// ([`ac_config`](Self::ac_config)).
    /// [`ParsedNetlist::ac_sens_config`](crate::spice::ParsedNetlist::ac_sens_config)
    /// takes the stimulus from the deck's `AC` spec instead.
    pub fn ac_sens_config(&self, source_id: &str) -> Option<crate::AcSensConfig> { … }
}

/// Frequency-axis spacing for an AC sweep.
pub enum AcSweep {
    /// `dec` — points per decade, log spacing.
    Dec,
    /// `oct` — points per octave, log spacing.
    Oct,
    /// `lin` — total points, linear spacing.
    Lin,
}

/// Which analysis a `.meas` card measures.
pub enum MeasureAnalysis {
    /// `.meas tran`: on the `.tran` result, x is time (s).
    Tran,
    /// `.meas ac`: on the `.ac` result, x is frequency (Hz).
    Ac,
    /// `.meas dc`: on the `.dc` sweep, x is the swept source's value.
    Dc,
}

/// A `.meas` card: the analysis it applies to and the measurement.
///
/// Take it with [`Measurement::on`](crate::measure::Measurement::on) on that
/// analysis's result, or wrap it in a [`Spec`](crate::measure::Spec) to give
/// it limits.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::spice::{parse_str, MeasureAnalysis};
///
/// let deck = "* rc\nV1 in 0 1\nR1 in out 1k\nC1 out 0 1u\n.tran 10u 5m uic\n\
///             .meas tran t_half when v(out)=0.5 rise=1\n.end\n";
/// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
/// let meas = &netlist.measurements[0];
/// assert_eq!(meas.analysis, MeasureAnalysis::Tran);
/// let result = sindr::solve_transient(&netlist.circuit, &netlist.analyses[0].transient_config().unwrap())?;
/// // An RC step crosses half way at τ·ln 2.
/// let t = meas.measurement.on(&result)?;
/// assert!((t - 1e-3 * std::f64::consts::LN_2).abs() < 2e-5);
/// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
/// ```
pub struct MeasureRequest {
    /// The analysis whose result it measures.
    pub analysis: MeasureAnalysis,
    /// The measurement, named as the card names it.
    pub measurement: crate::measure::Measurement,
}
```

## `sindr/src/spice/ast.rs`

Internal AST produced by the lexer/parser before lowering to [`crate::Circuit`].

Everything in here is `pub(crate)`. These types are the contract between
the parser stage (plans 02-03) and the lowering stage (plans 03-04). They
are deliberately broader than what `sindr` accepts so that we can produce
good error messages on unsupported constructs rather than failing the
grammar.

## `sindr/src/spice/build.rs`

Lift flattened raw forms ([`crate::spice::flatten::Flattened`]) into the public
[`crate::spice::ParsedNetlist`] (sindr `Circuit` + `AnalysisRequest`s).

Per-element mapping rules:

* **R / L / C** — evaluate `value` against the element's scope snapshot
  and emit the matching `CircuitElement`.
* **V / I** — evaluate the optional DC term and translate the optional
  `RawWaveform` (PULSE / SIN / PWL) into `crate::Waveform`. SPICE's
  `td/tr/tf/pw/period` for PULSE map directly; SIN's `theta` (damping)
  is dropped with a warning in lenient mode and an error in strict mode
  when non-zero.
* **D** — look up `.model`; kind must be `D`. Other kinds raise
  `UnsupportedModelType`. `IS`, `N`, `RS`, `CJO` (alias `CJ0`, `CJ`),
  `VJ` (alias `PB`), `M` (alias `MJ`), `FC`, `TT`, `BV` and `IBV` fill a
  `DiodeModel`.
* **Q** — look up `.model`; kind must be `NPN` or `PNP`. `BF` sets `bf`;
  `IS`, `BR`, `NF`, `NR` and `VAF` (alias `VA`) fill a `BjtModel`.
  Any other D or Q card parameter is a warning in lenient mode and an
  error in strict mode, naming it. **SPICE node
  order on the Q line is `[c, b, e]`; sindr's `Bjt::nodes` is
  `[b, c, e]`** — transpose at this layer.
* **E / G / F / H** — evaluate the gain and emit `Vcvs` / `Vccs` /
  `Cccs` / `Ccvs` with the nodes as written (sindr uses SPICE's
  directions). An `F`/`H` control must be a `V` line in the same scope.
* **K** — after its scope's elements are built, replace the two `L`
  lines it names with one `Transformer` named after the `K` line.
* **X** — should not appear in `flat.elements` (the flattener already
  expanded them). Hitting one here is an internal bug.

## `sindr/src/spice/error.rs`

Error and warning types for the SPICE parser.

[`SpiceParseError`] is a [`miette::Diagnostic`]: every span-bearing variant
carries the source text and a labelled span so callers using
`miette = { features = ["fancy"] }` get pretty terminal output for free.

`unused_assignments` is suppressed module-wide because miette's
`Diagnostic` derive expands to a chain of `let mut x = ...; x = ...;`
per field that fires the lint for every variant.

```rust
/// Fatal errors raised while parsing a SPICE netlist.
///
/// Every variant that points at a location in source carries both the
/// [`NamedSource`] and a [`SourceSpan`] so it renders nicely under
/// `miette`'s fancy reporter. That includes errors found after parsing
/// (undefined models and parameters, parameter cycles, bad analysis-card
/// values): they point at the offending line, inside the `.include`d file
/// when that is where it is.
pub enum SpiceParseError {
    /// First character of an element line was not a recognised device prefix.
    #[error("unknown device prefix '{prefix}'")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::unknown_device),
        help("supported device prefixes: R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, M, J, B, E, G, F, H, K, X")
    )]
    UnknownDevice {
        /// The unrecognised prefix character.
        prefix: char,
        /// Source text the error was found in.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span pointing at the offending prefix.
        #[label("unknown prefix")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A `.<card>` directive that the parser does not recognise.
    #[error("unknown control card '.{card}'")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::unknown_card),
        help("supported cards: .subckt/.ends, .model, .param, .include, .lib, .tran, .dc, .ac, .op, .tf, .sens, .noise, .pz, .ic, .nodeset, .end")
    )]
    UnknownCard {
        /// The card name without its leading `.`.
        card: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the card token.
        #[label("unknown card")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// Device prefix is recognised by SPICE but not implemented by the parser.
    #[error("unsupported device '{device}'")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::unsupported_device),
        help("the parser currently supports: R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, M, J, B, E, G, F, H, K, X, with the POLY form of E/G/F/H and the VALUE form of E/G. The TABLE/LAPLACE forms are not implemented yet.")
    )]
    UnsupportedDevice {
        /// Element id that triggered the error.
        device: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the unsupported element.
        #[label("unsupported device")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// `.model` declares a model type the parser does not implement.
    #[error("unsupported model type '{kind}' on model '{name}'")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::unsupported_model_type),
        help("sindr currently supports model types: D, NPN, PNP, NMOS, PMOS, NJF, PJF")
    )]
    UnsupportedModelType {
        /// Model type token (e.g. `NMOS`).
        kind: String,
        /// Model name as declared.
        name: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the model type token.
        #[label("unsupported model type")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// `X<inst>` references a `.subckt` definition that was never declared.
    #[error("undefined subcircuit '{name}'")]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::undefined_subckt))]
    UndefinedSubckt {
        /// Referenced subcircuit name.
        name: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the offending instance.
        #[label("undefined subckt")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A device references a `.model` that was never declared.
    #[error("undefined model '{name}'")]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::undefined_model))]
    UndefinedModel {
        /// Referenced model name.
        name: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the offending reference.
        #[label("undefined model")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A `.param` expression references a name that was never bound.
    #[error("undefined parameter '{name}'")]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::undefined_param))]
    UndefinedParam {
        /// Referenced parameter name.
        name: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the unresolved reference.
        #[label("undefined parameter")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// Parameter expressions form a cycle (`a = b * 2; b = a + 1`).
    #[error("circular parameter reference: {}", cycle.join(" -> "))]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::circular_param),
        help("break the cycle by substituting a literal value for one parameter")
    )]
    CircularParam {
        /// Cycle of parameter names, in dependency order.
        cycle: Vec<String>,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the first parameter in the cycle.
        #[label("part of cycle")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A device or directive received the wrong number of node/argument tokens.
    #[error("arity mismatch on '{card}': expected {expected}, got {got}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::arity_mismatch))]
    ArityMismatch {
        /// Card or device id whose arity is wrong.
        card: String,
        /// Human-readable description of the expected arity.
        expected: String,
        /// Number of tokens actually supplied.
        got: usize,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the offending line.
        #[label("wrong number of arguments")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A numeric literal could not be parsed as an `f64`.
    #[error("invalid number literal '{raw}'")]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::bad_number))]
    BadNumber {
        /// Raw token text.
        raw: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the bad literal.
        #[label("not a number")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A SPICE SI/engineering suffix could not be recognised.
    #[error("unknown SI suffix '{suffix}'")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::bad_si_suffix),
        help("supported suffixes: T, G, MEG, K, M, U, N, P, F, MIL")
    )]
    BadSiSuffix {
        /// Suffix tail of the literal.
        suffix: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the suffix.
        #[label("unknown suffix")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// Generic grammar failure (catch-all from the winnow parser), and the
    /// errors raised while evaluating cards: a value that isn't finite, an
    /// expression nested more than 256 levels deep, an out-of-range analysis
    /// card.
    #[error("syntax error: {message}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::syntax))]
    Syntax {
        /// Human-readable description of the failure.
        message: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the offending tokens.
        #[label("here")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A `.include` referred to a file that doesn't exist on disk.
    #[error("included file not found: {}", path.display())]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::include_not_found))]
    IncludeNotFound {
        /// Path that was searched for.
        path: PathBuf,
        /// Source text of the file containing the `.include`.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the `.include` directive.
        #[label("not found")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// A `.include`d file was found but failed to read.
    #[error("I/O error reading included file {}", path.display())]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::include_io))]
    IncludeIo {
        /// Path that failed to read.
        path: PathBuf,
        /// Underlying I/O error.
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
    },

    /// `parse_str` saw a relative `.include` but has no base directory to resolve against.
    #[error("relative .include '{include}' is not allowed when parsing from a string")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(sindr::spice::relative_include_in_string),
        help("use parse_file or parse_str_with_options with an explicit include_search_path")
    )]
    RelativeIncludeInString {
        /// The relative include path as written.
        include: String,
        /// Source text.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the directive.
        #[label("relative include")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },

    /// `.lib file section` referenced a section name that doesn't exist in the file.
    #[error("section '{section}' not found in library {}", file.display())]
    #[diagnostic(code(sindr::spice::lib_section_not_found))]
    LibSectionNotFound {
        /// Section name as referenced.
        section: String,
        /// Library file searched.
        file: PathBuf,
        /// Source text of the calling file.
        #[source_code]
        src: NamedSource<String>,
        /// Span of the `.lib` directive.
        #[label("missing section")]
        bad_span: SourceSpan,
    },
}

/// Non-fatal warning collected when [`crate::spice::ParseOptions::strict`] is `false`.
///
/// Plain data — callers decide how (or whether) to render. The parser fills
/// `span` and `file` whenever the warning is locatable.
pub struct ParseWarning {
    /// Human-readable warning message.
    pub message: String,
    /// Span in the originating file, if known.
    pub span: Option<SourceSpan>,
    /// File the warning originated in, if known.
    pub file: Option<String>,
}
```

## `sindr/src/spice/export.rs`

Write a [`Circuit`] as a SPICE deck: [`to_netlist`].

```rust
/// Why [`to_netlist`] couldn't write a circuit.
pub enum ExportError {
    /// The element has no SPICE equivalent that sindr can express.
    #[error("`{id}` can't be written as SPICE: {reason}")]
    Unsupported {
        /// The element's id.
        id: String,
        /// What has no SPICE equivalent.
        reason: String,
    },
    /// A node or element name a SPICE deck can't hold, or two names that
    /// SPICE, being case-insensitive, would merge.
    #[error("{what} `{name}` can't be written as SPICE: {reason}")]
    BadName {
        /// `"node"`, `"element"` or `"block"`.
        what: &'static str,
        /// The name as the circuit has it.
        name: String,
        /// What is wrong with it.
        reason: String,
    },
    /// The design hierarchy is broken: see [`DesignError`].
    #[error(transparent)]
    Design(#[from] DesignError),
    /// A value that is NaN or infinite.
    #[error("`{id}`: {field} is {value}, not a finite number")]
    NonFinite {
        /// The element's id.
        id: String,
        /// The field holding the value.
        field: &'static str,
        /// The value.
        value: f64,
    },
}

/// Writes `circuit` as a SPICE deck titled `title`: element lines, then one
/// `.model` card per distinct diode or transistor model, then `.end`. No
/// analysis cards are written.
///
/// The deck is SPICE3, so ngspice reads it, and [`parse_str`](super::parse_str)
/// reads back every element it can parse (R, L, C, V, I, D, Q, M, J) into a
/// circuit that solves the same.
///
/// # What is written
///
/// | Element | As |
/// |---|---|
/// | `Resistor`, `Capacitor`, `Inductor` | `R`, `C`, `L` |
/// | `VoltageSource`, `CurrentSource` | `V`, `I`, with `DC` or a waveform |
/// | `Diode`, `Bjt` | `D`, `Q`, with a `.model` card |
/// | `Mosfet` | `M d g s s` with `W=1 L=1`, so a level-1 card's `KP`, `CGSO` and `CGDO` are sindr's values as they are. A body diode with only `IS`, `CJO`, `VJ`, `M` and `FC` is the card's drain–bulk junction; one with more is a `D<name>_body` line beside it, and the card's `IS` is 0 |
/// | `Jfet` | `J`, with an `NJF`/`PJF` card: `VTO` the pinch-off, `BETA = idss/VTO²`, `IS=0` for sindr's ideal gate, and the gate capacitances as `CGS`, `CGD`, `PB`, `FC` (and `M` when it isn't 0.5, which ngspice ignores) |
/// | `Vcvs`, `Vccs`, `Ccvs`, `Cccs` | `E`, `G`, `H`, `F` |
/// | `Behavioural` | `B n+ n- V={expr}` or `I={expr}`, its nodes and sources by their deck names |
/// | `Transformer` | two `L` and a `K` |
/// | `Switch`, `Pushbutton`, `Fuse` | `R` at the resistance sindr stamps |
/// | `SwitchSpdt` | two `R`, common to each throw |
/// | `Crystal` | `R`, `L`, `C` in series (the motional arm) beside `C` (C0) |
/// | `FerriteBead` | `R` (DC) into `L` ∥ `R` (∥ `C`) |
/// | `Potentiometer` | two `R`, top–wiper and wiper–bottom |
/// | `Photoresistor`, `Thermistor` | `R` at their resistance |
/// | `Led`, `SchottkyDiode` | `D` with their Shockley parameters |
///
/// A source's waveform and its static value are written as one waveform:
/// SPICE ignores a `DC` value during a transient, where sindr adds it.
/// Square, triangle and PWM waves become the `PULSE` that traces the same
/// wave; a sine's phase becomes `SIN`'s delay.
///
/// sindr's parser reads every line written here back.
///
/// # Names
///
/// The ground node is written as `0`. An element keeps its id when the id
/// starts with its SPICE letter (`R1` for a resistor); otherwise the letter
/// is put in front (`load` becomes `Rload`). Elements written as two lines
/// add `_top`/`_bottom` (potentiometer) or `_p`/`_s` (transformer windings).
/// SPICE folds case, and sindr's parser reads everything as lowercase.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`ExportError::Unsupported`] for an element with no SPICE equivalent:
/// a MOSFET with flicker noise, a JFET with a pinch-off SPICE can't write,
/// IGBT, zener, op-amp, comparator, relay, photodiode,
/// varactor, voltage regulator, a BJT with parasitic capacitances, a junction
/// away from 27 °C (sindr reads no temperature from a deck), or a phased sine
/// of zero frequency. [`ExportError::BadName`] for a name holding whitespace
/// or SPICE punctuation, a node other than ground named `0` or `gnd`, two
/// names that differ only in case, or an F/H source whose controlling source
/// isn't a voltage source. [`ExportError::NonFinite`] for a NaN or infinite
/// value.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "gnd".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["in".into(), "gnd".into()],
///             voltage: 5.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "load".into(),
///             nodes: ["in".into(), "gnd".into()],
///             resistance: 1e3,
///         }),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
/// let deck = sindr::spice::to_netlist(&circuit, "divider")?;
/// assert_eq!(deck, "divider\nV1 in 0 DC 5\nRload in 0 1000\n.end\n");
/// # Ok::<(), sindr::spice::ExportError>(())
/// ```
///
pub fn to_netlist(circuit: &Circuit, title: &str) -> Result<String, ExportError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/spice/flatten.rs`

Subcircuit flattener.

Walks a `Vec<RawCard>` (as produced by the parser) and expands every
`X<inst>` subcircuit instance inline, producing a flat element list with
`.`-separated hierarchical naming for both nodes and component ids.

Algorithm:

1. **Pass 1 — collect definitions.** Walk the cards once moving every
   `.subckt` into a `name -> RawSubckt` table, every `.model` into a
   `name -> RawModel` table, every top-level `.param` list into a
   deferred-evaluation queue, and every `.tran/.dc/.ac/.op` into the
   analyses list. Top-level element lines go into `top_elements`.

2. **Pass 2 — evaluate top params, then expand.** Run the deferred
   `.param` lists against the outer `ParamScope`. Then walk
   `top_elements`: subckt instances recurse into `expand_instance`;
   other elements are emitted directly with their current scope
   snapshot.

Recursion into `expand_instance` builds a fresh scope frame, populates
it from the subckt's `defaults` then the instance's overrides
(overrides win), establishes a `port -> caller_node` mapping, and
emits each body card with renamed nodes / ids:

* Ground node `"0"` and `.global` nets are **never** prefixed.
* A node matching a subckt port maps to the caller's node.
* Any other node is prefixed with `instance_path.join(".")`.
* Component ids are prefixed similarly.

Recursion into the same subckt name on the active expansion stack
raises [`SpiceParseError::Syntax`].

## `sindr/src/spice/mod.rs`

SPICE3 netlist parser for the sindr circuit simulator.

Parses a practical subset of Berkeley SPICE3f5 netlists into a
[`crate::Circuit`] plus structured analysis directives. The supported
device set tracks what `sindr` can solve: R, L, C, V, I, D, Q (NPN/PNP),
M (level-1 NMOS/PMOS), J (NJF/PJF), B (behavioural), the linear controlled
sources E, G, F and H (and their `POLY` form, and the `VALUE` form of E and
G), K (two coupled `L` lines,
read as one [`Transformer`](crate::CircuitElement::Transformer)) and X
(subcircuit instance). Subcircuits declared with `.subckt` /
`.ends` become [`Block`](crate::Block)s and X lines
[`Instance`](crate::Instance)s; the solver flattens them with
`.`-separated hierarchical naming ([`Circuit::flatten`](crate::Circuit::flatten)),
and a [`SourceMap`] maps each flattened node back to its instance path.
[`to_netlist`] writes blocks back as `.subckt`s.
`.global` nets, declared anywhere in the deck (inside a `.subckt` too),
land in [`Circuit::globals`](crate::Circuit::globals) and keep their name
inside every instance instead of taking its prefix.

`.ic` cards land in [`ParsedNetlist::initial_conditions`], which
[`ParsedNetlist::transient_config`] passes on. `.options` (`RELTOL`,
`VNTOL`, `TRTOL`, `ITL1`) and `.nodeset` cards land in
[`ParsedNetlist::options`]; [`ParsedNetlist::solver`] runs the deck's
analyses with them.

The module is the `spice` feature, on by default like every feature.
A build that turns the defaults off (`default-features = false`) keeps
it by listing it: `features = ["spice"]`.

### Quick start

Parse a deck from a string and solve its operating point:

```
let deck = "\
* 10 V across a 1k / 2k divider
V1 in 0 10
R1 in out 1k
R2 out 0 2k
.op
.end
";
let netlist = sindr::spice::parse_str(deck)?;
let result = sindr::solve_circuit(&netlist.circuit)?;
assert!((result.node_voltages["out"] - 20.0 / 3.0).abs() < 1e-9);
```

For a deck on disk, parse it, hand the [`Circuit`](crate::Circuit) to the
solver, then dispatch each parsed analysis directive to the matching
`sindr` routine (`no_run`: `amp.cir` doesn't exist where doctests run):

```no_run
use sindr::spice::{parse_file, AnalysisRequest};

let netlist = parse_file("amp.cir")?;
println!("parsed `{}` ({} components)", netlist.title, netlist.circuit.components.len());

// `netlist.analyses` carries the deck's `.op` / `.tran` / `.dc` / `.ac` / `.tf` / `.sens` / `.noise` / `.pz`
// directives, in source order. The parser does not run them — you do.
for analysis in &netlist.analyses {
    match analysis {
        AnalysisRequest::Op => {
            let result = sindr::solve_op(&netlist.circuit)?;
            println!("op: {} node voltages", result.node_voltages.len());
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Dc { source, .. } => {
            match analysis.dc_axes().unwrap()? {
                (inner, Some(outer)) => {
                    let sweep = sindr::dc_sweep_nested(&netlist.circuit, &inner, &outer)?;
                    println!("dc sweep of {source}: {} curves", sweep.curves.len());
                }
                (axis, None) => {
                    let sweep = sindr::dc_sweep(&netlist.circuit, &axis)?;
                    println!("dc sweep of {source}: {} points", sweep.points.len());
                }
            }
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Tran { tstop, .. } => {
            let config = analysis.transient_config().unwrap();
            let _ = sindr::solve_transient(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
            println!("transient to {tstop} s");
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Ac { .. } => {
            // The stimulus comes from the deck's `AC` spec on a V line.
            let config = netlist.ac_config().unwrap()?;
            let ac = sindr::ac_analysis::solve_ac(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
            println!("ac sweep: {} points", ac.points.len());
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Sens { .. } => {
            let sens = sindr::solve_sensitivity(&netlist.circuit, &analysis.sens_config().unwrap())?;
            println!("sens: {} parameters", sens.entries.len());
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Noise { .. } => {
            let noise = sindr::solve_noise(&netlist.circuit, &analysis.noise_config().unwrap())?;
            println!("noise: {} V rms at the output", noise.total_output_noise);
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Tf { .. } => {
            let tf = sindr::solve_tf(&netlist.circuit, &analysis.tf_config().unwrap())?;
            println!("tf: gain {}, rin {} Ω, rout {} Ω", tf.gain, tf.input_resistance, tf.output_resistance);
        }
        AnalysisRequest::Pz { .. } => {
            let pz = sindr::solve_pz(&netlist.circuit, &analysis.pz_config().unwrap())?;
            println!("pz: {} poles, {} zeros", pz.poles.len(), pz.zeros.len());
        }
        // `AnalysisRequest` is non-exhaustive: later releases add analyses.
        other => println!("not run here: {other:?}"),
    }
}
```

### Model cards

A `.model` card's parameters are read where sindr's models have them:

| Card | Parameters | Into |
|---|---|---|
| `D` | `IS`, `N`, `RS`, `CJO` (or `CJ0`, `CJ`), `VJ` (or `PB`), `M` (or `MJ`), `FC`, `TT`, `BV`, `IBV`, `KF`, `AF` | [`DiodeModel`](crate::DiodeModel) |
| `NPN`, `PNP` | `BF` | the element's `bf` |
| `NPN`, `PNP` | `IS`, `BR`, `NF`, `NR`, `VAF` (or `VA`), `KF`, `AF` | [`BjtModel`](crate::BjtModel) |
| `NMOS`, `PMOS` | `LEVEL` (1 only), `KP`, `VTO`, `LAMBDA`, `GAMMA`, `PHI`, `LD` | [`MosfetParams`](crate::devices::mosfet::MosfetParams) |
| `NMOS`, `PMOS` | `CGSO`, `CGDO`, `CGBO` | [`MosfetParasiticCaps`](crate::circuit::MosfetParasiticCaps) |
| `NMOS`, `PMOS` | `IS`, `CBD`, `PB`, `MJ`, `FC` (the drain–bulk junction) | the element's `body_diode` |
| `NJF`, `PJF` | `VTO`, `BETA` | the element's `idss` and `vp` |
| `NJF`, `PJF` | `CGS`, `CGD`, `PB` (or `VJ`), `M`, `FC` | [`JfetParasiticCaps`](crate::circuit::JfetParasiticCaps) |

A `.model` inside a `.subckt` belongs to that subcircuit: its elements
use it ahead of a top-level card of the same name, and nothing outside
sees it, as vendor model files expect.

### MOSFETs and JFETs

`Mxxx nd ng ns nb model [W=] [L=] [M=]` is SPICE's level 1 with
ngspice's defaults (`W` = `L` = 100 µm, `KP` = 2e-5 A/V², `IS` =
1e-14 A):

* `kp = KP·W/(L − 2·LD)·M`; `VTO`, `LAMBDA`, `GAMMA` and `PHI` as written.
* The gate capacitances are SPICE's overlap ones, `CGSO·W + CGBO·(L − 2·LD)`
  and `CGDO·W`, times `M`: the bulk is the source, so gate–bulk is
  gate–source.
* The drain–bulk junction becomes the body diode. `IS=0` with no `CBD`
  leaves none.

sindr's MOSFET ties its body to its source, so a bulk node other than
the source is an error in strict mode and a warning in lenient mode.
`LEVEL` other than 1 is always an error: another level is a different
model. `AD`, `AS`, `PD`, `PS`, `NRD` and `NRS` only scale parameters
sindr refuses, so they are dropped. `TOX` (which turns on SPICE's Meyer
gate capacitance), `RD`/`RS` above 0, `KF`, the `OFF` flag and other
instance parameters are unsupported.

`Jxxx nd ng ns model [area]` gives `idss = BETA·VTO²·area` and a
pinch-off of `VTO` (default −2 V), signed as
[`JfetKind`](crate::JfetKind) expects. `CGS·area` and `CGD·area` are
the gate junction capacitances, graded by `PB`, `M` and `FC` (ngspice
ignores `M` and grades at 0.5). sindr's gate junction conducts no
current and its JFET has no channel-length modulation or series
resistance, so `IS`, `LAMBDA`, `RD` and `RS` are read only at 0.

sindr's BJT is Ebers–Moll, so its Early effect isn't SPICE's
Gummel–Poon base charge: with `VAF` set, results differ slightly from
SPICE's. Diode and BJT `EG` and `XTI` set how `IS` follows
temperature, as SPICE's `IS(T)`; `TNOM` is read only at 27 °C, the
temperature sindr's values are at. Any other parameter (`CJE`, `VAR`,
`IKF`, …) is an error in strict mode and a warning per card in lenient
mode, naming them.
Part annotations that don't affect the simulation (`MFG`, `TYPE`,
`VCEO`, `ICRATING`, `IAVE`, `VPK`) are dropped without a word.

### Controlled sources and coupling

| Line | Into |
|---|---|
| `Exxx n+ n- nc+ nc- gain` | [`Vcvs`](crate::CircuitElement::Vcvs) |
| `Gxxx n+ n- nc+ nc- gm` | [`Vccs`](crate::CircuitElement::Vccs) |
| `Fxxx n+ n- vname alpha` | [`Cccs`](crate::CircuitElement::Cccs) |
| `Hxxx n+ n- vname rm` | [`Ccvs`](crate::CircuitElement::Ccvs) |
| `Kxxx lname1 lname2 k` | [`Transformer`](crate::CircuitElement::Transformer) |

Nodes and current directions are SPICE's, so they map across as
written. An `F` or `H` line's `vname` must be a `V` line in the same
scope (the top level, or the same `.subckt` body). A `K` line replaces
its two `L` lines, which must be in its scope, with one transformer named
after the `K` line: primary from `lname1`, secondary from `lname2`, the
first node of each its dot. Each `L` can be coupled once; sindr has no
three-winding transformer. The nonlinear forms `TABLE` and `LAPLACE`
are unsupported devices: an error in strict mode, a warning
(and the line dropped) in lenient mode.

### Behavioural sources

| Line | Into |
|---|---|
| `Bxxx n+ n- V={expr}`, `Exxx n+ n- VALUE={expr}` | [`Behavioural`](crate::CircuitElement::Behavioural), a voltage |
| `Bxxx n+ n- I={expr}`, `Gxxx n+ n- VALUE={expr}` | [`Behavioural`](crate::CircuitElement::Behavioural), a current from `n+` to `n-` |
| `Exxx`/`Hxxx n+ n- POLY(n) …` | a behavioural voltage: the polynomial of `n` node-pair voltages (E) or `V`-line currents (H) |
| `Gxxx`/`Fxxx n+ n- POLY(n) …` | a behavioural current, the same of voltages (G) or currents (F) |

`POLY` coefficients follow SPICE2's order: by total degree, and within
one degree over the controls in nondecreasing index order, so for two
`p0 + p1·x1 + p2·x2 + p3·x1² + p4·x1·x2 + p5·x2² + …`. A
one-dimensional `POLY` with one coefficient is its linear term, as in
SPICE2 (ngspice refuses it).

The expression runs to the end of the card, braces optional, in the
syntax of [`Expression`](crate::expression::Expression): `v(n)`,
`v(n,m)`, `i(vname)`, `time`, arithmetic, comparisons, `?:` and
ngspice's functions. A `.param` name inside it reads as its value. Inside
a `.subckt` it reads that body's own nodes and `V` lines.

### Values

Numbers take SPICE's case-insensitive suffixes: `t` (1e12), `g` (1e9),
`meg` (1e6), `k` (1e3), `m` (1e-3), `mil` (25.4e-6), `u` (1e-6),
`n` (1e-9), `p` (1e-12), `f` (1e-15) and `a` (1e-18). Letters after the
suffix are ignored, so `4.7uF` is 4.7e-6. `{…}` expressions may nest
at most 256 levels deep. A value that evaluates to NaN or ±∞ (`1e400`,
`{1/0}`) is an error at its line.

Analysis cards are checked as they are read: a `.dc` must sweep one or
two different voltage or current sources the deck defines, each with a
non-zero step that moves from start towards stop; an `.ac` needs `fstart <= fstop`, and
`fstart > 0` for `dec`/`oct`.

### Strictness and warnings

By default the parser runs in **strict** mode: any unsupported card,
device, model type, or grammar failure aborts with a
[`SpiceParseError`] carrying a labelled span. Set
[`ParseOptions::strict`] to `false` to downgrade the recoverable cases
(unsupported devices/cards) to [`ParseWarning`]s collected in
[`ParsedNetlist::warnings`], so a deck containing an unsupported element
still parses:

```
use sindr::spice::{parse_str_with_options, ParseOptions};

let opts = ParseOptions::default().with_strict(false);
let netlist = parse_str_with_options(deck, opts)?;
for warning in &netlist.warnings {
    eprintln!("warning: {warning:?}");
}
```

### Diagnostics

[`SpiceParseError`] implements [`miette::Diagnostic`] and embeds the
source text with labelled spans. Add `miette` with its `fancy` feature
and render the error through a [`miette::Report`] for annotated,
underlined output pointing at the offending line (`no_run`: `bad.cir`
doesn't exist where doctests run):

```no_run
match sindr::spice::parse_file("bad.cir") {
    Ok(netlist) => { /* ... */ }
    Err(e) => eprintln!("{:?}", miette::Report::new(e)),
}
```

### Export

[`to_netlist`] writes a [`Circuit`](crate::Circuit) as a SPICE deck that
ngspice runs; its docs list what each element is written as. [`parse_str`]
reads every line it writes back, so an exported deck parses to a circuit
that solves the same (a transformer comes back named after its `K` line).

Known gaps against full SPICE3 are listed in the repository's
[`LIMITATIONS.md`](https://github.com/steffendybvik/sindr-rs/blob/main/LIMITATIONS.md).

```rust
pub use analysis:: { … }

pub use error::{ParseWarning, SpiceParseError};

pub use export::{to_netlist, ExportError};

pub use source_map::{HierarchyPath, SourceMap};

/// Successful result of parsing a SPICE netlist.
///
/// [`Self::circuit`] keeps the `.subckt` hierarchy as blocks and
/// instances. Every analysis flattens it; use [`Self::source_map`] to
/// translate flattened node names back to their
/// original `(instance_path, node)` pair.
pub struct ParsedNetlist {
    /// The circuit, with each `.subckt` as a [`Block`](crate::Block) and each
    /// X line as an [`Instance`](crate::Instance). A subckt whose instances
    /// bind different `.param` values gives one block per distinct body,
    /// named `name`, `name_2`, …. The solver takes it as is;
    /// [`Circuit::flatten`](crate::Circuit::flatten) gives the flat element
    /// list.
    pub circuit: crate::Circuit,
    /// Analysis directives declared in the netlist (`.op`, `.tran`, `.dc`,
    /// `.ac`, `.tf`, `.sens`).
    ///
    /// Order matches declaration order in the source.
    pub analyses: Vec<AnalysisRequest>,
    /// `.ic` node voltages (V), keyed by node name: where a transient
    /// starts, or with no `uic` what its operating point holds them at.
    /// [`ParsedNetlist::transient_config`] passes them to
    /// [`TransientConfig::with_initial_voltages`](crate::TransientConfig::with_initial_voltages).
    /// Only top-level cards are read.
    pub initial_conditions: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// `.nodeset` node voltages (V), keyed by node name: a starting guess for
    /// the DC operating point. [`Self::options`] carries them too, as its
    /// [`nodeset`](crate::SolverOptions::nodeset). Only top-level cards are
    /// read.
    pub nodesets: HashMap<String, f64>,
    /// The deck's `.options` (`reltol`, `vntol`, `trtol`, `itl1`) over the
    /// defaults, with its `.nodeset` cards as the nodeset. Run the deck's
    /// analyses through [`Self::solver`] to use them. Only top-level cards
    /// are read.
    pub options: crate::SolverOptions,
    /// `.meas` / `.measure` cards, in source order. Only top-level cards are
    /// read.
    pub measurements: Vec<MeasureRequest>,
    /// The `AC` specs on the deck's `V` and `I` lines, in source order,
    /// those inside `.subckt` bodies included under their flattened ids.
    /// [`Self::ac_config`] drives `.ac` from them.
    pub ac_stimuli: Vec<AcStimulus>,
    /// Non-fatal warnings collected in lenient mode. Always empty when
    /// [`ParseOptions::strict`] is `true`.
    pub warnings: Vec<ParseWarning>,
    /// Hierarchy recovery: flattened node name → original instance path + node.
    pub source_map: SourceMap,
    /// Title line of the netlist (first non-blank line). May be empty if the
    /// source has no title.
    pub title: String,
}

impl ParsedNetlist {
    /// A [`Solver`](crate::Solver) with the deck's [`options`](Self::options).
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* opts\nV1 in 0 5\nR1 in a 1k\nD1 a 0 dmod\n.model dmod D\n\
    ///             .options reltol=1e-6 itl1=200\n.nodeset v(a)=0.7\n.op\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// assert_eq!(netlist.options.max_iterations, 200);
    /// let op = netlist.solver().circuit(&netlist.circuit)?;
    /// assert!((op.node_voltages["a"] - 0.7).abs() < 0.1);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn solver(&self) -> crate::Solver { … }

    /// The [`TransientConfig`](crate::TransientConfig) for the deck's first
    /// `.tran`, with its `.ic` cards as
    /// [`initial_voltages`](crate::TransientConfig::initial_voltages), so
    /// the run starts as ngspice's does: from the operating point with the
    /// `.ic` nodes held, or with `uic` from the `.ic` values alone. `None`
    /// without a `.tran`. See [`AnalysisRequest::transient_config`] for the
    /// rest of the card.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// // .ic holds `a` at 3 V while the operating point is solved; then
    /// // the capacitor discharges towards the divider's 0.5 V.
    /// let deck = "* ic\nV1 in 0 1\nR1 in a 1k\nR2 a 0 1k\nC1 a 0 1u\n\
    ///             .ic v(a)=3\n.tran 10u 5m\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.transient_config().unwrap();
    /// let tran = sindr::solve_transient(&netlist.circuit, &config)?.transient.unwrap();
    /// assert!(tran.timesteps[0].node_voltages["a"] > 2.9);
    /// assert!((tran.timesteps.last().unwrap().node_voltages["a"] - 0.5).abs() < 1e-3);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    pub fn transient_config(&self) -> Option<crate::TransientConfig> { … }

    /// The [`AcConfig`](crate::ac_analysis::AcConfig) for the deck's first
    /// `.ac`, driving the source whose line carries an `AC` spec at that
    /// spec's magnitude and phase, so the deck runs as ngspice runs it.
    /// `None` without an `.ac`. See [`AnalysisRequest::ac_config`] for the
    /// sweep.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* rc\nV1 in 0 dc 0 ac 2\nR1 in out 1k\nC1 out 0 1u\n.ac dec 10 1 100k\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.ac_config().unwrap()?;
    /// assert_eq!((config.source_id.as_str(), config.ac_magnitude), ("v1", 2.0));
    /// let ac = sindr::ac_analysis::solve_ac(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    /// // Well below the 159 Hz pole the output follows the 2 V stimulus.
    /// assert!((ac.points[0].node_voltages["out"].norm() - 2.0).abs() < 1e-3);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The inner `Result` is [`SimError::InvalidComponent`](crate::SimError)
    /// unless exactly one source carries an `AC` spec and it's a `V` line:
    /// sindr's AC analysis drives a single voltage source.
    pub fn ac_config(&self) -> Option<Result<crate::ac_analysis::AcConfig, crate::SimError>> { … }

    /// The [`AcSensConfig`](crate::AcSensConfig) for the deck's first
    /// `.sens ... ac`, its stimulus the source whose line carries an `AC`
    /// spec, as [`ac_config`](Self::ac_config) has it. `None` without one.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::spice::parse_str;
    /// use sindr::SensParameter;
    ///
    /// let deck = "* rc\nV1 in 0 dc 0 ac 1\nR1 in out 1k\nC1 out 0 1u\n\
    ///             .sens v(out) ac dec 10 1 100k\n.end\n";
    /// let netlist = parse_str(deck)?;
    /// let config = netlist.ac_sens_config().unwrap()?;
    /// let sens = sindr::solve_ac_sensitivity(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    /// // Well below the pole, V(out) hardly depends on R1 or C1.
    /// let r1 = sens.points[0].get_parameter("r1", SensParameter::Resistance).unwrap();
    /// assert!(r1.per_percent.norm() < 1e-4);
    /// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// The inner `Result` is as for [`ac_config`](Self::ac_config).
    pub fn ac_sens_config(&self) -> Option<Result<crate::AcSensConfig, crate::SimError>> { … }
}

/// Knobs controlling parser strictness and include-path resolution.
///
/// Start from [`Default`] (strict, no include-path override) and set what
/// you need with [`with_strict`](Self::with_strict) and
/// [`with_include_search_path`](Self::with_include_search_path). It is
/// `#[non_exhaustive]`, so new options can come without breaking callers.
pub struct ParseOptions {
    /// If `true` (default), any unsupported card/device or syntax error is
    /// fatal. If `false`, recoverable unsupported items are skipped and
    /// recorded as [`ParseWarning`]s instead.
    pub strict: bool,
    /// Override the base directory for `.include` / `.lib` resolution.
    ///
    /// `None` = derive from the input path (when using [`parse_file`]) or
    /// the process working directory (when using [`parse_str`]). Setting
    /// this is required if you call [`parse_str`] on a netlist that
    /// contains relative `.include`s.
    pub include_search_path: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
}

impl ParseOptions {
    /// Set [`strict`](Self::strict): `false` turns recoverable unsupported
    /// items into [`ParseWarning`]s instead of errors.
    pub fn with_strict(mut self, strict: bool) -> Self { … }

    /// Set [`include_search_path`](Self::include_search_path), the base
    /// directory for relative `.include` / `.lib` paths.
    pub fn with_include_search_path(mut self, path: impl Into<std::path::PathBuf>) -> Self { … }
}

/// Parse a SPICE netlist from an in-memory string in strict mode.
///
/// Use [`parse_str_with_options`] if you need lenient mode or a custom
/// include search path.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`SpiceParseError`] on the first grammar / lookup / unsupported
/// construct.
pub fn parse_str(src: &str) -> Result<ParsedNetlist, SpiceParseError> { … }

/// Parse a SPICE netlist from disk in strict mode.
///
/// `.include` and `.lib` directives resolve relative to `path`'s parent
/// directory.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`SpiceParseError`] on read failure, grammar failure, or any
/// unsupported construct.
pub fn parse_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<ParsedNetlist, SpiceParseError> { … }

/// Parse a SPICE netlist from an in-memory string with explicit options.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`SpiceParseError`] in strict mode on any unsupported construct;
/// in lenient mode, only fatal grammar / lookup failures error.
pub fn parse_str_with_options(
    src: &str,
    opts: ParseOptions,
) -> Result<ParsedNetlist, SpiceParseError> { … }

/// Parse a SPICE netlist from disk with explicit options.
///
/// `.include` and `.lib` directives resolve relative to `path`'s parent
/// directory unless overridden via [`ParseOptions::include_search_path`].
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`SpiceParseError`] on read failure or fatal parse error.
pub fn parse_file_with_options(
    path: impl AsRef<Path>,
    opts: ParseOptions,
) -> Result<ParsedNetlist, SpiceParseError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/spice/param_eval.rs`

`.param` arithmetic evaluator with lexical scoping.

Operates on the [`ParamExpr`](crate::spice::ast::ParamExpr) AST shaped by the
grammar. Pure: takes a [`ParamScope`] (a stack of frames) and folds
the expression to an `f64`. The grammar layer is responsible for
turning failures into [`crate::spice::SpiceParseError`]s with proper spans;
at this layer we surface a small private [`EvalError`].

Scoping rules:
- `ParamScope` is a stack of `HashMap<String, f64>` frames. Lookup
  walks innermost-outward, so an inner-frame definition shadows an
  outer one (subcircuit instance overrides outer params).
- Within a single `.param` list, forward references resolve via a
  topological-sort dependency walk before evaluation. References to
  outer-scope names are resolved through `scope.get` and are not part
  of the dep graph. Cycles among the bindings raise
  [`EvalError::Circular`].

```rust
impl ParamScope {
    /// New scope with one empty top-level frame.
    pub fn new() -> Self { … }

    /// Push an empty frame (entering a nested instance).
    pub fn push_scope(&mut self) { … }

    /// Pop the innermost frame. No-op if only one frame remains.
    pub fn pop_scope(&mut self) { … }

    /// Define `name = value` in the innermost frame, shadowing any
    /// outer-frame definition.
    pub fn define(&mut self, name: &str, value: f64) { … }

    /// Look up `name`, walking frames innermost-outward.
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<f64> { … }

    /// Flatten every frame into a single map. Inner frames shadow outer
    /// (innermost wins, matching `get`'s lookup order). Used by the
    /// flattener to capture the scope visible at expansion time so the
    /// build pass can evaluate `ParamExpr` without re-walking the
    /// hierarchy.
    pub fn snapshot_flat(&self) -> HashMap<String, f64> { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/spice/parser.rs`

winnow grammar that turns preprocessed SPICE lines into [`RawCard`] AST nodes.

This module is the bridge between the SPICE3 surface syntax and the
internal AST. It is pure parsing: no expression evaluation, no `.subckt`
flattening, no `Circuit` construction. Span tracking is mandatory — every
AST node carries a byte range so callers get caret-style diagnostics.

#### Input contract

The parser consumes a [`Preprocessed`] value built by the preprocessor
pass. Each [`LogicalLine`] is a single SPICE card after comment stripping
and `+` continuation joining; the preprocessor has also case-folded the
text. The grammar therefore never has to deal with case, comments, or
line continuations.

#### Span policy

Element / card parsers run on the local [`LogicalLine::text`] string; the
returned spans are *local* to that string. The top-level driver
([`parse`]) translates them to absolute spans inside the original source
file via `LogicalLine::byte_range.start`.

## `sindr/src/spice/preprocess.rs`

SPICE preprocessing pass: title extraction, comment stripping,
continuation joining, case folding, and `.include` / `.lib` resolution.

This stage runs before the winnow grammar so that the grammar only ever
sees one logical line at a time, in lowercase, with no comments and
with all transitively included files already spliced in.

Three SPICE traps are handled here:
- **Title line**: SPICE3 *unconditionally* treats the first non-blank
  line of the top-level file as a title and excludes it from grammar
  input — even if it looks like a card. Missing this swallows a real
  element line on every netlist that lacks a title.
- **`Meg` vs `m`**: not handled here directly (see [`crate::spice::si`]),
  but case folding happens here so the grammar matches `meg` exactly.
- **`.lib file section`**: two-argument `.lib` only splices the lines
  between `.lib <section>` and `.endl` markers in the included file.

## `sindr/src/spice/si.rs`

SPICE SI / engineering-suffix decoding.

SPICE3 numeric literals carry an optional case-insensitive suffix
(`k`, `meg`, `u`, `pF`, ...) followed by arbitrary trailing alphabetic
"decoration" that is silently ignored: `4.7uF` parses as 4.7e-6 with
the `F` discarded.

The order of the suffix table matters: longer prefixes must be tried
before any shorter prefix that is a substring of them. The infamous
example is `meg` vs `m` — without longest-match, `1Meg` would parse
as 1e-3 with a leftover `eg`.

## `sindr/src/spice/source_map.rs`

Hierarchy recovery for flattened subcircuit instances.

After lowering, every subcircuit-internal node is renamed to a flat,
`.`-separated path (`X1.X2.in`). The [`SourceMap`] lets callers walk
back from a flattened name to the original instance path + node, which
is what most schematic-style probe UIs want.

```rust
/// Map from a flattened node name to its original hierarchical location.
pub type SourceMap = HashMap<String, HierarchyPath>;

/// Original hierarchical position of a flattened node.
pub struct HierarchyPath {
    /// Stack of `X<inst>` instance names from outermost to innermost.
    /// Empty for nodes at the top level.
    pub instance_path: Vec<String>,
    /// Node name as written inside its declaring scope (the subckt body or
    /// the top-level netlist).
    pub original_node: String,
}

impl HierarchyPath {
    /// Separator used when flattening hierarchical node names.
    ///
    /// `.` matches the convention SPICE simulators use, ngspice among them.
    pub fn flatten_separator() -> char { … }
}
```

## `sindr/src/temp_sweep.rs`

Temperature sweep analysis.

Varies junction temperature across a range and solves the circuit at each
temperature point. IS is re-scaled using the SPICE formula at each step,
and the thermal voltage follows the temperature.

Mirrors the dc_sweep.rs pattern exactly: clones the circuit, mutates the
temperature field on all IS-bearing components, and calls solve_circuit.

```rust
/// One temperature sweep data point.
pub struct TempSweepPoint {
    /// Temperature for this point (Kelvin).
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Simulation result at this temperature.
    pub result: SimulationResult,
}

/// Result of a temperature sweep analysis.
///
/// One operating-point solution per temperature step. Use the `points`
/// vector to iterate `(temperature, result)` pairs.
pub struct TempSweepResult {
    /// Start of the swept temperature range (K).
    pub start: f64,
    /// End of the swept temperature range (K).
    pub stop: f64,
    /// Operating points, in order from `start` to `stop`.
    pub points: Vec<TempSweepPoint>,
}

impl TempSweepResult {
    /// `(temperature in K, node voltage in V)` pairs for a node, one per
    /// point. Empty when there's no such node.
    pub fn node_voltage_curve(&self, node: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }

    /// `(temperature in K, current in A)` pairs for a component, one per
    /// point: its [`ComponentResult::current_through`], as
    /// [`DcSweepResult::component_current_curve`] reads it.
    ///
    /// [`ComponentResult::current_through`]: crate::ComponentResult::current_through
    /// [`DcSweepResult::component_current_curve`]: crate::DcSweepResult::component_current_curve
    pub fn component_current_curve(&self, component_id: &str) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> { … }
}

/// A temperature sweep: `num_points` temperatures from `start` to `stop`
/// (K), both ends included.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::temp_sweep::TempSweepConfig;
///
/// // −40 °C to 125 °C in 12 points.
/// let config = TempSweepConfig::new(233.15, 398.15, 12);
/// assert_eq!(config.num_points, 12);
/// ```
pub struct TempSweepConfig {
    /// First temperature (K).
    pub start: f64,
    /// Last temperature (K).
    pub stop: f64,
    /// Points including both ends. At least 2.
    pub num_points: usize,
}

impl TempSweepConfig {
    /// `num_points` temperatures from `start` to `stop` (K).
    pub fn new(start: f64, stop: f64, num_points: usize) -> Self { … }
}

/// Sweeps junction temperature across a range and solves the circuit at
/// each step.
///
/// At each temperature, the saturation current `IS` of every IS-bearing
/// component (BJT, diode, LED, Zener, Schottky, photodiode) is rescaled
/// using the SPICE temperature formula, and its thermal voltage set to kT/q,
/// before solving. The base circuit is not modified.
///
/// `temperature` here is junction temperature — the thermistor's own
/// temperature input is independent.
///
/// # Arguments
///
/// - `circuit` — circuit to sweep (cloned per point, not modified)
/// - `config` — the temperatures: endpoints in kelvin (e.g. 250.0 to
///   400.0) and the number of points including both
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if `num_points < 2` or above 10⁷, or either endpoint
///   is not finite or not above 0 K
/// - Any [`SimError`] from solving at one of the temperatures (propagated
///   immediately)
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement, temperature_sweep};
/// use sindr::temp_sweep::TempSweepConfig;
/// use sindr::element::{Diode, VoltageSource};
///
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 1.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Diode(Diode {
///             id: "D1".into(),
///             nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
///             temperature: 300.15,
///             model: None,
///         }),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// // Sweep from 250 K (-23 °C) to 400 K (127 °C) in 4 steps.
/// let sweep = temperature_sweep(&circuit, &TempSweepConfig::new(250.0, 400.0, 4)).unwrap();
/// assert_eq!(sweep.points.len(), 4);
/// ```
///
pub fn temperature_sweep(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    config: &TempSweepConfig,
) -> Result<TempSweepResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/transfer_function.rs`

DC small-signal transfer function, as SPICE's `.tf`.

Linearises the circuit at its DC operating point, then reports the DC
gain from an input source to an output, the resistance the input source
sees, and the resistance at the output.

```rust
/// What a transfer function is measured at.
pub enum TfOutput {
    /// `V(node[,reference])`: the voltage of `node` against `reference`,
    /// or against ground when `reference` is `None`.
    Voltage {
        /// Output node.
        node: String,
        /// Reference node; ground when `None`.
        reference: Option<String>,
    },
    /// `I(source)`: the current through an independent voltage source,
    /// from its `nodes[0]` through the source to its `nodes[1]`.
    Current {
        /// Id of the voltage source the current runs through.
        source_id: String,
    },
}

impl TfOutput {
    /// `V(node)`: the voltage of `node` against ground.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::TfOutput;
    ///
    /// assert_eq!(
    ///     TfOutput::voltage("out"),
    ///     TfOutput::Voltage { node: "out".into(), reference: None },
    /// );
    /// ```
    pub fn voltage(node: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// `V(node,reference)`: the voltage of `node` against `reference`.
    pub fn voltage_between(node: impl Into<String>, reference: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }

    /// `I(source_id)`: the current through the independent voltage source
    /// `source_id`.
    pub fn current(source_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }
}

/// Transfer-function analysis configuration. Build one with
/// [`TfConfig::new`].
pub struct TfConfig {
    /// The output the gain is measured at.
    pub output: TfOutput,
    /// Id of the input: an independent voltage or current source.
    pub input_source: String,
}

impl TfConfig {
    /// The transfer function from the independent source `input_source` to
    /// `output`, as SPICE's `.tf output input_source`.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::{TfConfig, TfOutput};
    ///
    /// // SPICE `.tf v(out) V1`.
    /// let config = TfConfig::new(TfOutput::voltage("out"), "V1");
    /// assert_eq!(config.input_source, "V1");
    /// ```
    pub fn new(output: TfOutput, input_source: impl Into<String>) -> Self { … }
}

/// Result of a transfer-function analysis.
///
/// The gain's unit follows the input and output: V/V for a voltage in and
/// out, A/A for a current in and out, Ω or S for a mix.
pub struct TfResult {
    /// Small-signal DC gain: d(output)/d(input).
    pub gain: f64,
    /// Resistance (Ω) the input source sees, looking into the circuit.
    /// Infinite when it draws no small-signal current.
    pub input_resistance: f64,
    /// Resistance (Ω) at the output with every independent source zeroed.
    /// For a voltage output it is the resistance between the output node
    /// and its reference; for a current output, the resistance in series
    /// with the measuring source.
    pub output_resistance: f64,
    /// Configuration used to produce this result.
    pub config: TfConfig,
}

/// Runs a DC small-signal transfer-function analysis, as SPICE's `.tf`.
///
/// # Algorithm
///
/// 1. Solve the DC operating point of `circuit` (capacitors and varactors
///    open, inductors and transformer windings shorted).
/// 2. Linearise every nonlinear element at that operating point, as
///    [`solve_ac`](crate::ac_analysis::solve_ac) does at ω = 0. A relay's
///    contact is open or closed as the bias point leaves it.
/// 3. Excite the input source with a unit signal, everything else zero,
///    and read the output: that is the gain. The input source's own
///    response gives the input resistance.
/// 4. Drive a unit test current into the output (or a unit voltage on a
///    current output's source) and read the response: that is the output
///    resistance.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// - [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] if the input is not an independent
///   voltage or current source, the output node is not in the circuit, or
///   a current output does not name an independent voltage source. These
///   are checked before the DC solve, so a misspelt name isn't hidden by a
///   DC failure
/// - Any [`SimError`] from the DC operating-point solve
/// - [`SimError::SingularMatrix`] if the linearised system is singular
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```
/// use sindr::{Circuit, CircuitElement};
/// use sindr::transfer_function::{solve_tf, TfConfig, TfOutput};
/// use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};
///
/// // A 1 kΩ / 3 kΩ divider: gain 3/4, Rin 4 kΩ, Rout 1k ‖ 3k = 750 Ω.
/// let circuit = Circuit {
///     ground_node: "0".into(),
///     components: vec![
///         CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
///             id: "V1".into(),
///             nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
///             voltage: 1.0,
///             waveform: None,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "R1".into(),
///             nodes: ["in".into(), "out".into()],
///             resistance: 1_000.0,
///         }),
///         CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
///             id: "R2".into(),
///             nodes: ["out".into(), "0".into()],
///             resistance: 3_000.0,
///         }),
///     ],
///     ..Default::default()
/// };
///
/// let config = TfConfig::new(TfOutput::voltage("out"), "V1");
/// let tf = solve_tf(&circuit, &config)?;
/// assert!((tf.gain - 0.75).abs() < 1e-9);
/// assert!((tf.input_resistance - 4_000.0).abs() < 1e-6);
/// assert!((tf.output_resistance - 750.0).abs() < 1e-6);
/// # Ok::<(), sindr::SimError>(())
/// ```
///
pub fn solve_tf(circuit: &Circuit, config: &TfConfig) -> Result<TfResult, SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/validation.rs`

Pre-solve circuit validation.

Catches obvious topology mistakes (no ground, disconnected subgraphs,
floating nodes) and device values the models can't use (a junction
temperature at or below 0 K, a BJT `bf` at or below 0) before they reach
the solver, where the failure mode would be a less helpful "singular
matrix" or "invalid solution" error. Run automatically
by [`solve_circuit`](crate::solve_circuit); also exposed standalone via
[`validate_circuit`].

```rust
/// Validate a circuit before solving.
///
/// Checks are run in order of most-helpful-first:
/// 1. Ground node exists (at least one component touches it)
/// 2. All nodes reachable from ground (BFS connectivity)
/// 3. No floating nodes (every non-ground node has degree >= 2)
/// 4. Unique component ids
/// 5. Values the models can use: resistances, inductances and every
///    `temperature` (K) positive and finite, capacitances zero or more,
///    source values and controlled-source gains finite, a BJT's `bf`
///    positive and finite, and the device-model fields each check names
/// 6. A behavioural source's `i(src)` names a voltage-defined element
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns [`SimError::NoGround`] if no component terminal matches
/// `circuit.ground_node`.
///
/// Returns [`SimError::DisconnectedNodes`] listing nodes unreachable from
/// ground.
///
/// Returns [`SimError::FloatingNode`] naming the first node with fewer than
/// 2 connections.
///
/// Returns [`SimError::InvalidResistance`] for a resistor whose resistance
/// is zero, negative or not finite.
///
/// Returns [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] for a repeated id, or naming the
/// component, field and value for any other value out of range.
pub fn validate_circuit(circuit: &Circuit) -> Result<(), SimError> { … }
```

## `sindr/src/variation.rs`

Monte Carlo and corner analysis: how a circuit's measurements spread
when its parts vary within their tolerances.

A [`Tolerance`] says how one parameter of one component varies: by how
much, and with which [`Distribution`]. [`monte_carlo`] draws every
tolerance at random for each of its runs; [`corners`] sets each at its
low or high end, every combination or a chosen list. Both wrap any
analysis, as a closure from a [`Circuit`] to a result, and take each
[`Measurement`] on every run. A run that fails (a convergence failure,
say) is recorded, not fatal.

On top of the runs: [`VariationResult::check_specs`] judges each
[`Spec`] on every run (yield, and the run nearest or furthest past a
limit), and [`ratings_over`] checks every part's
[`Ratings`](crate::Ratings) on every run, reporting each at its worst
with the run, tolerance values and time behind it.

The draws come from a seeded generator, and each run's from its own
index, so a run repeats exactly from its seed whether runs go one after
another or, with the `parallel` feature, across threads.

```
use sindr::measure::{Measure, Measurement, Signal, Stat};
use sindr::variation::{monte_carlo, MonteCarloConfig, Parameter, Tolerance};
use sindr::{solve_op, Circuit, CircuitElement};
use sindr::element::{Resistor, VoltageSource};

let r = |id: &str, a: &str, b: &str| CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
    id: id.into(),
    nodes: [a.into(), b.into()],
    resistance: 10e3,
});
let divider = Circuit::new(
    "0",
    vec![
        CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
            id: "v1".into(),
            nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
            voltage: 10.0,
            waveform: None,
        }),
        r("r1", "in", "out"),
        r("r2", "out", "0"),
    ],
);
// Every resistor ±1 %, 3σ Gaussian.
let tolerances = Tolerance::on_every(&divider, Parameter::Resistance, 0.01);
let config = MonteCarloConfig::new(tolerances, 200).with_seed(7);
let vout = Measurement::new("vout", Measure::stat(Signal::v("out"), Stat::Avg));
let result = monte_carlo(&divider, &config, &[vout], solve_op)?;
let stats = result.stats("vout").unwrap();
assert!((stats.mean - 5.0).abs() < 0.01);
assert!(stats.min > 4.9 && stats.max < 5.1);
```

```rust
/// Which parameter of a component a [`Tolerance`] varies.
pub enum Parameter {
    /// A resistor's resistance (Ω).
    Resistance,
    /// A capacitor's capacitance (F).
    Capacitance,
    /// An inductor's inductance (H).
    Inductance,
    /// A voltage source's DC voltage (V).
    Voltage,
    /// A current source's DC current (A).
    Current,
}

/// How a [`Tolerance`]'s parameter is drawn in [`monte_carlo`].
pub enum Distribution {
    /// Evenly across `nominal·(1 ± relative)`.
    Uniform,
    /// Normal about the nominal, with the band `relative` at `sigmas`
    /// standard deviations: a 1 % part at 3σ has σ = 0.33 %. Unclipped, so
    /// a draw falls outside the band about 0.27 % of the time at 3σ.
    Gaussian {
        /// Standard deviations the band spans, above 0.
        sigmas: f64,
    },
}

/// How one parameter of one component varies.
pub struct Tolerance {
    /// The component's id, flattened (`x1.r3` inside an instance).
    pub component: String,
    /// Which of its parameters.
    pub parameter: Parameter,
    /// The band as a fraction of the nominal value, in `[0, 1)`: 0.05
    /// for 5 %.
    pub relative: f64,
    /// How [`monte_carlo`] draws within it.
    pub distribution: Distribution,
}

impl Tolerance {
    /// `parameter` of `component` within `relative`, Gaussian at 3σ, as
    /// a part's tolerance is usually specified.
    pub fn new(component: impl Into<String>, parameter: Parameter, relative: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The same, drawn uniformly across the band.
    pub fn uniform(component: impl Into<String>, parameter: Parameter, relative: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// With `distribution` in place of the default.
    pub fn with_distribution(mut self, distribution: Distribution) -> Self { … }

    /// A tolerance of `relative` on `parameter` of every component of
    /// `circuit` that has it, hierarchy included, each independent.
    pub fn on_every(circuit: &Circuit, parameter: Parameter, relative: f64) -> Vec<Tolerance> { … }
}

/// Configuration of a [`monte_carlo`] analysis.
pub struct MonteCarloConfig {
    /// What varies.
    pub tolerances: Vec<Tolerance>,
    /// Number of runs, at least 1.
    pub runs: usize,
    /// Seed of the draws: the same seed gives the same runs.
    pub seed: u64,
}

impl MonteCarloConfig {
    /// `runs` runs over `tolerances`, with seed 0.
    pub fn new(tolerances: Vec<Tolerance>, runs: usize) -> Self { … }

    /// With `seed` in place of 0.
    pub fn with_seed(mut self, seed: u64) -> Self { … }
}

/// Where a [`Tolerance`] sits in one corner of a [`corners`] analysis.
pub enum Corner {
    /// `nominal·(1 − relative)`.
    Low,
    /// The nominal value.
    Nominal,
    /// `nominal·(1 + relative)`.
    High,
}

/// Which corners a [`corners`] analysis runs.
pub enum Corners {
    /// Every low/high combination: 2ⁿ runs for n tolerances, at most
    /// [`MAX_CORNER_TOLERANCES`] of them.
    All,
    /// These corners, each a [`Corner`] per tolerance in order.
    List(Vec<Vec<Corner>>),
}

/// Most tolerances [`Corners::All`] takes: 2¹⁶ = 65 536 runs.
pub const MAX_CORNER_TOLERANCES: usize = 16;

/// One run of a [`monte_carlo`] or [`corners`] analysis.
pub struct VariationRun {
    /// Each tolerance's parameter value in this run, in order.
    pub values: Vec<f64>,
    /// Each measurement, in order, or why it couldn't be taken: the
    /// analysis failing gives every measurement its error.
    pub measurements: Vec<Result<f64, String>>,
}

/// One measurement's spread over the runs it could be taken on.
pub struct MeasurementStats {
    /// The measurement's name.
    pub name: String,
    /// Mean over the measured runs.
    pub mean: f64,
    /// Sample standard deviation (n − 1); 0 for one run.
    pub std_dev: f64,
    /// Smallest value.
    pub min: f64,
    /// Largest value.
    pub max: f64,
    /// Runs it was taken on.
    pub measured: usize,
    /// Runs it couldn't be taken on.
    pub failed: usize,
}

/// Result of a [`monte_carlo`] or [`corners`] analysis.
pub struct VariationResult {
    /// The tolerances, in the order each run's `values` follow.
    pub tolerances: Vec<Tolerance>,
    /// Every run, in order.
    pub runs: Vec<VariationRun>,
    /// One entry per measurement, in order. NaN statistics when no run
    /// could take it.
    pub stats: Vec<MeasurementStats>,
}

impl VariationResult {
    /// The statistics of the measurement called `name`.
    pub fn stats(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&MeasurementStats> { … }

    /// The fraction of runs whose measurement `name` lies in
    /// `[min, max]`; a run that couldn't take it fails. `None` for an
    /// unknown name.
    pub fn yield_within(&self, name: &str, min: f64, max: f64) -> Option<f64> { … }

    /// Each of `specs` judged on every run, by the measurement of the same
    /// name: how many runs pass, fail or couldn't be measured, the yield,
    /// and the run that came nearest a limit or went furthest past one.
    /// A spec whose measurement this result didn't take is all unmeasured.
    pub fn check_specs(&self, specs: &[Spec]) -> Vec<SpecSpread> { … }
}

/// One run picked out of a variation analysis: which, and the condition
/// behind it.
pub struct WorstRun {
    /// Index into the runs.
    pub run: usize,
    /// The value it gave.
    pub value: f64,
    /// Signed margin to the nearer limit, in the value's unit: negative is
    /// outside. `None` for a spec with no limits.
    pub margin: Option<f64>,
    /// Each tolerance's parameter value in that run: the condition.
    pub values: Vec<f64>,
}

/// One spec over the runs of a variation analysis.
pub struct SpecSpread {
    /// The spec's name (its measurement's).
    pub name: String,
    /// Runs within the limits.
    pub passed: usize,
    /// Runs outside them.
    pub failed: usize,
    /// Runs the measurement couldn't be taken on.
    pub unmeasured: usize,
    /// `passed` over every run, unmeasured ones counting as failures.
    pub yield_fraction: f64,
    /// The run nearest a limit, or furthest past one. `None` when no run
    /// was measured.
    pub worst: Option<WorstRun>,
}

/// Which runs a [`ratings_over`] analysis makes.
pub enum Sampling {
    /// Random draws, as [`monte_carlo`].
    MonteCarlo(MonteCarloConfig),
    /// Band ends, as [`corners`].
    Corners {
        /// What varies.
        tolerances: Vec<Tolerance>,
        /// Which corners.
        which: Corners,
    },
}

/// One part's rating at its worst over the runs of [`ratings_over`].
pub struct WorstRating {
    /// Component id, flattened.
    pub part: String,
    /// Which rating.
    pub rating: RatingKind,
    /// The limit; `None` when the part doesn't set it.
    pub limit: Option<f64>,
    /// The worst value over every run; `None` when sindr can't measure it.
    pub worst: Option<f64>,
    /// Margin left at the worst run, as a percentage of the limit
    /// (negative when exceeded); `None` when unverified.
    pub margin_percent: Option<f64>,
    /// Exceeded if any run exceeded it, unverified if it can't be checked,
    /// otherwise within.
    pub status: RatingStatus,
    /// The run with the worst value. `None` when no run gave one.
    pub run: Option<usize>,
    /// Each tolerance's parameter value in that run.
    pub values: Vec<f64>,
    /// When the worst value happened in that run (s); `None` for DC.
    pub time: Option<f64>,
    /// Runs in which it was exceeded.
    pub exceeded_runs: usize,
}

/// Result of [`ratings_over`].
pub struct RatingsSpread {
    /// The tolerances, in the order each `values` follows.
    pub tolerances: Vec<Tolerance>,
    /// Number of runs made.
    pub runs: usize,
    /// Runs whose analysis failed, with why. Their ratings are unknown.
    pub failed_runs: Vec<(usize, String)>,
    /// Each part and rating at its worst, in circuit order.
    pub checks: Vec<WorstRating>,
}

impl RatingsSpread {
    /// Ratings exceeded in at least one run.
    pub fn exceeded(&self) -> Vec<&WorstRating> { … }

    /// `true` only when every run solved and every rating stayed within
    /// its limit in all of them: nothing exceeded, nothing unverified.
    pub fn is_safe(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// The part and rating with the least margin left, or the most
    /// exceeded.
    pub fn tightest(&self) -> Option<&WorstRating> { … }
}

/// Runs `analysis` `config.runs` times, each with every tolerance drawn
/// afresh, and takes `measurements` on each result.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// [`SimError::InvalidComponent`] for a tolerance on a component that
/// isn't there or doesn't have its parameter, a relative band outside
/// `[0, 1)`, a Gaussian whose `sigmas` isn't above 0, or no runs. A run
/// that fails isn't an error: see [`VariationRun::measurements`].
pub fn monte_carlo<R, F>(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    config: &MonteCarloConfig,
    measurements: &[Measurement],
    analysis: F,
) -> Result<VariationResult, SimError>
where
    R: Measurable,
    F: Fn(&Circuit) -> Result<R, SimError> + Sync,
 { … }

/// Runs `analysis` with each tolerance at the low or high end of its band
/// (or nominal), for every combination or the listed ones, and takes
/// `measurements` on each result. A tolerance's distribution doesn't
/// matter here.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`monte_carlo`], and for more than [`MAX_CORNER_TOLERANCES`]
/// tolerances with [`Corners::All`], or a listed corner whose length isn't
/// the number of tolerances.
pub fn corners<R, F>(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    tolerances: &[Tolerance],
    which: &Corners,
    measurements: &[Measurement],
    analysis: F,
) -> Result<VariationResult, SimError>
where
    R: Measurable,
    F: Fn(&Circuit) -> Result<R, SimError> + Sync,
 { … }

/// Runs `analysis` over `sampling`'s runs and checks every part against
/// its [`Ratings`](crate::Ratings) in each, as [`check_ratings`]: each
/// part and rating at its worst over all of them, with the run, the
/// tolerance values and (for a transient) the time behind it.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// As [`monte_carlo`] or [`corners`] for a bad sampling. A run whose
/// analysis fails isn't an error: see [`RatingsSpread::failed_runs`].
pub fn ratings_over<F>(
    circuit: &Circuit,
    sampling: &Sampling,
    analysis: F,
) -> Result<RatingsSpread, SimError>
where
    F: Fn(&Circuit) -> Result<SimulationResult, SimError> + Sync,
 { … }
```

## `sindr/src/waveform.rs`

Time-varying waveform definitions for voltage/current sources.

Each waveform variant implements `evaluate(t)` returning the instantaneous
value at time `t`. When attached to a VoltageSource or CurrentSource via
`waveform: Some(w)`, the source value at each transient timestep becomes
`dc_offset + w.evaluate(t)` (where dc_offset is the existing `voltage`/`current` field),
evaluated at the step's end time. Transient snapshots report that value as
the source's voltage or current. A step that ends on a jump (a square, PWM
or zero-rise pulse edge) sees the value just before it; the next step
starts from the value after.

```rust
/// A time-varying waveform.
pub enum Waveform {
    /// Sinusoidal: amplitude * sin(2*pi*frequency*t + phase) + offset
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "sine"))]
    Sine {
        /// Peak amplitude (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
