        /// DC offset added to the sine (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
        /// Phase offset (radians). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        phase: f64, // radians
    },

    /// SPICE-compatible pulse waveform.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pulse"))]
    Pulse {
        /// Initial (low) value (V or A).
        v1: f64, // initial value
        /// Pulsed (high) value (V or A).
        v2: f64, // pulsed value
        /// Delay before the first pulse (s). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        delay: f64, // delay before first pulse (s)
        /// Rise time from `v1` to `v2` (s).
        rise_time: f64, // rise time (s)
        /// Fall time from `v2` back to `v1` (s).
        fall_time: f64, // fall time (s)
        /// Width of the high portion of the pulse (s).
        pulse_width: f64, // pulse width (s)
        /// Repetition period (s). Zero, negative or non-finite means a
        /// single pulse, as SPICE reads a zero period.
        period: f64, // period (s)
    },

    /// Square wave with configurable duty cycle.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "square"))]
    Square {
        /// Peak amplitude about the offset (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// DC offset added to the wave (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
        /// Duty cycle (fraction high), 0.0 to 1.0. Default 0.5.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_duty"))]
        duty: f64, // 0.0 to 1.0, default 0.5
    },

    /// Triangle wave.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "triangle"))]
    Triangle {
        /// Peak amplitude about the offset (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// DC offset added to the wave (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
    },

    /// PWM (pulse width modulation) — square wave with variable duty.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pwm"))]
    Pwm {
        /// High-level amplitude above the offset (V or A).
        amplitude: f64,
        /// Frequency (Hz).
        frequency: f64,
        /// Duty cycle (fraction high), 0.0 to 1.0.
        duty: f64, // 0.0 to 1.0
        /// DC offset (low level) (V or A). Default 0.
        #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
        offset: f64,
    },

    /// Piecewise-linear waveform. `points` is a list of `(t, value)`
    /// breakpoints sorted by `t`. Values are linearly interpolated between
    /// adjacent points; for `t < points[0].0` the first value is held, and
    /// for `t > points.last().0` the last value is held. An empty list
    /// evaluates to `0.0` everywhere.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pwl"))]
    Pwl {
        /// Breakpoints as `(time in s, value)` pairs sorted by time. The
        /// value is V or A, matching the source it drives.
        points: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
    },
}

/// Most breakpoints [`Waveform::breakpoints`] returns.
pub const MAX_BREAKPOINTS: usize = 10_000_000;

impl Waveform {
    /// The waveform's value at time `t` (s): volts on a voltage source,
    /// amperes on a current source.
    pub fn evaluate(&self, t: f64) -> f64 { … }

    /// Times in `(0, t_end)` (s) where this waveform has a corner or a jump:
    /// pulse edges, square/PWM transitions, triangle peaks, PWL points. A sine
    /// has none. Sorted; at most [`MAX_BREAKPOINTS`] of them.
    ///
    /// The transient stepper lands a step exactly on each one, so a fast
    /// edge between two steps isn't stepped over.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr::Waveform;
    ///
    /// let pulse = Waveform::Pulse {
    ///     v1: 0.0, v2: 5.0, delay: 1e-3, rise_time: 1e-9, fall_time: 1e-9,
    ///     pulse_width: 2e-3, period: 10e-3,
    /// };
    /// assert_eq!(pulse.breakpoints(5e-3), vec![1e-3, 1e-3 + 1e-9, 3e-3 + 1e-9, 3e-3 + 2e-9]);
    /// ```
    pub fn breakpoints(&self, t_end: f64) -> Vec<f64> { … }

    /// [`Self::breakpoints`], and whether some were dropped to keep to
    /// [`MAX_BREAKPOINTS`].
    pub fn capped_breakpoints(&self, t_end: f64) -> (Vec<f64>, bool) { … }

    /// Return the period of this waveform in seconds, if periodic. `None`
    /// for a single pulse (period zero, negative or non-finite), PWL, and a
    /// frequency that isn't positive.
    pub fn period(&self) -> Option<f64> { … }
}
```


# Public API of `sindr-devices`

## `sindr-devices/src/battery.rs`

Equivalent-circuit battery: open-circuit voltage by state of charge,
series resistance and an optional RC pair.

```text
 +  ──[ R0 ]──┬──[ R1 ]──┬──(OCV(SoC))──  −
              └──[ C1 ]──┘
```

The terminal voltage is `OCV(SoC) − R0·i − v1`, with `i` the discharge
current (out of the positive terminal) and `v1` the RC pair's voltage,
`C1·dv1/dt = i − v1/R1`. The pair gives the slow sag and recovery after
a load step. State of charge falls as `dSoC/dt = −i/(3600·capacity)`.

Aging, temperature and current-dependent capacity (Peukert) are not
modelled.

```rust
/// The RC pair: the polarisation that makes a loaded cell sag over seconds
/// and recover after the load goes.
pub struct BatteryRc {
    /// Polarisation resistance (Ω).
    pub r: f64,
    /// Polarisation capacitance (F).
    pub c: f64,
}

/// A battery's equivalent circuit.
pub struct BatteryParams {
    /// Capacity (Ah): the charge from full (SoC 1) to empty (SoC 0).
    pub capacity: f64,
    /// Open-circuit (rest) voltage against state of charge: `(SoC, volts)`
    /// pairs with SoC rising from 0 to 1, read by linear interpolation.
    pub ocv: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
    /// Series (ohmic) resistance (Ω), positive.
    pub r_series: f64,
    /// Optional RC pair for the slow part of the sag.
    #[cfg_attr(
        feature = "serde",
        serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")
    )]
    pub rc: Option<BatteryRc>,
}

impl BatteryParams {
    /// A cell with a flat `volts` at every state of charge.
    pub fn constant(volts: f64, capacity: f64, r_series: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A single lithium-ion or lithium-polymer cell: a typical rest-voltage
    /// curve, 3.27 V empty to 4.20 V full (3.84 V at half charge), with the
    /// capacity (Ah) and series resistance (Ω) of the part. A small pouch
    /// cell is around 0.1–0.3 Ω, an 18650 around 0.03–0.05 Ω.
    pub fn lithium_ion(capacity: f64, r_series: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A CR2032-class lithium coin cell: 225 mAh, about 3.0 V for most of
    /// its life and falling off over the last tenth, with 15 Ω series
    /// resistance and a 25 Ω, 0.2 F pulse-recovery pair. Approximate,
    /// from typical published discharge curves; a coin cell's resistance
    /// rises steeply as it empties and in the cold, which isn't modelled.
    pub fn cr2032() -> Self { … }
}

/// Open-circuit voltage (V) at state of charge `soc`, interpolated along
/// the curve. Outside 0..1 it holds the end values.
pub fn open_circuit_voltage(soc: f64, params: &BatteryParams) -> f64 { … }

/// The resistance (Ω) a battery shows at DC: `R0`, plus `R1` once the RC
/// pair has settled.
pub fn dc_resistance(params: &BatteryParams) -> f64 { … }

/// State of charge after `amp_hours` (Ah) is drawn from `soc`.
pub fn discharged(soc: f64, amp_hours: f64, params: &BatteryParams) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/bjt.rs`

BJT (Bipolar Junction Transistor) device model.

Ebers–Moll companion model with Early voltage. Produces a 3×3 conductance
/ current contribution that an MNA solver stamps for [base, collector,
emitter] terminals at each Newton–Raphson iteration.

Both NPN and PNP are supported via [`BjtKind`]; the PNP case mirrors NPN
through sign conventions on `vbe` and `vbc`.

```rust
/// BJT polarity.
pub enum BjtKind {
    /// NPN (electrons are majority carriers in base region).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "npn"))]
    Npn,
    /// PNP (holes are majority carriers in base region).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pnp"))]
    Pnp,
}

/// Operating region of a BJT — useful for diagnostics and circuit
/// classification (amplifier biased "active", switch in "saturation", …).
pub enum BjtRegion {
    /// Both junctions reverse-biased — negligible currents.
    Cutoff,
    /// Forward-active: BE forward-biased, BC reverse-biased. Linear amplifier region.
    Active,
    /// Both junctions forward-biased — output voltage clamped near `VCE_sat`.
    Saturation,
}

impl BjtRegion {
    /// Lowercase string label for the region (`"cutoff"`, `"active"`, `"saturation"`).
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str { … }
}

/// Ebers–Moll model parameters for a BJT.
pub struct BjtParams {
    /// Saturation current (A).
    pub is: f64, // Saturation current (A)
    /// Forward current gain (unitless).
    pub bf: f64, // Forward current gain
    /// Forward emission coefficient (unitless).
    pub nf: f64, // Forward emission coefficient
    /// Reverse current gain (unitless).
    pub br: f64, // Reverse current gain
    /// Reverse emission coefficient (unitless).
    pub nr: f64, // Reverse emission coefficient
    /// Forward Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite (no Early effect).
    pub vaf: f64, // Forward Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite (no Early effect).
    /// Reverse Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite.
    pub var: f64, // Reverse Early voltage (V). 0.0 = infinite.
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`BjtParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given.
    pub temperature: f64, // Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C.
}

impl BjtParams {
    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Construct default Ebers–Moll parameters for the given forward gain `bf`.
    pub fn new(bf: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// Companion model output for one NR iteration.
/// Contains conductances and equivalent currents for MNA stamping.
pub struct BjtCompanion {
    /// B–E forward junction conductance (S).
    pub g_be: f64, // B-E forward junction conductance
    /// B–C reverse junction conductance (S).
    pub g_bc: f64, // B-C reverse junction conductance
    /// Early-voltage output conductance between C and E (S).
    pub g_ce: f64, // Early voltage output conductance between C and E
    /// Collector current at the operating point (A), into the collector, in
    /// the NPN frame: a PNP caller negates it for the physical current.
    pub ic: f64, // collector current at operating point
    /// Base current at the operating point (A), into the base, NPN frame.
    pub ib: f64, // base current at operating point
    /// B–E junction voltage at the operating point (V), for RHS computation.
    pub vbe: f64, // junction voltage (for RHS computation)
    /// B–C junction voltage at the operating point (V), for RHS computation.
    pub vbc: f64, // junction voltage (for RHS computation)
}

/// Evaluate the Ebers–Moll transport model at junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc`
/// (V, sign-adjusted for PNP by the caller), returning the linearised
/// [`BjtCompanion`] for MNA stamping.
///
/// `g_be` and `g_bc` are the exact slopes of the junction currents, with no
/// cap: overshoot is left to the solver's junction voltage limiting. For the
/// full terminal Jacobian, Early effect included, use
/// [`bjt_terminal_jacobian`].
pub fn bjt_companion(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> BjtCompanion { … }

/// Base and collector currents `(ib, ic)` (A), each into its terminal, at
/// junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc` (V). Both are in the NPN frame: for a PNP,
/// pass the negated junction voltages and negate the currents. Includes the
/// Early effect the DC solve applies: `ic = i_tr + |i_tr|/VAF · vce` with
/// `vce = vbe − vbc`.
///
/// This is the large-signal model that [`bjt_terminal_jacobian`]
/// differentiates. The emitter current is `−(ib + ic)`.
pub fn bjt_terminal_currents(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Exact small-signal Jacobian of the BJT terminal currents with respect to
/// the junction voltages, at one operating point.
///
/// These are the true derivatives of [`bjt_terminal_currents`], Early effect
/// included, valid in every region (cutoff, forward-active, saturation,
/// reverse-active). The DC stamp and AC analysis both use them.
///
/// In terms of the node voltages, with `vbe = vb − ve` and `vbc = vb − vc`:
/// `∂I/∂vb = ∂I/∂vbe + ∂I/∂vbc`, `∂I/∂vc = −∂I/∂vbc`, `∂I/∂ve = −∂I/∂vbe`.
/// These entries are the same for NPN and PNP: the polarity sign cancels.
pub struct BjtJacobian {
    /// ∂Ib/∂Vbe (S).
    pub dib_dvbe: f64,
    /// ∂Ib/∂Vbc (S).
    pub dib_dvbc: f64,
    /// ∂Ic/∂Vbe (S).
    pub dic_dvbe: f64,
    /// ∂Ic/∂Vbc (S).
    pub dic_dvbc: f64,
}

impl BjtJacobian {
    /// The 3×3 terminal conductance matrix `∂(Ib, Ic, Ie)/∂(Vb, Vc, Ve)`,
    /// rows and columns ordered [base, collector, emitter]. Rows and columns
    /// each sum to zero (KCL and invariance to a common-mode shift).
    pub fn terminal_matrix(&self) -> [[f64; 3]; 3] { … }
}

/// Evaluate the exact terminal Jacobian of [`bjt_terminal_currents`] at
/// junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc` (V, sign-adjusted for PNP).
pub fn bjt_terminal_jacobian(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> BjtJacobian { … }

/// The derivatives of a BJT's terminal currents and of its terminal Jacobian
/// with respect to one parameter, at fixed junction voltages, in the NPN
/// frame: a PNP caller negates the currents and keeps the Jacobian, as for
/// [`bjt_terminal_currents`] and [`bjt_terminal_jacobian`].
pub struct BjtDerivative {
    /// ∂Ib/∂p: base current (A) per unit of the parameter.
    pub ib: f64,
    /// ∂Ic/∂p: collector current (A) per unit of the parameter.
    pub ic: f64,
    /// ∂J/∂p: each entry of the [`BjtJacobian`] (S) per unit of the
    /// parameter.
    pub jacobian: BjtJacobian,
}

/// [`BjtDerivative`]s with respect to each parameter of [`BjtParams`] the
/// DC model uses, from [`bjt_derivatives`].
pub struct BjtDerivatives {
    /// With respect to `is` (per A).
    pub is: BjtDerivative,
    /// With respect to `bf`.
    pub bf: BjtDerivative,
    /// With respect to `br`.
    pub br: BjtDerivative,
    /// With respect to `nf`.
    pub nf: BjtDerivative,
    /// With respect to `nr`.
    pub nr: BjtDerivative,
    /// With respect to `vaf` (per V). Zero while the Early effect is off
    /// (`vaf` of 0 or infinite).
    pub vaf: BjtDerivative,
}

/// The exact derivatives of [`bjt_terminal_currents`] and
/// [`bjt_terminal_jacobian`] at junction voltages `vbe`/`vbc` (V,
/// sign-adjusted for PNP) with respect to each parameter, for sensitivity
/// analysis.
pub fn bjt_derivatives(vbe: f64, vbc: f64, params: &BjtParams) -> BjtDerivatives { … }

/// Detect operating region from junction voltages.
pub fn detect_region(vbe: f64, vbc: f64) -> BjtRegion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/datasheet.rs`

Datasheet figures a device model can be fitted to.

A datasheet gives a part's characteristics as figures at test
conditions: a diode's forward voltage at a current, a transistor's gain
at a collector current, a MOSFET's threshold at a drain current. These
structs hold such figures as an editor's parts library stores them:
quantities in volts, amps, ohms or plain ratios, each figure with its
minimum, typical and maximum as separate optional values. The
`from_datasheet` constructors next to each model fit the model through
them: [`MosfetParams::from_datasheet`](crate::mosfet::MosfetParams::from_datasheet)
here, and the diode, LED, zener and BJT ones on `sindr`'s `DiodeModel`
and `BjtModel`.

A figure's [`nominal`](DatasheetValue::nominal) value is what a fit
uses: the typical value, else the middle of minimum and maximum, else
whichever of the two is given.

```rust
/// One datasheet figure: its minimum, typical and maximum, any of which
/// may be missing. All in the same unit, the base unit of the quantity
/// (V, A, Ω) or a plain ratio.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct DatasheetValue {
    /// Minimum.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub min: Option<f64>,
    /// Typical.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub typ: Option<f64>,
    /// Maximum.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub max: Option<f64>,
}

impl DatasheetValue {
    /// A figure with only a typical value.
    pub fn typical(typ: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// A figure given as a range.
    pub fn range(min: f64, max: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// The value a fit uses: the typical value, else the middle of minimum
    /// and maximum, else whichever of them is given. `None` when the figure
    /// is empty.
    pub fn nominal(&self) -> Option<f64> { … }

    /// Whether no value is given.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// [`nominal`](Self::nominal), for the figure named `figure`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DatasheetError::Missing`] naming `figure` when it's empty;
    /// [`DatasheetError::Invalid`] when it isn't finite.
    pub fn require(&self, figure: &'static str) -> Result<f64, DatasheetError> { … }
}

/// Why a model can't be fitted to datasheet figures.
pub enum DatasheetError {
    /// A figure the fit needs is missing.
    Missing {
        /// The figure, as the struct's field names it.
        figure: &'static str,
    },
    /// A figure is out of range: a current that isn't positive, a second
    /// forward point below the first.
    Invalid {
        /// The figure.
        figure: &'static str,
        /// What's wrong with it.
        reason: &'static str,
    },
}

/// A diode's or LED's forward characteristic: `vf` at `if_`, and
/// optionally a second point `vf2` at `if2`.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`.
pub struct DiodeDatasheet {
    /// Forward voltage Vf (V) at [`if_`](Self::if_).
    pub vf: DatasheetValue,
    /// Test current If (A), positive.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "if"))]
    pub if_: f64,
    /// A second forward voltage (V), at [`if2`](Self::if2). With it the
    /// emission coefficient is fitted too.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vf2: Option<DatasheetValue>,
    /// The second point's test current (A), positive and not `if_`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub if2: Option<f64>,
}

impl DiodeDatasheet {
    /// `vf` (V) at `if_` (A).
    pub fn new(vf: impl Into<DatasheetValue>, if_: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds a second point, `vf2` (V) at `if2` (A).
    pub fn with_second_point(mut self, vf2: impl Into<DatasheetValue>, if2: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// A zener's breakdown: `vz` at the test current `iz`.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`.
pub struct ZenerDatasheet {
    /// Zener voltage Vz (V), positive, at [`iz`](Self::iz).
    pub vz: DatasheetValue,
    /// Test current Iz (A), positive: 5 mA for a BZX84, 20 mA for many
    /// 1N47xx parts.
    pub iz: f64,
}

impl ZenerDatasheet {
    /// `vz` (V) at `iz` (A).
    pub fn new(vz: impl Into<DatasheetValue>, iz: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// A bipolar transistor's gain and saturation: `hfe` at `hfe_ic`, and
/// optionally `vce_sat` at `vce_sat_ic` with base current `vce_sat_ib`.
/// Currents are magnitudes, the same for an NPN and a PNP.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`.
pub struct BjtDatasheet {
    /// DC current gain hFE (ratio), at [`hfe_ic`](Self::hfe_ic).
    pub hfe: DatasheetValue,
    /// The collector current hFE is given at (A). The Ebers–Moll model's
    /// gain doesn't change with current, so this is kept for the record
    /// and doesn't move the fit; 0 when not given.
    pub hfe_ic: f64,
    /// Collector–emitter saturation voltage (V), at
    /// [`vce_sat_ic`](Self::vce_sat_ic) and
    /// [`vce_sat_ib`](Self::vce_sat_ib).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vce_sat: Option<DatasheetValue>,
    /// The collector current Vce(sat) is given at (A).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vce_sat_ic: Option<f64>,
    /// The base current Vce(sat) is given at (A); typically `ic / 10`.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub vce_sat_ib: Option<f64>,
}

impl BjtDatasheet {
    /// `hfe` at `ic` (A).
    pub fn new(hfe: impl Into<DatasheetValue>, ic: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Adds Vce(sat) `vce_sat` (V) at collector current `ic` and base
    /// current `ib` (A).
    pub fn with_vce_sat(mut self, vce_sat: impl Into<DatasheetValue>, ic: f64, ib: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// A MOSFET's threshold and on-resistance: gate threshold `vth` at drain
/// current `vth_id` (with the gate tied to the drain, as datasheets
/// measure it), and `rds_on` at gate–source voltage `rds_on_vgs`,
/// optionally at drain current `rds_on_id`.
///
/// Voltages and currents are read as magnitudes, so a P-channel part's
/// figures may be given with the datasheet's minus signs or without.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`.
pub struct MosfetDatasheet {
    /// Gate threshold voltage Vgs(th) (V), at [`vth_id`](Self::vth_id).
    pub vth: DatasheetValue,
    /// The drain current the threshold is given at (A): 250 µA or 1 mA on
    /// most datasheets.
    pub vth_id: f64,
    /// Drain–source on-resistance Rds(on) (Ω), at
    /// [`rds_on_vgs`](Self::rds_on_vgs).
    pub rds_on: DatasheetValue,
    /// The gate–source voltage Rds(on) is given at (V).
    pub rds_on_vgs: f64,
    /// The drain current Rds(on) is given at (A). Without it the fit uses
    /// the on-resistance at a vanishing drain current.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub rds_on_id: Option<f64>,
}

impl MosfetDatasheet {
    /// Threshold `vth` (V) at `vth_id` (A), and on-resistance `rds_on`
    /// (Ω) at `rds_on_vgs` (V).
    pub fn new(
        vth: impl Into<DatasheetValue>,
        vth_id: f64,
        rds_on: impl Into<DatasheetValue>,
        rds_on_vgs: f64,
    ) -> Self { … }

    /// Sets [`rds_on_id`](Self::rds_on_id).
    pub fn with_rds_on_id(mut self, id: f64) -> Self { … }
}
```

## `sindr-devices/src/diode.rs`

Diode model: Shockley equation, companion model, voltage limiting.

Provides the mathematical foundation for Newton-Raphson simulation
of diodes and LEDs. Each NR iteration linearizes the diode at its
current operating point into a companion conductance + current source.

```rust
/// Boltzmann constant over the elementary charge, k/q (V/K).
pub const K_OVER_Q: f64 = 8.617_333_262e-5;

/// Nominal temperature (K) the device parameters are given at: 27 °C.
pub const T_NOM: f64 = 300.15;

/// Thermal voltage kT/q at the nominal temperature [`T_NOM`] (V).
pub const V_T: f64 = K_OVER_Q * T_NOM;

/// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at temperature `t` (K).
pub fn thermal_voltage(t: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// Minimum conductance shunt to prevent singular Jacobian in reverse bias.
pub const GMIN: f64 = 1e-12;

/// Diode parameters (Shockley model).
pub struct DiodeParams {
    /// Saturation current (A).
    pub is: f64,
    /// Emission coefficient (dimensionless).
    pub n: f64,
    /// Series resistance (Ω). Default 0.0 — no effect on existing models.
    pub rs: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`DiodeParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given, so scale it with
    /// [`temperature_scale_is`] for a junction away from [`T_NOM`].
    pub temperature: f64,
    /// Reverse breakdown (SPICE `BV`/`IBV`). `None`: the junction never
    /// breaks down, as in SPICE without `BV`.
    pub breakdown: Option<Breakdown>,
}

/// Reverse breakdown of a diode, as a SPICE card's `BV` and `IBV` give it.
///
/// Breakdown adds `−IS·exp(−(v_j + xbv)/(N·V_T))` to the junction current,
/// with `xbv` fitted as ngspice fits it: the current at `v_j = −bv` is
/// `−ibv`, less about `IS·bv/V_T` that ngspice's fit carries. Away from the
/// knee this is the ngspice current to within `IS`.
pub struct Breakdown {
    /// Breakdown voltage BV (V), positive.
    pub bv: f64,
    /// Current at `−bv`, IBV (A), positive. SPICE's default is 1 mA.
    pub ibv: f64,
}

impl DiodeParams {
    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Standard silicon diode: IS = 1e-14 A, N = 1.0.
    pub fn silicon() -> Self { … }

    /// LED with a given forward voltage (V) at 20 mA.
    ///
    /// IS is derived from the Shockley equation: IS = 0.020 / (exp(Vf / (N * VT)) - 1)
    /// with N = 2.0 (typical LED emission coefficient).
    pub fn led(forward_voltage: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// LED parameters by colour name, case ignored, as
    /// [`led::COLORS`](crate::led::COLORS) lists them. Unknown names are red.
    pub fn for_led_color(color: &str) -> Self { … }
}

/// Scale saturation current IS for junction temperature.
///
/// IS(T) = IS(T0) * (T/T0)^(XTI/N) * exp(Eg / (N * k/q) * (1/T0 - 1/T))
///
/// This is the SPICE formula. For a BJT, SPICE scales IS with N = 1.
///
/// Arguments:
/// - `is_t0`: IS at reference temperature T0 (A)
/// - `t`: Junction temperature (K)
/// - `t0`: Reference temperature (K), typically [`T_NOM`]
/// - `eg`: Bandgap energy (eV): 1.11 for Si, 0.69 for Ge, 1.42 for GaAs
/// - `xti`: Temperature exponent: SPICE's default is 3.0 for diodes and BJTs
/// - `n`: Emission coefficient (1.0 for a BJT)
pub fn temperature_scale_is(is_t0: f64, t: f64, t0: f64, eg: f64, xti: f64, n: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// Compute the companion model (linearised) at operating point `v_d`.
///
/// Returns `(g_d, i_eq)` where:
/// - `g_d` is the companion conductance (dI/dV at v_d), floored at [`GMIN`]
/// - `i_eq` is the companion current source (I_d - g_d * v_d)
///
/// `i_eq` is built from the same floored `g_d`, so `g_d * v_d + i_eq` is
/// always the diode current: the floor shapes the Newton steps in deep
/// reverse bias without adding a GMIN leakage to the converged current.
///
/// These stamp into MNA exactly like a resistor (g_d) and current source (i_eq).
///
/// When `params.rs > 0`, `v_d` is the terminal voltage across junction and
/// series resistance together. The junction voltage is solved from
/// `I = IS * (exp((v_d - I*RS) / (N*V_T)) - 1)`, with V_T at
/// `params.temperature`, and the terminal conductance `g_j / (1 + RS*g_j)`
/// is returned, so `g_d * v_d + i_eq` is the terminal current at `v_d`.
///
/// Units and signs: `v_d` is anode − cathode (V), `g_d` is in S and `i_eq`
/// in A, both for current flowing anode → cathode.
pub fn diode_companion(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Compute the diode current (A, anode → cathode) at terminal voltage
/// `v_d` (V, anode − cathode), including the drop across `params.rs`.
pub fn diode_current(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> f64 { … }

/// Current (A) and conductance (S) of the junction itself at junction
/// voltage `v_j`: Shockley, plus the breakdown branch when `params` has one.
pub fn junction_current(v_j: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Charge-storage parameters of a junction, as a SPICE diode card's `CJO`,
/// `VJ`, `M`, `FC` and `TT` give them. The default stores no charge.
pub struct JunctionCharge {
    /// Zero-bias depletion capacitance CJO (F). Default 0.
    pub cjo: f64,
    /// Junction potential VJ (V). Default 1.
    pub vj: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient M, in `[0, 1)`. Default 0.5.
    pub m: f64,
    /// Forward-bias depletion coefficient FC, in `[0, 1)`: above `FC·VJ` the
    /// depletion capacitance is continued linearly. Default 0.5.
    pub fc: f64,
    /// Transit time TT (s): the diffusion charge is `TT·I_d`. Default 0.
    pub tt: f64,
}

impl JunctionCharge {
    /// Whether the junction stores any charge at all.
    pub fn is_none(&self) -> bool { … }

    /// The slope dC/dv (F/V) of the depletion capacitance at junction
    /// voltage `v` (V): the diffusion part, `TT·g_d`, is the caller's.
    pub fn depletion_capacitance_slope(&self, v: f64) -> f64 { … }

    /// Stored charge (C) and capacitance dQ/dV (F) at junction voltage `v`
    /// (V), carrying current `i_d` (A) with conductance `g_d` (S).
    ///
    /// The SPICE junction charge: depletion `CJO·VJ·(1 − (1 − v/VJ)^(1−M))/(1−M)`
    /// up to `FC·VJ`, continued with a linear capacitance above it so it
    /// stays finite in forward bias, plus diffusion `TT·I_d`.
    pub fn charge(&self, v: f64, i_d: f64, g_d: f64) -> (f64, f64) { … }
}

/// The junction behind RS at terminal voltage `v_d` (V): its conductance
/// `g_j` (S) and capacitance `c_j` (F). In AC the diode is RS in series with
/// `g_j + jωC_j`.
pub fn junction_small_signal(
    v_d: f64,
    params: &DiodeParams,
    charge: &JunctionCharge,
) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Stored charge (C) and its derivative with respect to the terminal
/// voltage (F) of a diode at terminal voltage `v_d` (V, anode − cathode).
///
/// The charge is the junction's at the junction voltage the diode current
/// sets across RS. The drop the charging current itself makes across RS is
/// left out, so with RS > 0 the charge sits across the terminals.
pub fn diode_charge(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams, charge: &JunctionCharge) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Critical voltage for voltage limiting.
///
/// V_crit = N * V_T * ln(N * V_T / (sqrt(2) * IS)), with `vt` the thermal
/// voltage at the junction temperature.
pub fn critical_voltage(is: f64, n: f64, vt: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// SPICE-style voltage limiting to prevent NR overshoot.
///
/// If the proposed new voltage `v_new` exceeds V_crit above `v_old`,
/// the step is compressed logarithmically to keep the exponential
/// in the Shockley equation from overflowing. `vt` is the thermal voltage at
/// the junction temperature.
pub fn limit_voltage(v_new: f64, v_old: f64, v_crit: f64, n: f64, vt: f64) -> f64 { … }

/// The derivatives of a diode's operating point with respect to one of its
/// parameters, at a fixed terminal voltage: what a sensitivity analysis
/// needs of the device.
pub struct DiodeDerivative {
    /// ∂I/∂p: terminal current (A, anode → cathode) per unit of the
    /// parameter.
    pub current: f64,
    /// ∂v_j/∂p: voltage across the junction behind RS (V) per unit of the
    /// parameter.
    pub junction_voltage: f64,
    /// ∂g_j/∂p: the junction's conductance (S) per unit of the parameter.
    pub junction_conductance: f64,
}

/// [`DiodeDerivative`]s with respect to each parameter of [`DiodeParams`]
/// that shapes the DC curve, from [`diode_derivatives`].
pub struct DiodeDerivatives {
    /// With respect to `is` (per A), `n` held.
    pub is: DiodeDerivative,
    /// With respect to `n`, `is` held.
    pub n: DiodeDerivative,
    /// With respect to `rs` (per Ω).
    pub rs: DiodeDerivative,
}

/// The exact derivatives of the diode at terminal voltage `v_d` (V, anode −
/// cathode) with respect to `params.is`, `params.n` and `params.rs`, the
/// breakdown branch included: the junction voltage moves with the parameter
/// so that `v_j + RS·I = v_d` still holds.
///
/// `is` and `n` are taken as they are in `params`; a caller whose IS follows
/// temperature chains through its own scaling.
pub fn diode_derivatives(v_d: f64, params: &DiodeParams) -> DiodeDerivatives { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/igbt.rs`

IGBT (Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor) simplified model.

An IGBT combines MOSFET gate control with BJT output characteristics.
This educational model uses the MOSFET Level-1 square law for the
collector current, and blocks reverse collector-emitter voltage.

Nodes: [gate, collector, emitter] — same ordering convention as BJT.
Gate controls current like a MOSFET; collector/emitter behave like BJT.

Simplified model is appropriate for educational simulation.
Full IGBT models (IGBTv3) have 20+ parameters — out of scope.

```rust
/// IGBT parameters (simplified model).
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct IgbtParams {
    /// Gate threshold voltage (V). Typical: 4.0–6.0 V.
    pub vth: f64,
    /// Transconductance parameter (A/V²). Typical: 5.0.
    pub k: f64,
    /// On-state collector-emitter saturation voltage (V). Typical: 2.0.
    ///
    /// Not used by the current I–V model: the collector current follows the
    /// square law alone. Kept so existing circuits still deserialize.
    pub vce_sat: f64,
}

/// IGBT companion model output.
pub struct IgbtCompanion {
    /// Transconductance ∂Ids/∂Vge (S).
    pub gm: f64,
    /// Output conductance ∂Ids/∂Vce (S): zero in saturation and cutoff.
    pub g_ce: f64,
    /// Collector current at the operating point (A), collector → emitter.
    pub ids: f64,
    /// Companion current source value for MNA stamping (A), collector →
    /// emitter: `ids − gm·vge − g_ce·vce`.
    pub i_eq: f64,
}

/// Evaluate IGBT companion model at gate-emitter voltage `vge` and
/// collector-emitter voltage `vce`.
///
/// Collector current (MOSFET Level-1), with `vov = vge − vth`:
/// - cutoff (`vov ≤ 0`) or reverse (`vce ≤ 0`): 0
/// - saturation (`vce ≥ vov`): `K/2 · vov²`
/// - triode (`0 < vce < vov`): `K · (vov − vce/2) · vce`
///
/// `gm` and `g_ce` are the exact partial derivatives of that current, so the
/// linearisation `Ic ≈ gm·vge + g_ce·vce + i_eq` is a Newton step. The stamp
/// puts `gm` in as a gate-controlled current source and `g_ce` as a C–E
/// conductance.
pub fn igbt_companion(vge: f64, vce: f64, params: &IgbtParams) -> IgbtCompanion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/inductor.rs`

Saturating inductor core: inductance that falls as the current rises.

A ferrite or iron core holds its initial inductance `L0` at small
currents and falls towards an air-core floor `l_sat` once the flux
approaches saturation. The flux linkage is

```text
λ(i) = l_sat·i + (L0 − l_sat)·i_sat·tanh(i / i_sat)
L(i) = dλ/di = l_sat + (L0 − l_sat)·sech²(i / i_sat)
```

so L is `L0` at zero current, `l_sat + 0.42·(L0 − l_sat)` at `i_sat`
and `l_sat + 0.07·(L0 − l_sat)` at `2·i_sat`. The curve is
single-valued: no hysteresis, remanence or core loss. Put a resistor in
series or parallel for loss.

A simulator integrates the flux (`v = dλ/dt`) and recovers the current
with [`current_from_flux`].

```rust
/// Saturation of an inductor whose small-signal inductance is `L0`.
pub struct InductorSaturation {
    /// Current (A) at which the core saturates: the knee of `tanh`. A
    /// datasheet's saturation current (the current at which L has fallen
    /// 20–30 %) is roughly `0.6·i_sat` here.
    pub i_sat: f64,
    /// Inductance (H) left once the core is fully saturated, positive and
    /// at most `L0`. An air-core winding keeps about `L0/μr`.
    pub l_sat: f64,
}

impl InductorSaturation {
    /// Saturation at `i_sat` (A), keeping a tenth of `l0` (H) when
    /// saturated.
    pub fn at(i_sat: f64, l0: f64) -> Self { … }
}

/// Flux linkage (Wb) of an inductor with small-signal inductance `l0` (H)
/// carrying `i` (A).
pub fn flux(i: f64, l0: f64, s: &InductorSaturation) -> f64 { … }

/// Incremental inductance `dλ/di` (H) at current `i` (A).
pub fn incremental_inductance(i: f64, l0: f64, s: &InductorSaturation) -> f64 { … }

/// The current (A) that carries flux `lambda` (Wb): the inverse of [`flux`].
///
/// λ(i) is odd and strictly increasing (its slope is at least `l_sat`), so
/// the root is unique. Newton's method from the saturated-line estimate,
/// kept inside a shrinking bracket, finds it to a relative 1e-12 in a few
/// iterations.
pub fn current_from_flux(lambda: f64, l0: f64, s: &InductorSaturation) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/jfet.rs`

JFET (Junction Field-Effect Transistor) device model.

Shichman–Hodges square-law model. N-channel and P-channel are both
supported via [`JfetKind`]; the P-channel case mirrors N-channel through
sign conventions on `vgs` and `vds`.

At each Newton–Raphson iteration, [`jfet_companion`] returns a
linearised contribution that an MNA solver stamps for the [gate, drain,
source] terminals.

```rust
/// JFET channel polarity.
pub enum JfetKind {
    /// N-channel JFET (pinch-off voltage `Vp < 0`).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "nchannel"))]
    NChannel,
    /// P-channel JFET (pinch-off voltage `Vp > 0`); sign-mirrored from N-channel.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pchannel"))]
    PChannel,
}

/// Linearised JFET companion model — the output of one Newton–Raphson
/// iteration ready for MNA stamping.
pub struct JfetCompanion {
    /// Transconductance `∂Id/∂Vgs` (S).
    pub gm: f64,
    /// Drain–source conductance `∂Id/∂Vds` (S).
    pub gds: f64,
    /// Equivalent Norton current for the MNA right-hand side (A), drain →
    /// source, in the N-channel frame (a P-channel caller negates it).
    pub i_eq: f64,
}

/// Compute JFET companion at operating point (vgs, vds).
/// Nodes order: [gate, drain, source] — same as MOSFET convention.
/// N-channel: Vp < 0 (typically -2 to -6 V), Idss > 0 (A). `vgs`, `vds` and
/// `vp` are in V.
///
/// In the ohmic region `gm = 2·Idss·Vds/Vp²` keeps its sign, so it is
/// negative when the drain is below the source.
///
/// P-channel is evaluated in the mirrored N-channel frame (`-vgs`, `-vds`,
/// `-|vp|`): `gm` and `gds` carry over to the physical device unchanged, but
/// `i_eq` is the mirrored frame's, so the physical Norton current is
/// `-i_eq`.
pub fn jfet_companion(vgs: f64, vds: f64, kind: JfetKind, idss: f64, vp: f64) -> JfetCompanion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/led.rs`

LED colour presets.

Maps common LED colours to their typical forward voltage, then derives
DiodeParams via the Shockley equation so LEDs can be stamped as nonlinear
diodes in any MNA solver.

[`LedColor`] has the five original colours. Colour names, amber and
orange included, are read by [`forward_voltage_of`] and
[`color_in`], which ignore case.

```rust
/// Common LED colour variants.
pub enum LedColor {
    /// Red LED (~1.8 V typical forward voltage).
    Red,
    /// Green LED (~2.2 V typical forward voltage).
    Green,
    /// Blue LED (~3.2 V typical forward voltage).
    Blue,
    /// Yellow LED (~2.0 V typical forward voltage).
    Yellow,
    /// White LED (~3.0 V typical forward voltage).
    White,
}

impl LedColor {
    /// Typical forward voltage (V) at 20 mA for this colour.
    pub fn forward_voltage(self) -> f64 { … }

    /// Parse from a lowercase string. Unknown strings default to `Red`.
    pub fn from_str(s: &str) -> Self { … }
}

/// Every colour name sindr knows, lowercase, with its typical forward
/// voltage (V) at 20 mA. Amber (≈ 590 nm) and orange (≈ 605 nm) parts are
/// AlInGaP, like most red and yellow indicators, and sit between red and
/// green: about 2.0–2.1 V at 20 mA on common 3 mm and 5 mm datasheets.
pub const COLORS: &[(&str, f64)] = &[
    ("red", 1.8),
    ("orange", 2.0),
    ("amber", 2.05),
    ("yellow", 2.0),
    ("green", 2.2),
    ("blue", 3.2),
    ("white", 3.0),
];

/// The typical forward voltage (V) at 20 mA of the colour `name`, case
/// ignored; `None` for a name sindr doesn't know.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr_devices::led::forward_voltage_of;
///
/// assert_eq!(forward_voltage_of("Amber"), Some(2.05));
/// assert_eq!(forward_voltage_of("ultraviolet"), None);
/// ```
pub fn forward_voltage_of(name: &str) -> Option<f64> { … }

/// The first colour word in `text`, as its lowercase name: `"LED red
/// 3mm"` is `"red"`. Words are split at anything but letters and digits,
/// and compared without case.
///
/// ```
/// use sindr_devices::led::color_in;
///
/// assert_eq!(color_in("LED Amber 5mm"), Some("amber"));
/// assert_eq!(color_in("Green"), Some("green"));
/// assert_eq!(color_in("LTST-C190"), None);
/// ```
pub fn color_in(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str> { … }

/// `DiodeParams` for a given LED colour.
pub fn led_params(color: LedColor) -> DiodeParams { … }

/// `DiodeParams` from a colour name, case ignored ([`COLORS`], amber and
/// orange included). Unknown names default to red.
pub fn led_params_from_str(color: &str) -> DiodeParams { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/lib.rs`

Pure-Rust electronics device physics: linearised companion models for
semiconductor and passive components used by MNA-based circuit simulators.

`sindr-devices` provides the small-signal linearisation that
Newton–Raphson solvers need at every iteration: given an applied voltage,
each device returns a `(g_eq, i_eq)` pair — an equivalent conductance and
Norton-current source. Stamp those into the MNA matrix and the solver
converges on the operating point.

This crate has **no dependency** on a particular solver. Use it standalone
if you're building your own MNA implementation, or pair it with the
companion crate [`sindr`](https://crates.io/crates/sindr) for an
end-to-end simulator.

### Devices

| Module | Device | Model |
|---|---|---|
| [`battery`] | Battery | Open-circuit voltage by state of charge, series R, optional RC pair |
| [`diode`] | Silicon diode | Shockley with series resistance, temperature IS scaling, breakdown and junction charge |
| [`bjt`] | BJT (NPN/PNP) | Ebers–Moll with Early voltage |
| [`mosfet`] | MOSFET (NMOS/PMOS) | Level-1 |
| [`jfet`] | JFET (N/P-channel) | Shichman–Hodges |
| [`igbt`] | IGBT | MOSFET gate control + BJT output conductance |
| [`led`] | LED | Diode with colour-dependent forward voltage |
| [`zener`] | Zener diode | Shockley + piecewise `1/rz` reverse-breakdown branch (sindr itself stamps a zener as a [`diode`] with `Breakdown`) |
| [`schottky`] | Schottky diode | Shockley with low-N, low-IS parameters |
| [`varactor`] | Varactor | Voltage-dependent junction capacitance |
| [`inductor`] | Saturating inductor core | `λ(i) = L_sat·i + (L₀ − L_sat)·I_sat·tanh(i/I_sat)` |
| [`thermistor`] | NTC thermistor | Beta model `R(T) = R₀·exp(β·(1/T − 1/T₀))` |
| [`photodiode`] | Photodiode | Diode + photocurrent offset |
| [`photoresistor`] | Photoresistor (LDR) | Light-level-dependent resistance |
| [`datasheet`] | Datasheet figures | Min/typ/max figures at test conditions that `from_datasheet` constructors fit models to |
| [`regulator`] | Linear voltage regulator | Piecewise linear: dropout, quiescent current, current limit, line and load regulation, positive or negative; LM7805 and AMS1117 presets |

### Quick example

```
use sindr_devices::diode::{DiodeParams, diode_companion};

let params = DiodeParams::silicon();          // IS=1e-14, N=1.0, rs=0.0
let v_applied = 0.65;                          // forward bias, volts
let (g_eq, i_eq) = diode_companion(v_applied, &params);

// Stamp g_eq into Y(p,p), Y(q,q), -g_eq into Y(p,q)/Y(q,p),
// and i_eq into b(p)/-i_eq into b(q) in your MNA system.
assert!(g_eq > 0.0);
```

### Conventions

- **Voltages and currents** are in SI units (V, A).
- **Temperature** is in kelvin. Default is 300.15 K (≈ 27 °C, the SPICE
  default). A junction's `vt()` is the thermal voltage kT/q at its own
  `temperature` ([`diode::thermal_voltage`]); its `is` is used as given,
  so scale it with [`diode::temperature_scale_is`] away from
  [`diode::T_NOM`].
- **Sign convention** for two-terminal companions: `v_applied` is the
  voltage from `nodes[0]` to `nodes[1]`, and `i_eq` is the current
  flowing into `nodes[0]`.
- **Companion form**: each `*_companion` function returns the linearised
  `(g_eq, i_eq)` at the operating point — the form Newton–Raphson stamps
  directly.

```rust
/// This crate's version, as in its `Cargo.toml`.
///
/// ```
/// assert_eq!(sindr_devices::VERSION, env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
/// ```
pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

pub mod battery;

pub mod bjt;

pub mod datasheet;

pub mod diode;

pub mod igbt;

pub mod inductor;

pub mod jfet;

pub mod led;

pub mod mosfet;

pub mod photodiode;

pub mod photoresistor;

pub mod regulator;

pub mod schottky;

pub mod thermistor;

pub mod varactor;

pub mod zener;
```

## `sindr-devices/src/mosfet.rs`

MOSFET Level 1 (Shichman-Hodges) model with body effect.

Implements NMOS and PMOS transistors with three operating regions:
cutoff, triode (linear), and saturation. The companion model linearizes
the device at each NR iteration for MNA stamping.

`sindr` treats every MOSFET as a three-terminal part with its body tied
to its source (Vbs = 0), so the body effect never applies there; the
model keeps it for callers that drive the body separately.

```rust
/// MOSFET type (NMOS or PMOS).
pub enum MosfetKind {
    /// N-channel MOSFET (electrons are majority carriers in the channel).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "nmos"))]
    Nmos,
    /// P-channel MOSFET (holes are majority carriers in the channel).
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(rename = "pmos"))]
    Pmos,
}

impl MosfetKind {
    /// Gate–source and drain–source voltages `(vgs, vds)` of a three-terminal
    /// MOSFET with node voltages `vg`, `vd`, `vs`, in the N-channel frame that
    /// [`mosfet_companion`] works in: mirrored (`vsg`, `vsd`) for a PMOS.
    ///
    /// A three-terminal MOSFET is a discrete part, whose body is tied to its
    /// source inside the package, so its `vbs` is always 0.
    pub fn nmos_frame(self, vg: f64, vd: f64, vs: f64) -> (f64, f64) { … }
}

/// Operating region of a MOSFET.
pub enum MosfetRegion {
    /// Below threshold — channel off, negligible drain current.
    Cutoff,
    /// Triode (linear) region — `Vds` below saturation, device acts as a voltage-controlled resistor.
    Triode,
    /// Saturation region — channel pinched off, drain current set by `Vgs`.
    Saturation,
}

impl MosfetRegion {
    /// Lowercase string label for the region (`"cutoff"`, `"triode"`, `"saturation"`).
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str { … }
}

/// MOSFET device parameters (Level 1 Shichman-Hodges).
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct MosfetParams {
    /// Transconductance parameter (A/V^2). SPICE KP parameter.
    pub kp: f64,
    /// Zero-bias threshold voltage (V). SPICE VTO parameter, signed as in
    /// SPICE: positive for an enhancement NMOS, negative for an enhancement
    /// PMOS (see [`MosfetParams::in_nmos_frame`]).
    pub vto: f64,
    /// Channel-length modulation (1/V). SPICE LAMBDA parameter.
    pub lambda: f64,
    /// Body effect coefficient (V^0.5). SPICE GAMMA parameter.
    pub gamma: f64,
    /// Surface potential (V). SPICE PHI parameter.
    pub phi: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise coefficient. Noise analysis puts `KF·|Id|^AF / f`
    /// (A²/Hz) across drain–source. sindr has no channel geometry, so this
    /// is SPICE's `KF/(Cox·L²)`. Default 0: no flicker noise.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default))]
    pub kf: f64,
    /// Flicker-noise current exponent AF. Default 1.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_af"))]
    pub af: f64,
}

impl MosfetParams {
    /// Default NMOS parameters (typical educational values).
    pub fn default_nmos() -> Self { … }

    /// Default PMOS parameters (typical educational values).
    pub fn default_pmos() -> Self { … }

    /// These parameters in the N-channel frame that [`mosfet_companion`]
    /// works in. Callers mirror a PMOS's voltages (`vsg`, `vsd`, …) before
    /// calling it; this mirrors the threshold to match, so a SPICE-signed
    /// VTO (−0.7 V for [`MosfetParams::default_pmos`]) becomes the +0.7 V
    /// the N-channel equations expect.
    pub fn in_nmos_frame(&self, kind: MosfetKind) -> MosfetParams { … }

    /// Level-1 parameters fitted to a datasheet's threshold and
    /// on-resistance: KP and VTO are solved so that the drain current at
    /// `Vgs = Vds = vth` is `vth_id`, and the drain–source resistance at
    /// `Vgs = rds_on_vgs` is `rds_on` (at `rds_on_id` when given, else at a
    /// vanishing drain current). LAMBDA, GAMMA and PHI keep the
    /// [`default_nmos`](Self::default_nmos) / [`default_pmos`](Self::default_pmos)
    /// values; VTO is signed for `kind`, as SPICE signs it.
    ///
    /// ```
    /// use sindr_devices::datasheet::MosfetDatasheet;
    /// use sindr_devices::mosfet::{MosfetKind, MosfetParams};
    ///
    /// // A small-signal NMOS: Vgs(th) 2.1 V at 250 µA, 1.2 Ω at 10 V.
    /// let ds = MosfetDatasheet::new(2.1, 250e-6, 1.2, 10.0);
    /// let p = MosfetParams::from_datasheet(MosfetKind::Nmos, &ds).unwrap();
    /// assert!(p.vto > 0.0 && p.vto < 2.1);
    /// ```
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`DatasheetError`] when a figure is missing or not positive, when
    /// `rds_on_vgs` isn't above the threshold, or when no Level-1 device
    /// meets both figures (an `rds_on_id` so high that the part leaves the
    /// triode region).
    pub fn from_datasheet(kind: MosfetKind, ds: &MosfetDatasheet) -> Result<Self, DatasheetError> { … }
}

/// Companion model output for MNA stamping.
pub struct MosfetCompanion {
    /// Drain current at the operating point (A), drain → source, in the
    /// NMOS frame: callers mirror a PMOS (negate) to get its physical current.
    pub id: f64,
    /// Transconductance ∂Id/∂Vgs (S).
    pub gm: f64,
    /// Output conductance ∂Id/∂Vds (S).
    pub gds: f64,
    /// Body transconductance ∂Id/∂Vbs (S), from the body effect. Zero when
    /// Vbs >= PHI, where the threshold stops depending on Vbs.
    pub gmb: f64,
    /// Operating region.
    pub region: MosfetRegion,
    /// Effective threshold voltage after the body effect (V), NMOS frame.
    pub vth: f64,
}

/// Compute threshold voltage with body effect.
///
/// Vth = VTO + GAMMA * (sqrt(PHI - Vbs) - sqrt(PHI))
///
/// For NMOS with Vbs <= 0: Vth increases (harder to turn on). Once the body
/// is forward-biased past PHI (Vbs >= PHI) the sqrt term is clamped to 0
/// and Vth no longer depends on Vbs.
/// For PMOS, caller passes sign-adjusted Vbs and
/// [`MosfetParams::in_nmos_frame`] parameters. With the body tied to the
/// source, as in sindr, Vbs = 0 and Vth = VTO.
pub fn threshold_voltage(vbs: f64, params: &MosfetParams) -> f64 { … }

/// Evaluate the Level 1 MOSFET model at a given operating point.
///
/// Works in the N-channel frame. For NMOS: Vgs, Vds, Vbs are used directly.
/// For PMOS: pass the mirrored voltages (Vsg, Vsd, Vsb; see
/// [`MosfetKind::nmos_frame`]) and [`MosfetParams::in_nmos_frame`]
/// parameters, so the equations work identically.
///
/// `gmb` is zero once the body is forward-biased past PHI, matching
/// [`threshold_voltage`].
pub fn mosfet_companion(vgs: f64, vds: f64, vbs: f64, params: &MosfetParams) -> MosfetCompanion { … }

/// The derivatives of a MOSFET's drain current, transconductance and output
/// conductance with respect to one parameter, at fixed terminal voltages, in
/// the N-channel frame of [`mosfet_companion`].
pub struct MosfetDerivative {
    /// ∂Id/∂p: drain current (A) per unit of the parameter.
    pub id: f64,
    /// ∂gm/∂p (S) per unit of the parameter.
    pub gm: f64,
    /// ∂gds/∂p (S) per unit of the parameter.
    pub gds: f64,
}

/// [`MosfetDerivative`]s with respect to `kp`, `vto` and `lambda`, from
/// [`mosfet_derivatives`].
pub struct MosfetDerivatives {
    /// With respect to `kp` (per A/V²).
    pub kp: MosfetDerivative,
    /// With respect to `vto` (per V) as `params` has it: in the N-channel
    /// frame, so a PMOS caller negates it for its SPICE-signed VTO.
    pub vto: MosfetDerivative,
    /// With respect to `lambda` (per 1/V).
    pub lambda: MosfetDerivative,
}

/// The exact derivatives of [`mosfet_companion`]'s `id`, `gm` and `gds` at
/// `vgs`, `vds`, `vbs` (V, N-channel frame) with respect to `kp`, `vto` and
/// `lambda`, for sensitivity analysis. All zero in cutoff.
pub fn mosfet_derivatives(
    vgs: f64,
    vds: f64,
    vbs: f64,
    params: &MosfetParams,
) -> MosfetDerivatives { … }

/// Detect MOSFET operating region from terminal voltages.
pub fn detect_region(vgs: f64, vds: f64, vth: f64) -> MosfetRegion { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/photodiode.rs`

Photodiode companion model.

Model: I = IS*(exp(Vd/(N*VT))-1) - I_photo, with VT = kT/q at the
junction `temperature`
I_photo = responsivity * irradiance (photocurrent, flows in reverse direction)

In dark (irradiance=0), behaves identically to a silicon diode.
With irradiance, produces reverse photocurrent that can drive loads.

```rust
/// Photodiode parameters.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct PhotodiodeParams {
    /// Dark saturation current (A).
    pub is: f64,
    /// Ideality factor (~1.0 for photodiodes).
    pub n: f64,
    /// Responsivity (A/W). Converts irradiance to photocurrent.
    /// Typical silicon photodiode: 0.4–0.7 A/W.
    pub responsivity: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`PhotodiodeParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given.
    pub temperature: f64,
}

impl PhotodiodeParams {
    /// Silicon photodiode: IS = 1e-12 A, N = 1.0, responsivity = 0.5 A/W.
    pub fn silicon() -> Self { … }

    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// Linearized companion model for a photodiode at operating point v_d.
///
/// Returns `(g_d, i_eq)`: conductance (S) and Norton current (A) for current
/// flowing anode → cathode, at `v_d` = anode − cathode (V). `irradiance` is
/// incident optical power in W (not W/m²). `i_eq` includes the
/// photocurrent, which flows cathode → anode, opposite to forward current.
pub fn photodiode_companion(v_d: f64, irradiance: f64, params: &PhotodiodeParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/photoresistor.rs`

Photoresistor (LDR) model: resistance as a function of illuminance.

Uses logarithmic interpolation between dark and bright endpoints,
matching real LDR behaviour (resistance halves roughly every decade of lux).

```rust
/// Photoresistor parameters.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct PhotoresistorParams {
    /// Resistance in darkness (Ω). Default: 1 MΩ.
    pub r_dark: f64,
    /// Resistance at full illumination (Ω). Default: 1 kΩ.
    pub r_bright: f64,
}

/// Compute LDR resistance from a normalised light level.
///
/// `light_level` is clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`:
/// - `0.0` → `params.r_dark`
/// - `1.0` → `params.r_bright`
///
/// Interpolation is logarithmic: `R = r_dark * (r_bright / r_dark) ^ light_level`
pub fn ldr_resistance(light_level: f64, params: &PhotoresistorParams) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/regulator.rs`

Linear voltage regulator: dropout, quiescent current, current limit,
line and load regulation.

The output is a piecewise-linear function of the input voltage and the
output current, both measured from the regulator's ground pin:

```text
regulating: Vout = V + line·(Vin − (V + Vdo)) − Rout·Iout
dropout:    Vout = Vin − Vdo − Rdo·Iout
```

whichever is lower. Past the current limit the output falls steeply, so
the current stays within 1 % of the limit into any load, short circuits
included. The input draws `Iout + Iq`.

A negative set voltage is a negative regulator (7905, 7912): the same
characteristic mirrored through the ground pin, so `Vin`, `Vout` and
`Iout` all change sign, and "lower" above reads "nearer zero".

```rust
/// Regulator parameters. [`Default`] is ideal: no dropout, no quiescent
/// current, no limit, perfect regulation, but never more out than in.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct RegulatorParams {
    /// Dropout voltage at no load (V): the least `Vin − Vout` it regulates
    /// with.
    pub dropout: f64,
    /// Rise in dropout per ampere of output current (Ω), for a dropout that
    /// grows with load.
    pub dropout_resistance: f64,
    /// Quiescent (ground-pin) current (A), drawn from the input on top of
    /// the output current.
    pub quiescent_current: f64,
    /// Output current limit (A). `None` is unlimited.
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"))]
    pub current_limit: Option<f64>,
    /// Line regulation: change in output per volt of input (V/V), around
    /// the input where it just leaves dropout.
    pub line_regulation: f64,
    /// Load regulation as an output resistance (Ω): the output falls this
    /// much per ampere drawn.
    pub output_resistance: f64,
}

impl RegulatorParams {
    /// An LM7805-class 5 V regulator, from typical 78xx datasheets at
    /// 25 °C: 2 V dropout (typical, 1 A), 4.3 mA quiescent
    /// (typical), 2.2 A peak current, line regulation 3 mV over 7–25 V
    /// (typical), load regulation 100 mV over 5 mA–1.5 A (maximum; no
    /// typical is given). Short-circuit foldback (0.23 A at 35 V in) is not
    /// modelled.
    pub fn lm7805() -> Self { … }

    /// An AMS1117-class low-dropout regulator, from its datasheet: 1.1 V
    /// dropout at 0.8 A (typical), 5 mA quiescent (typical), 1.1 A current
    /// limit (typical), line regulation 0.2 % and load regulation 0.4 %
    /// (maxima) of a 3.3 V output, over 4.75–12 V in and 0–0.8 A out.
    pub fn ams1117() -> Self { … }
}

/// Which part of its characteristic a regulator is on.
pub enum RegulatorRegion {
    /// Holding its set voltage (less line and load regulation).
    Regulating,
    /// Out of headroom: the output follows the input down.
    Dropout,
}

/// The regulator's output on one linear piece:
/// `Vout = offset + d_vin·Vin + d_iout·Iout`, all from the ground pin.
pub struct RegulatorLinear {
    /// Constant term (V).
    pub offset: f64,
    /// ∂Vout/∂Vin (V/V).
    pub d_vin: f64,
    /// ∂Vout/∂Iout (Ω), negative.
    pub d_iout: f64,
    /// Regulating or in dropout.
    pub region: RegulatorRegion,
    /// `true` when past the current limit.
    pub limiting: bool,
}

impl RegulatorLinear {
    /// The output voltage this piece gives at `vin`, `iout`.
    pub fn vout(&self, vin: f64, iout: f64) -> f64 { … }
}

/// The piece of a regulator set to `voltage` that applies at input `vin`
/// (V, from the ground pin) and output current `iout` (A, out of the output
/// pin).
pub fn regulator_piece(
    params: &RegulatorParams,
    voltage: f64,
    vin: f64,
    iout: f64,
) -> RegulatorLinear { … }

/// Where a regulator set to `voltage` changes piece, as signed distances
/// at input `vin` and output current `iout` (from the ground pin): leaving
/// regulation, reaching the 0 V floor, the current limit, and the two ends
/// of the quiescent-current ramp. [`regulator_piece`] and
/// [`regulator_quiescent`] switch only where one of these changes sign.
/// Each is linear in `vin` and `iout`, so a straight step between two
/// operating points crosses each at most once. An edge the parameters
/// don't have (no current limit) is `+∞`.
pub fn regulator_edges(params: &RegulatorParams, voltage: f64, vin: f64, iout: f64) -> [f64; 5] { … }

/// The quiescent current a regulator set to `voltage` draws from its input
/// at `vin` (V, from the ground pin), as `i0 + g·Vin` (A, into the input and
/// out at the ground pin). It is the full `quiescent_current` once the input
/// reaches the dropout voltage (0.1 V at least), ramps linearly to 0 below
/// that, and is 0 with no input. Mirrored for a negative `voltage`.
pub fn regulator_quiescent(params: &RegulatorParams, voltage: f64, vin: f64) -> (f64, f64) { … }

/// Power a regulator set to `voltage` dissipates (W): `(Vin − Vout)·Iout +
/// Vin·Iq`, with voltages from the ground pin and `Iq` the quiescent current
/// drawn at `vin` ([`regulator_quiescent`]). Both terms are positive for a
/// negative regulator too, where `Vin`, `Vout`, `Iout` and `Iq` are all
/// negative.
pub fn regulator_dissipation(
    params: &RegulatorParams,
    voltage: f64,
    vin: f64,
    vout: f64,
    iout: f64,
) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/schottky.rs`

Schottky diode companion model.

Schottky diodes use the same Shockley equation as silicon diodes
but with higher saturation current (IS ≈ 1e-8 A) and lower forward
voltage (~0.3V vs ~0.6V silicon). Reuses diode_companion().

```rust
/// Schottky diode parameters.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct SchottkyParams {
    /// Saturation current (A). Higher than silicon due to lower barrier.
    pub is: f64,
    /// Emission coefficient (dimensionless). ~1.0 for Schottky (more ideal
    /// than silicon).
    pub n: f64,
}

impl SchottkyParams {
    /// Standard BAT85 Schottky: IS = 1e-8 A, N = 1.0 → Vf ≈ 0.3V at 10 mA.
    pub fn standard() -> Self { … }
}

/// Linearized companion model for a Schottky diode at operating point v_d.
///
/// Returns `(g_d, i_eq)`: conductance (S) and equivalent Norton current (A)
/// for current flowing anode → cathode, at `v_d` = anode − cathode (V).
/// Delegates to diode_companion with Schottky parameters.
pub fn schottky_companion(v_d: f64, params: &SchottkyParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/thermistor.rs`

NTC thermistor resistance model (Beta model).

Thermistors have temperature-dependent resistance but are passive —
resistance is computed once from the temperature parameter, not from
circuit voltages. No NR iteration needed.

```rust
/// NTC thermistor parameters (Beta model).
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct ThermistorParams {
    /// Resistance at reference temperature T0 (Ω).
    pub r0: f64,
    /// Beta coefficient (K). Typically 3000–5000 for NTC.
    pub beta: f64,
    /// Reference temperature (K). Standard: 298.15 K (25°C).
    pub t0: f64,
}

impl ThermistorParams {
    /// Standard 10 kΩ NTC thermistor (Epcos B57164K0103K000 or equivalent).
    /// R0 = 10kΩ at 25°C, Beta = 3950 K.
    pub fn ntc_10k() -> Self { … }
}

/// Compute thermistor resistance at a given temperature (Kelvin).
///
/// Uses the Beta model: R(T) = R0 * exp(beta * (1/T - 1/T0))
///
/// Does not panic; clamps T to a minimum of 1 K to avoid division by zero.
pub fn thermistor_resistance(temperature_k: f64, params: &ThermistorParams) -> f64 { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/varactor.rs`

Varactor diode model: voltage-dependent junction capacitance.

A varactor is a reverse-biased diode whose junction capacitance varies with
applied voltage. In DC analysis it is an open circuit. In transient analysis
the capacitance is evaluated at the previous timestep voltage (freeze-and-stamp).
In AC analysis it is the capacitance at the DC bias point.

```rust
/// Varactor diode parameters.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct VaractorParams {
    /// Zero-bias junction capacitance (F). Typical: 10e-12 (10 pF).
    pub cj0: f64,
    /// Built-in junction potential (V). Typical: 0.7 for Si.
    pub phi: f64,
    /// Grading coefficient (dimensionless). Typical: 0.5 (abrupt junction).
    pub m: f64,
}

/// Junction capacitance (F) at `v` = anode − cathode (V); reverse bias is
/// negative.
///
/// C_j(V) = C_j0 / (1 - V/phi)^m
///
/// Clamped: V must not reach phi (singularity). Clamp V to 0.9 * phi max.
/// For reverse bias (V < 0), capacitance increases correctly.
/// For forward bias (V approaching phi), capacitance would diverge — clamp.
pub fn junction_capacitance(v: f64, params: &VaractorParams) -> f64 { … }

/// Compute the transient companion model for the varactor at `v_prev`
/// (V, anode − cathode) over a step of `dt` seconds.
///
/// Returns `(g_eq, i_eq)`, in S and A, where:
/// - g_eq = C_j(v_prev) / dt  (backward Euler capacitor conductance)
/// - i_eq = -g_eq * v_prev    (capacitor history current)
///
/// The current from anode to cathode is `g_eq * v + i_eq`, the same
/// convention as [`diode_companion`](crate::diode::diode_companion).
///
/// In DC analysis, stamp as open circuit: return (0.0, 0.0).
/// Caller passes dt = 0.0 to signal DC, returning open circuit.
pub fn varactor_companion(v_prev: f64, dt: f64, params: &VaractorParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr-devices/src/zener.rs`

Zener diode model: piecewise companion for Newton-Raphson simulation.

Forward bias: standard Shockley diode.
Reverse breakdown: linearised clamp at -Vz.

```rust
/// Zener diode parameters.
///
/// Set the fields you need and fill the rest with `..Default::default()`,
/// so a field added in a later release doesn't break the literal.
pub struct ZenerParams {
    /// Breakdown voltage (V), positive: 5.1 for a BZX55C5V1.
    pub vz: f64,
    /// Breakdown region dynamic resistance (Ω). Smaller = sharper knee.
    pub rz: f64,
    /// Saturation current for the forward diode region (A).
    pub is: f64,
    /// Junction temperature (K). Default 300.15 K = 27°C. Sets the thermal
    /// voltage [`ZenerParams::vt`]; `is` is used as given.
    pub temperature: f64,
}

impl ZenerParams {
    /// Construct default Zener parameters for the given breakdown voltage `vz` (V).
    pub fn new(vz: f64) -> Self { … }

    /// Thermal voltage kT/q (V) at the junction temperature.
    pub fn vt(&self) -> f64 { … }
}

/// Piecewise Zener companion model. Returns `(g_eq, i_eq)` for MNA stamping:
/// `g_eq` in S and `i_eq` in A, for current flowing anode → cathode, at
/// `v_d` = anode − cathode (V). Breakdown is `v_d ≤ −vz`.
///
/// - `v_d > -vz`: standard Shockley companion (clamped to avoid overflow).
/// - `v_d <= -vz`: linearised 1/rz clamp driving the junction to -Vz.
pub fn zener_companion(v_d: f64, params: &ZenerParams) -> (f64, f64) { … }
```

## `sindr/examples/bjt_amplifier.rs`

```rust
use sindr::{examples, solve_circuit};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::npn_common_emitter();
    let result = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;

    let bjt = result
        .bjt_results
        .first()
        .ok_or("expected at least one BJT in the result")?;

    println!("=== NPN Common Emitter Operating Point ===");
    println!("Vbe    = {:.4} V", bjt.vbe);
    println!("Vce    = {:.4} V", bjt.vce);
    println!("Ib     = {:.4} mA", bjt.ib * 1e3);
    println!("Ic     = {:.4} mA", bjt.ic * 1e3);
    println!("Ie     = {:.4} mA", bjt.ie * 1e3);
    println!("Region : {}", bjt.region);
    println!("Power  = {:.4} mW", bjt.power * 1e3);

    Ok(())
}

## `sindr/examples/bode_plot.rs`

```rust
use sindr::ac_analysis::{solve_ac, AcConfig};
use sindr::examples;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = examples::rc_lowpass_filter();

    let config = AcConfig::new("V1", 10.0, 100_000.0, 50);

    let result = solve_ac(&circuit, &config)?;

    println!("=== RC Low-Pass Filter — Bode Plot ===");
    println!("{:>10}\t{:>7}\t{:>7}", "freq(Hz)", "gain(dB)", "phase(deg)");

    for point in result.points.iter() {
        let gain = point.gain_db("n2", config.ac_magnitude).unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
        let phase = point.phase_deg("n2").unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
        println!("{:>10.2}\t{:>7.2}\t{:>7.2}", point.frequency, gain, phase);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/dc_sweep_diode.rs`

```rust
// DC sweep of a series-resistor + diode circuit (I-V curve)
//
// Topology: V1 (swept) → R_series (100 Ω) → D1 (diode) → GND
//
// Run: cargo run -p sindr --example dc_sweep_diode
//
// Expected output:
//   V_applied(V)    I_diode(A)
//   Reverse-bias (V < 0): near-zero current
//   Forward-bias (V > ~0.5): exponential current turn-on

use sindr::element::{Diode, Resistor, VoltageSource};
use sindr::DcSweepAxis;
use sindr::{dc_sweep, Circuit, CircuitElement};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = Circuit {
        ground_node: "0".into(),
        components: vec![
            CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
                id: "V1".into(),
                nodes: ["n1".into(), "0".into()],
                voltage: 0.0, // initial value irrelevant; dc_sweep overrides it
                waveform: None,
            }),
            // Series resistor required: diode directly across V-source is degenerate
            CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
                id: "R_series".into(),
                nodes: ["n1".into(), "n2".into()],
                resistance: 100.0,
            }),
            CircuitElement::Diode(Diode {
                id: "D1".into(),
                nodes: ["n2".into(), "0".into()], // anode: n2, cathode: GND
                temperature: 300.15,
                model: None,
            }),
        ],
        ..Default::default()
    };

    // Sweep V1 from -1 V to +1 V in 101 points
    let sweep = dc_sweep(&circuit, &DcSweepAxis::new("V1", -1.0, 1.0, 101))?;

    println!("V_applied(V)\tI_diode(A)");
    for (v, i) in sweep.component_current_curve("D1") {
        println!("{:>8.3}\t{:>12.6e}", v, i);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/fourier.rs`

```rust
//! Harmonics, THD and a windowed FFT of a clipped sine: a 2 V, 1 kHz sine
//! through 1 kΩ into antiparallel diodes.
//!
//! Run with `cargo run --example fourier`.

use sindr::fourier::{Fft, Fourier, Window};
use sindr::measure::Signal;
use sindr::solve_transient;
use sindr::spice::parse_str;

const DECK: &str = "\
clipper
V1 in 0 SIN(0 2 1k)
R1 in out 1k
D1 out 0 dmod
D2 0 out dmod
.model dmod D(IS=1e-14 N=1)
.tran 5u 5m 0 5u
.end
";

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let netlist = parse_str(DECK)?;
    let config = netlist.transient_config().ok_or("the deck has a .tran")?;
    let result = solve_transient(&netlist.circuit, &config)?;
    let out = Signal::v("out");

    // .four 1k v(out)
    let four = Fourier::new(1e3).on(&result, &out)?;
    println!("Fourier analysis of {out}: THD {:.4} %", four.thd_percent);
    println!("harmonic  frequency (Hz)  magnitude (V)  phase (°)");
    println!("{:>8}  {:>14}  {:>13.6}  {:>9}", 0, 0, four.dc, 0);
    for h in &four.harmonics {
        println!(
            "{:>8}  {:>14}  {:>13.6}  {:>9.4}",
            h.number, h.frequency, h.magnitude, h.phase
        );
    }

    // FFT of the last four periods, Hann-windowed: 250 Hz bins.
    let spectrum = Fft::new()
        .window(Window::Hann)
        .points(1024)
        .span(1e-3, 5e-3)
        .on(&result, &out)?;
    println!(
        "\nFFT, {:?} window, {} points, {} Hz bins:",
        spectrum.window, spectrum.points, spectrum.resolution
    );
    for bin in spectrum.bins.iter().filter(|b| b.magnitude > 1e-2) {
        println!("{:>8.0} Hz  {:.4} V", bin.frequency, bin.magnitude);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## `sindr/examples/import_netlist.rs`

```rust
//! Simulate a schematic tool's netlist with a test bench.
//!
//! A transistor switch: a 9 V battery comes in on connector J1, R1 feeds an
//! LED, and Q1 sinks it when a logic-level signal on test point TP1 drives
//! its base through R2. The netlist says nothing about voltages; the bench
//! adds the supply on J1's pins and the 3.3 V drive on TP1, then runs an
//! operating point. Results come back keyed by the netlist's own ids.
//!
//! Run: `cargo run -p sindr --example import_netlist`

use sindr::import::{
    simulate, Analysis, Bench, BenchSource, Component, ComponentKind, Net, Netlist, Pin, Simulation,
};

fn main() {
    let netlist = Netlist {
        components: vec![
            Component::new("J1", ComponentKind::Connector),
            Component::new("TP1", ComponentKind::TestPoint),
            Component::new("R1", ComponentKind::Resistor).with_value("680"),
            Component::new("D1", ComponentKind::Led).with_param("color", "green"),
            Component::new("Q1", ComponentKind::Npn).with_param("hfe", 200.0),
            Component::new("R2", ComponentKind::Resistor).with_value("4k7"),
        ],
        nets: vec![
            Net::new("net-1", [("J1", "1"), ("R1", "1")]).with_name("VBAT"),
            Net::new("net-2", [("R1", "2"), ("D1", "anode")]),
            Net::new("net-3", [("D1", "cathode"), ("Q1", "C")]),
            Net::new("net-4", [("TP1", "1"), ("R2", "1")]).with_name("DRIVE"),
            Net::new("net-5", [("R2", "2"), ("Q1", "B")]),
            Net::new("net-6", [("J1", "2"), ("Q1", "E")]).with_name("GND"),
        ],
    };

    let bench = Bench::new("GND")
        .with_source(BenchSource::voltage("battery", Pin::new("J1", "1"), 9.0))
        .with_source(BenchSource::voltage("drive", Pin::new("TP1", "1"), 3.3))
        .with_analysis(Analysis::OperatingPoint);

    let imported = match simulate(&netlist, &bench) {
        Ok(imported) => imported,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("can't simulate: {e}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };
    let Simulation::OperatingPoint(op) = imported.result else {
        unreachable!("the bench asked for an operating point")
    };

    for net in &netlist.nets {
        let node = imported.circuit.node(&net.id).unwrap_or(&net.id);
        let label = net.name.as_deref().unwrap_or(&net.id);
        println!("{label:>6}: {:7.3} V", op.voltage(node).unwrap_or(f64::NAN));
    }
    for id in ["R1", "D1", "R2"] {
        if let Some(c) = op.component(id) {
            println!(
                "{id:>6}: {:7.3} mA, {:6.2} mW",
                c.current_through * 1e3,
                c.power * 1e3
            );
        }
    }
}
```

## `sindr/examples/initial_voltages.rs`

```rust
// Seeding the Newton–Raphson starting point (SPICE `.nodeset`)
//
// Topology: V1 (5 V) → R1 (1 kΩ) → D1 → D2 → GND (two diodes in series)
//
// Run: cargo run -p sindr --example initial_voltages
//
// Expected output: both solves land on the same operating point
// (~1.38 V across the pair); the seed only changes where Newton starts.
// Seeds apply to nonlinear DC only, and node names that don't exist are
// ignored.

use sindr::element::{Diode, Resistor, VoltageSource};
use std::collections::HashMap;

use sindr::{solve_circuit, Circuit, CircuitElement, Solver, SolverOptions};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let circuit = Circuit {
        ground_node: "0".into(),
        components: vec![
            CircuitElement::VoltageSource(VoltageSource {
                id: "V1".into(),
                nodes: ["in".into(), "0".into()],
                voltage: 5.0,
                waveform: None,
            }),
            CircuitElement::Resistor(Resistor {
                id: "R1".into(),
                nodes: ["in".into(), "top".into()],
                resistance: 1_000.0,
            }),
            CircuitElement::Diode(Diode {
                id: "D1".into(),
                nodes: ["top".into(), "mid".into()],
                temperature: 300.15,
                model: None,
            }),
            CircuitElement::Diode(Diode {
                id: "D2".into(),
                nodes: ["mid".into(), "0".into()],
                temperature: 300.15,
                model: None,
            }),
        ],
        ..Default::default()
    };

    let plain = solve_circuit(&circuit)?;

    // Start Newton near the expected answer: ~0.65 V per diode.
    let seed = HashMap::from([("top".to_string(), 1.3), ("mid".to_string(), 0.65)]);
    let seeded =
        Solver::new(SolverOptions::default().with_nodeset(seed.clone())).circuit(&circuit)?;

    for node in ["top", "mid"] {
        println!(
            "V({node}): plain {:.6} V, seeded {:.6} V",
            plain.voltage(node).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
            seeded.voltage(node).unwrap_or(f64::NAN)
        );
    }

    Ok(())
}
```
